questions.name: #1 Honorary Degree
questions.en:
Victoria University of Wellington has conferred an honorary degree on a distinguished astrophysicist in a recent graduation ceremony.
Professor Warrick Couch ______ the honorary degree of Doctor of Science for his remarkable contribution to our knowledge of galaxies and dark energy.
Professor Couch is a distinguished astrophysicist who has ______ a crucial role in the discovery that the Universe is expanding at an accelerating rate, a finding which led to the lead scientists being awarded a Nobel Prize in Physics in 2011, which he attended in recognition of his contribution.
In his research, Professor Couch uses large ground-based and space-based telescopes to observe galaxy clusters, ______ are the largest Structures in the Universe.
He is also involved in a number of national and international committees overseeing the management of these telescopes.
  ______ ______ ______ his own research activities, Professor Couch has worked to support young researchers and provide public comment on astronomy internationally.
1. was receiving , received , had received , is received
2. led , played , done , found
3. who , they , those , which
4. As a result of , Instead of , In addition to , Regarding
questions.answer:
1. received
2. played
3. which
4. In
5. addition
6. to

questions.name: #2 Keith Haring
questions.en:
Keith Haring began as an underground artist, literally.
His first famous projects were pieces of stylized graffiti ______ in New York subway stations.
Haring travelled from station to station, drawing with chalk and chatting with commuters about his work.
These doodles helped him develop his classic style and he grew so ______ , doing up to 40 drawings a day, that it was not long before fame and a measure of fortune followed.
Soon, galleries and collectors from the art establishment wanted to buy full-sized pieces by Haring.
The paintings skyrocketed in price but this did not sit well with Haring's philosophy.
He believed that art, or ______ ______ his art, was for everyone.
Soon, Haring opened a store which he called the Pop Shop, which he hoped would attract a broad range of people.
While somewhat controversial among street artists, some of ______ accused Haring of 'selling out', the Pop Shop changed the way people thought about the relationship between art and business.
1. drawers , drew , draws , drawn
2. prolific , pedantic , perceptive , proactive
3. in part , at least , by contrast , actually
4. those , whom , them , whose
questions.full:
Keith Haring began as an underground artist, literally.
His first famous projects were pieces of stylized graffiti ______ in New York subway stations.
Haring travelled from station to station, drawing with chalk and chatting with commuters about his work.
These doodles helped him develop his classic style and he grew so ______ , doing up to 40 drawings a day, that it was not long before fame and a measure of fortune followed.

The paintings skyrocketed in price but this did not sit well with Haring's philosophy.

sense_groups.english: Keith Haring began as an underground artist, literally.
sense_groups.chinese: 基思·哈林最初是一位地下艺术家，名副其实。

sense_groups.english: His first famous projects were pieces of stylized graffiti drawn in New York subway stations.
sense_groups.chinese: 他最初著名的作品是在纽约地铁站画的风格化涂鸦。

sense_groups.english: Haring travelled from station to station, drawing with chalk and chatting with commuters about his work.
sense_groups.chinese: 哈林从一个车站到另一个车站，用粉笔画画，并与通勤者聊他的作品。

sense_groups.english: These doodles helped him develop his classic style and he grew so prolific, doing up to 40 drawings a day, that it was not long before fame and a measure of fortune followed.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些涂鸦帮助他形成了自己的经典风格，他变得非常多产，每天画多达40幅画，不久之后名声和一定财富随之而来。

sense_groups.english: Soon, galleries and collectors from the art establishment wanted to buy full-sized pieces by Haring.
sense_groups.chinese: 很快，艺术界的画廊和收藏家想要购买哈林的全尺寸作品。

sense_groups.english: The paintings skyrocketed in price but this did not sit well with Haring's philosophy.
sense_groups.chinese: 画作价格飙升，但这与哈林的理念不符。

sense_groups.english: He believed that art, or at least his art, was for everyone.
sense_groups.chinese: 他认为艺术，至少是他的艺术，是为所有人服务的。

sense_groups.english: Soon, Haring opened a store which he called the Pop Shop, which he hoped would attract a broad range of people.
sense_groups.chinese: 很快，哈林开了一家店，他称之为波普商店，希望它能吸引广泛的人群。

sense_groups.english: While somewhat controversial among street artists, some of whom accused Haring of 'selling out', the Pop Shop changed the way people thought about the relationship between art and business.
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然在街头艺术家中有些争议，其中一些人指责哈林‘出卖自己’，但波普商店改变了人们对艺术与商业关系的看法。

questions.name: #3 Intelligence Comparison
questions.en:
Comparing the intelligence of animals of different species is difficult, how do you compare a dolphin and a horse?
Psychologists have a technique for looking at intelligence that ______ not require the cooperation of the animal involved.
The relative size of an individual's brain is a reasonable indication of intelligence.
Comparing ______ species is not as simple as generally expected.
An elephant will have a larger brain than a human has simply because it is a large beast.
  ______ , we use the Cephalization index, which compares the size of an animal's brain with the size of its body.
Based on the Cephalization index, the brightest animals on the planet are humans, ______ by great apes, porpoises and elephants.
As a general ______ , animals that hunt for a living (like canines) are smarter than strict vegetarians (you don't need much intelligence to outsmart a leaf of lettuce).
Animals that live in social groups are always smarter and have larger EQ's than solitary animals.
1. can , do , did , does
2. across , to , through , with
3. Then , Instead , Because , Otherwise
4. followed , follows , follow , following
5. theory , principal , rule , principle
questions.full:

Psychologists have a technique for looking at intelligence that ______ not require the cooperation of the animal involved.

  ______ , we use the Cephalization index, which compares the size of an animal's brain with the size of its body.

As a general ______ , animals that hunt for a living (like canines) are smarter than strict vegetarians (you don't need much intelligence to outsmart a leaf of lettuce).
Animals that live in social groups are always smarter and have larger EQ's than solitary animals.

1. can , do , did , does
2. across , to , through , with
3. Then , Instead , Because , Otherwise
4. followed , follows , follow , following
5. theory , principal , rule , principle

答案:
1. does
2. across
3. Instead
4. followed
5. rule

sense_groups.english: Comparing the intelligence of animals of different species is difficult, how do you compare a dolphin and a horse?
sense_groups.chinese: 比较不同物种动物的智力很困难，你怎么比较海豚和马呢？

sense_groups.english: Psychologists have a technique for looking at intelligence that does not require the cooperation of the animal involved.
sense_groups.chinese: 心理学家有一种研究智力的方法，不需要所研究动物的配合。

sense_groups.english: The relative size of an individual's brain is a reasonable indication of intelligence.
sense_groups.chinese: 个体大脑的相对大小是智力的合理指标。

sense_groups.english: Comparing across species is not as simple as generally expected.
sense_groups.chinese: 跨物种比较并不像通常想象的那么简单。

sense_groups.english: An elephant will have a larger brain than a human has simply because it is a large beast.
sense_groups.chinese: 大象的大脑比人类大，仅仅因为它是一种大型动物。

sense_groups.english: Instead, we use the Cephalization index, which compares the size of an animal's brain with the size of its body.
sense_groups.chinese: 相反，我们使用脑化指数，它比较动物大脑大小与其身体大小。

sense_groups.english: Based on the Cephalization index, the brightest animals on the planet are humans, followed by great apes, porpoises and elephants.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据脑化指数，地球上最聪明的动物是人类，其次是类人猿、鼠海豚和大象。

sense_groups.english: As a general rule, animals that hunt for a living (like canines) are smarter than strict vegetarians (you don't need much intelligence to outsmart a leaf of lettuce).
sense_groups.chinese: 一般来说，以捕猎为生的动物（如犬科）比严格的素食动物更聪明（你不需要太多智慧来智取一片生菜叶）。

sense_groups.english: Animals that live in social groups are always smarter and have larger EQ's than solitary animals.
sense_groups.chinese: 群居动物总是比独居动物更聪明，情商也更高。

questions.name: #4 Longevity
questions.en:

It results in a much more ______ customer base for them to work from.
Why we are living longer is not the issue for anyone ______ in drawing up plans to market a product.
What they focus on is the fact that there are now more age groups to target, which means that a sales pitch can be re-worked a number of times to more exactly fit each one.
For example, ______ ______ referring simply to 'adults', there are now 'starting adults', 'young adults' and 'established adults'.
  ______ , markets no longer talk about 'children', but tend to refer to a fuller range of categories that includes 'kids', 'tweens', 'pre-teens' and 'teenagers'.
We now have a very diverse population in terms of age, and that can only be a ______ for business.
1. usual , precise , right , honest
2. mixed , concerned , involved , linked
3. while , by , even when , rather than
4. Even , While , Similarly , Really
5. favour , bonus , promise , desire
questions.answer:
1. precise
2. involved
3. rather
4. than
5. Similarly
6. bonus

sense_groups.english: People are living longer
sense_groups.chinese: 人们活得更长了

sense_groups.english: and this longevity is good news for sales teams.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种长寿对销售团队来说是个好消息。

sense_groups.english: It results in a much more precise customer base for them to work from.
sense_groups.chinese: 这导致他们面对的客户群体更加精确。

sense_groups.english: Why we are living longer is not the issue for anyone involved in drawing up plans to market a product.
sense_groups.chinese: 为什么我们活得更长，对于任何参与制定产品营销计划的人来说，都不是问题。

sense_groups.english: What they focus on is the fact that there are now more age groups to target,

sense_groups.english: which means that a sales pitch can be re-worked a number of times to more exactly fit each one.

sense_groups.english: Similarly, markets no longer talk about 'children',

sense_groups.english: but tend to refer to a fuller range of categories that includes 'kids', 'tweens', 'pre-teens' and 'teenagers'.
sense_groups.chinese: 而是倾向于提及更全面的类别，包括“小孩”、“青少年前期”、“青春期前”和“青少年”。

sense_groups.english: We now have a very diverse population in terms of age,
sense_groups.chinese: 我们现在在年龄方面拥有非常多样化的人口，

sense_groups.english: and that can only be a bonus for business.
sense_groups.chinese: 这对企业来说只能是一个额外的好处。

questions.name: #5 Push and Pull
questions.en:
People move to a new region for many different reasons.
The ______ for moving can come from a combination of what researchers sometimes call 'push and pull ______ ' — those that encourage people to leave a region, and those that attract people to a region.
Some of the factors that motivate people to move ______ seeking a better climate, finding more affordable housing, looking for work or retiring from work, leaving the ______ of city living, wanting a more pleasant environment, and wanting to be near to family and friends.
In reality, many complex factors and personal reasons may ______ to motivate a person or family to move.
1. accommodation , combination , abbreviation , motivation
2. factors , generators , ideas , settings
3. include , including , includes , included
4. congestion , configuration , concoction , conjunction
5.intercept , intercede , interact , intersperse
questions.full:
People move to a new region for many different reasons.
The ______ for moving can come from a combination of what researchers sometimes call 'push and pull ______ ' — those that encourage people to leave a region, and those that attract people to a region.
Some of the factors that motivate people to move ______ seeking a better climate, finding more affordable housing, looking for work or retiring from work, leaving the ______ of city living, wanting a more pleasant environment, and wanting to be near to family and friends.
In reality, many complex factors and personal reasons may ______ to motivate a person or family to move.

1. accommodation , combination , abbreviation , motivation
2. factors , generators , ideas , settings
3. include , including , includes , included
4. congestion , configuration , concoction , conjunction
5.intercept , intercede , interact , intersperse

答案:
1. motivation
2. factors
3. include
4. congestion
5. interact

sense_groups.english: People move to a new region for many different reasons.
sense_groups.chinese: 人们搬到新地区的原因有很多。

sense_groups.english: The motivation for moving can come from a combination of what researchers sometimes call 'push and pull factors' — those that encourage people to leave a region, and those that attract people to a region.
sense_groups.chinese: 搬家的动机可能来自研究人员有时称之为‘推拉因素’的组合——那些鼓励人们离开一个地区的因素，以及那些吸引人们来到一个地区的因素。

sense_groups.english: Some of the factors that motivate people to move include seeking a better climate, finding more affordable housing, looking for work or retiring from work, leaving the congestion of city living, wanting a more pleasant environment, and wanting to be near to family and friends.
sense_groups.chinese: 促使人们搬家的一些因素包括寻求更好的气候、寻找更实惠的住房、找工作或退休、离开城市生活的拥挤、想要更宜人的环境，以及想要靠近家人和朋友。

sense_groups.english: In reality, many complex factors and personal reasons may interact to motivate a person or family to move.
sense_groups.chinese: 实际上，许多复杂的因素和个人原因可能会相互作用，促使一个人或家庭搬家。

questions.name: #6 Language Extinct
questions.en:
At the moment, there are between six and seven thousand languages in the world.
According to linguists, fifty percent of these are in danger ______ ______ extinct.
The speed of language loss has accelerated over the past few decades because businesses that need to communicate with a range of people from other cultures ______ to employ more widely used languages, such as English, Chinese, or Spanish.
This attitude is understandable, but it means that many local languages are dying out before anyone ______ ______ the opportunity to study them.
According to linguists, some of these languages could reveal a great ______ of useful information about language learning and cognitive development.
In addition, a local language that has been built on the local culture contains words and phrases that express that culture; lose the language and you arguably may lose the culture, too.
And finally, historians will ______ that a language contains evidence of a region's history and should, for that reason alone, be preserved.
1. to become , became , of becoming , have become
2. select , prefer , fancy , must
3. would have , has had , have , having had
4. size , deal , load , capacity
5. speak , argue , explore , tell
questions.answer:
1. of
2. becoming
3. prefer
4. has
5. had
6. deal
7. argue

According to linguists, fifty percent of these are in danger ______ ______ extinct.

sense_groups.english: At the moment, there are between six and seven thousand languages in the world.
sense_groups.chinese: 目前，世界上有大约六千到七千种语言。

sense_groups.english: According to linguists, fifty percent of these are in danger of becoming extinct.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据语言学家的说法，其中百分之五十正面临灭绝的危险。

sense_groups.english: The speed of language loss has accelerated over the past few decades
sense_groups.chinese: 过去几十年里，语言消失的速度加快了，

sense_groups.english: because businesses that need to communicate with a range of people from other cultures prefer to employ more widely used languages, such as English, Chinese, or Spanish.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为需要与来自不同文化的人交流的企业更倾向于使用更广泛的语言，如英语、中文或西班牙语。

sense_groups.english: This attitude is understandable,
sense_groups.chinese: 这种态度可以理解，

sense_groups.english: but it means that many local languages are dying out before anyone has had the opportunity to study them.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这意味着许多地方语言在任何人有机会研究它们之前就消失了。

sense_groups.english: According to linguists, some of these languages could reveal a great deal of useful information about language learning and cognitive development.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据语言学家的说法，其中一些语言可能揭示大量关于语言学习和认知发展的有用信息。

sense_groups.english: In addition, a local language that has been built on the local culture contains words and phrases that express that culture;
sense_groups.chinese: 此外，基于当地文化形成的本地语言包含表达该文化的词汇和短语；

sense_groups.english: lose the language and you arguably may lose the culture, too.
sense_groups.chinese: 失去语言，你很可能也失去了文化。

sense_groups.english: And finally, historians will argue that a language contains evidence of a region's history
sense_groups.chinese: 最后，历史学家会认为语言包含一个地区历史的证据，

sense_groups.english: and should, for that reason alone, be preserved.
sense_groups.chinese: 仅凭这一点，就应该保护它。

questions.name: #7 Southern Cone
questions.en:

They have sought to construct democratic systems based on popular participation rather than elite and foreign ______ .

questions.name: #9 Cloth-making

Wool, cotton, flax, or hemp was first spun into a thin thread using a spindle.
The thread was then woven into a fabric.

Later machines called looms had rods that separated the threads to allow the weft to be inserted more ______ .
A piece of wood, called the shuttle, holding a spool of thread, was passed between the separated threads.
The basic principles of spinning and weaving have stayed the same until the present day, though during the industrial revolution of the 18th century many ways were found of automating the processes.
With new machines such as the spinning mule, many threads could be spun at the same time, and, with the help of devices like the flying shuttle, broad pieces of cloth could be woven at great speed.

3. role , principles , foundation , criteria
4. automating , slower , faster , existing

questions.name: #16 Good Information

But while this should be ______ for social reasons, is it beneficial in economic terms?

questions.name: #23 Sci-fi Movie
questions.en:
It's like the publishing version of one of those scenes from a sci-fi movie where an alien invasion impels traditional adversaries to join together to face their larger, common threat.
Today 56 newspapers, in Pakistan and India, in Israel and Lebanon, in China, in Greece and Turkey, in Africa and in North, South and Central America are publishing an unprecedented joint editorial calling for meaningful action to face the threat posed by climate change.
The editorial, ______ in 45 ______ in 20 different languages, appears on this first day of the Copenhagen climate conference.
The British paper the Guardian led the effort, which involved weeks of negotiations to reach a final version.
The editorial notes that "the science is complex but the facts are clear.
The world needs to take steps to limit temperature rises to 2 degrees C. A bigger rise of 3 to 4 degrees C would parch continents, turning farmland into desert.
Half of all species could become extinct, untold millions of people would be displaced, whole nations drowned by the sea.
The controversy over emails by British researchers that suggest they tried to suppress inconvenient data has muddied the waters but failed to dent the mass of evidence on which these predictions are based."
The editorial ______ that "the shift to a low-carbon society holds out the prospect of more opportunity than sacrifice.
Already some countries have recognized that embracing the transformation can bring growth, jobs and better quality lives.
The flow of capital tells its own story: last year for the first time more was invested in renewable forms of energy than producing ______ from fossil fuels."
So while gleeful anarchists like Oklahoma Senator James Inhofe go to Copenhagen to try to sabotage the proceedings, the worldwide array of newspapers attempts to remind the conference participants and the people they represent to keep their eye on the ball—the ball in this case being an oblate spheroid with almost seven billion human inhabitants and a fever that ______ needs to be treated.
As the Guardian's editor in chief, Alan Rusbridger, said, "Newspapers have never done anything like this before but they have never had to cover a story like this before."
1. published , publicized , burnished , transmitted
2. clans , countries , continents , terraces
3. modified , protested , recognized , declined
4. electricity , indivisibility , significance , negativity
5. solicitously , desperately , ephemerally , peripherally

questions.name: #25 Food Choices

The research is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The scientists noted the challenge in accessing data and creating metrics that can be compared across livestock and to potato, wheat and rice ______ .
They settled on national data from the U.S. Departments of Agriculture, the Interior and Energy.
The team calculated the production costs by assessing land area, water needs and fertilizer.
They also analyzed greenhouse gas ______ .
Producing pork, poultry, eggs and dairy were between two and six times less efficient than growing potatoes, wheat and rice.
And in the current ______ system, beef uses 28 times more land, 11 times more water and six times more fertilizer than the average of the other categories of livestock.

The researchers hope this data will help consumers make informed choices and policy makers create systems that can reduce the environmental costs of what we eat.

3. production , corruption , consumption , inventory
5. conjectures , manufacture , emissions , purification

sense_groups.chinese: 小丑鱼因电影《海底总动员》而闻名。

sense_groups.chinese: 在现实生活中，它们的社会等级很简单：大鱼支配小鱼。

sense_groups.chinese: 现在我们知道，为了加强这种社会结构，这些鱼通过攻击性和顺从性的声音信号进行交流。

sense_groups.chinese: 而更多的技术鼓励理论科学家在医学、生物学、力学、物理学和化学领域做出进一步的发现。

sense_groups.chinese: 并最终影响到家庭。

sense_groups.english: Some of these inventions simply made it easier to produce things on a large scale such as textile machines and foundries,

sense_groups.chinese: 它们快速且廉价地生产出大量的布料和金属制品。

sense_groups.chinese: 但一些发明带来了全新的可能性，比如第一批电池、汽船和火车头。

sense_groups.chinese: 其中一些发明需要几十年才能对世界产生重大影响。

sense_groups.english: Yet their creation, and the sheer amount of imagination and risk-taking involved, marked the beginning of a modern, global, technologically based economy of the kind that we live in today.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，它们的创造以及其中所蕴含的想象力和冒险精神，标志着我们今天所生活的这种现代、全球、以技术为基础的经济的开端。

sense_groups.english: Here are two seemingly unrelated facts.

sense_groups.english: One: from the late 1940s through 1963, we tested atomic bombs in the atmosphere.
sense_groups.chinese: 第一：从20世纪40年代末到1963年，我们在大气层中测试了原子弹。

sense_groups.english: Two: wine lovers are sometimes duped into spending exorbitant amounts for fake vintage bottles that weren't from the year they were supposedly grown.
sense_groups.chinese: 第二：葡萄酒爱好者有时会被骗花高价购买假年份酒，这些酒并非来自标签上标注的年份。

sense_groups.english: Carbon dating works by comparing the amount of carbon 14, which is a less common and less stable form of carbon, to the more abundant carbon 12.

sense_groups.english: For thousands of years, the ratio between the two has been the same.

sense_groups.english: The research team checked C-14 levels in 20 Australian red wines with vintages from 1958 to 1997.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究团队检查了20款澳大利亚红葡萄酒的碳14水平，这些酒的年份从1958年到1997年不等。

sense_groups.english: They compared the wine's C-14 to C-14 in atmospheric samples from the same years, and found a direct match—C-14 levels could give away the vintage year for each wine.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们将葡萄酒中的碳14与同一年份的大气样本中的碳14进行比较，发现直接匹配——碳14水平可以揭示每款酒的年份。

sense_groups.english: So beware of wine scammers.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以要小心葡萄酒骗子。

sense_groups.english: Because even at the atomic level, in vino veritas.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为即使在原子层面，酒中也有真相。

sense_groups.english: How did the zebra get its stripes?
sense_groups.chinese: 斑马是怎么得到条纹的？

sense_groups.english: One theory holds that stripes help confuse predators.
sense_groups.chinese: 一种理论认为条纹有助于迷惑捕食者。

sense_groups.english: But stripes might be primarily to protect zebras from ferocious…insects.
sense_groups.chinese: 但条纹可能主要是为了保护斑马免受凶猛的……昆虫的侵害。

sense_groups.english: That's according to a study in the Journal of Experimental Biology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是根据《实验生物学杂志》的一项研究得出的。

sense_groups.english: Horseflies are abundant in Africa.
sense_groups.chinese: 马蝇在非洲数量众多。

sense_groups.english: They deliver painful bites that spread disease and distract animals from grazing.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们叮咬疼痛，传播疾病，并使动物无法专心吃草。

sense_groups.english: The flies use polarized light hitting water as a guide to places to mate and lay eggs.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些苍蝇利用照射到水面上的偏振光作为寻找交配和产卵地点的指南。

sense_groups.english: And they read such light hitting dark mammal hides as a sign of a blood meal.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们把这种光照射到深色哺乳动物皮毛上解读为有血可吸的信号。

sense_groups.english: Zebra embryos start out dark and develop their white stripes before birth.
sense_groups.chinese: 斑马胚胎最初是深色的，在出生前发育出白色条纹。

sense_groups.english: Could the stripes confuse flies?
sense_groups.chinese: 条纹能迷惑苍蝇吗？

sense_groups.english: The researchers went to a farm infested with horseflies, where they set up models of black and white stripes of varying angles and widths, thus changing the direction of the reflected polarized light.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员去了一个马蝇肆虐的农场，在那里他们设置了不同角度和宽度的黑白条纹模型，从而改变了反射偏振光的方向。

sense_groups.english: They tracked how the patterns affected the flies' interest.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们追踪了这些图案如何影响苍蝇的兴趣。

sense_groups.english: They then tested models of horses colored black, brown, white or zebra-striped.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后他们测试了黑色、棕色、白色或斑马条纹的马模型。

sense_groups.english: And again tracked the effect on flies.
sense_groups.chinese: 并再次追踪了对苍蝇的影响。

sense_groups.english: Turns out that the black and white stripes on a zebra are optimal for avoiding a horsefly's attention.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果表明，斑马身上的黑白条纹最有利于避免马蝇的注意。

sense_groups.english: Meaning that zebras may have evolved stripes to ward off disease-carrying insects, and to dine in peace.
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着斑马可能进化出条纹是为了驱赶携带疾病的昆虫，并安静地进食。

questions.name: #42 Friday the 13th
questions.en:
It's Friday the 13th.
"You've gotta ask ______ a question: 'Do I feel lucky?'" If you don't, you could be ______ from triskaidekaphobia.
That's a fear of the number 13.
Napoleon, Herbert Hoover and FDR are well-documented triskaidekaphobics.
But why do folks think 13 is unlucky?
  ______ when it falls on a Friday, as it will three times this year?
The University of Delaware's Thomas Fernsler is known as Dr. 13.
He's an expert on the number's bad reputation, which may date back to biblical times.
After all, the 13th guest at the Last Supper was Judas.
And you know how that worked out for Jesus, who was crucified on a Friday.
Other factoids from Fernsler:
The first person to die in a car accident was killed in New York City on September the 13th in 1899, ______ that was a ______ .
And the ill-fated flight of Apollo 13 ______ at the 13th minute of the 13th hour Central Standard Time on April 11th, 1970.
And the numerals in the date 4/11/70 add up to 13!
As long as you don't include the 19 in 1970.
Hey, sometimes superstition can be hard work.
Today, some tall buildings lack a 13th floor.
Well, they have a 13th floor, but they call it the 14th floor.
Because the purveyors of bad luck are apparently easily fooled.
Meanwhile, over in France, panicky Parisian party-throwers can even hire a quatorziéme, a professional 14th guest.
Like Judas, Mark Twain was allegedly once poised to be the 13th guest at a dinner party.
A superstitious friend warned the very rational Twain not to go.
But Twain went.
"It was bad luck," he later remarked.
"They only had food for 12."

6. launched , reenforced , permafrost , debouched

questions.name: #43 Icebergs' Sound
questions.en:

But in the past ______ years, scientists have started to learn to distinguish the eerie, haunting sounds of iceberg life — ice cracking, icebergs grinding ______ each other, an iceberg grounding on the seafloor — and measure the extent to ______ those sounds contribute to the noise of the ocean.

sense_groups.english: Rodents are the workhorses of biomedical labs.
sense_groups.chinese: 啮齿动物是生物医学实验室的主力。

sense_groups.english: So it's important to know if they're stressed out, which could affect results.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以了解它们是否压力过大很重要，这可能会影响实验结果。

sense_groups.english: Now we know that lab rodents may be regularly exposed to a big stressor: men.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在我们知道，实验室啮齿动物可能经常暴露于一个巨大的压力源：男性。

sense_groups.chinese: 于是他们将小鼠和大鼠放入透明隔间，使其面部可见，并给它们注射刺激物。

sense_groups.english: The rodents expressed pain through grimacing when no humans were nearby.
sense_groups.chinese: 当附近没有人时，这些啮齿动物通过做鬼脸来表达疼痛。

sense_groups.english: But when confronted with a male researcher, or even just his odoriferous T-shirt, the animals grimaced less.
sense_groups.chinese: 但当面对男性研究员，甚至只是他带有气味的T恤时，这些动物做鬼脸的程度减轻了。

sense_groups.chinese: 女性观察者没有引起同样的啮齿动物反应。

sense_groups.english: Turns out that smelling a human male made rodents produce higher levels of a stress hormone and increase their body temperature.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果发现，闻到人类男性的气味会使啮齿动物产生更高水平的压力激素，并升高体温。

sense_groups.english: That stress response also blunted their sensitivity to pain.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种压力反应也削弱了它们对疼痛的敏感度。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal Nature Methods.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《自然方法》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Researchers may have to come up with ways to ward off the stress effects of male researchers.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员可能必须想出办法来抵御男性研究人员的压力影响。

sense_groups.english: Because to a rodent, men smell like hell.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为对于啮齿动物来说，男性闻起来糟透了。

questions.name: #46 Pharaoh's Mummy
questions.en:

Sixteen mummies still had identifiable hearts or arteries.
And nine of them showed hardening of those arteries.

Too many of those things will lead you to an early tomb.

questions.name: #47 Mount Everest
questions.en:
Called Chomolungma ("goddess mother of the world") in Tibet and Sagarmatha ("goddess of the sky") in Nepal, Mount Everest once went by the pedestrian name of Peak XV among Westerners.
That was before ______ established that it was the highest mountain on Earth, a fact that came as something of a surprise—Peak XV had seemed lost in the crowd of other formidable Himalayan peaks, many of which gave the ______ of greater height.
In 1852, the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India measured Everest's elevation as 29,002 feet above sea level.
This figure remained the officially ______ height for more than one hundred years.
In 1955, it was adjusted by a mere 26 feet to 29,028 (8,848 m).
The mountain received its official name in 1865 in honor of Sir George Everest, the British Surveyor General from 1830—1843 who had mapped the Indian subcontinent.
He had some ______ about having his name bestowed on the peak, arguing that the mountain should retain its local appellation, the standard policy of geographical societies.
Before the Survey of India, a number of other mountains ranked supreme in the eyes of the world.
In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the Andean peak Chimborazo was considered the highest.
At a relatively unremarkable 20,561 feet (6,310 m), it is in fact nowhere near the highest, ______ by about thirty other Andean peaks and several dozen in the Himalayas.
In 1809, the Himalayan peak Dhaulagiri (26,810 feet; 8,172 m) was declared the ultimate, only to be shunted aside in 1840 by Kanchenjunga (28,208 feet; 8,598 m), which today ranks third.
Everest's status has been unrivaled for the last century-and-a-half, but not without a few threats.

3. accepted , incepted , expected , intercepted

questions.name: #55 Below-ground Organisms
questions.en:
"If you want to find unique ______ and if you want to find a wide range of ______ below-ground organisms, you don't have to travel around the world.
You can walk across Central Park."
That statement comes from Noah Fierer, an ecology and evolutionary biology professor at the University of Colorado, Boulder.
He's also a ______ of a study that uncovered the surprisingly large diversity of subterranean microbial life at the 843-acre green rectangle in the heart of Manhattan.
The research is in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
Investigators looked at 596 ______ soil samples from the park and found thousands of different types of ______ .
They also compared those microbes with those living in 52 other soil samples taken from all around the planet.
The park had organisms that also exist in deserts, frozen tundra, forests, ______ and prairies.
Antarctica was the only area that had microbes that did not overlap with those found in Central Park.
And only a small percentage of the park's microbes were found to be already listed in databases.
The variety of microbes probably reflects a diversity of soil conditions within the park.
Seems that New York is a melting pot for people above the surface.
And for microbes beneath it.

2. different , coincident , impressionist , inconsiderate
3. holler , propaganda , pastor , coauthor
4. Manhattan , Canton , Revulsion , Sultan
5. separate , subjugate , waved , wage
6. pageants , maestros , microbes , sidestrokes
7. biogas , rainforests , oncocytomas , histiocytomas

questions.name: #56 Agrarian Parties
questions.en:
Agrarian parties are political parties chiefly representing the interests of peasants or, more broadly, the rural sector of society.
The extent to which they are important, or ______ they even exist, depends mainly on two factors.
One, obviously, is the size of an identifiable peasantry, or the size of the rural relative ______ the urban population.
The other is a matter of social integration: ______ agrarian parties to be important, the representation of countryside or peasantry must not be integrated with the other major sections of society.
  ______ , a country might possess a sizable rural population, but have an economic system in which the interests of the voters were predominantly related to their incomes, ______ than their occupations or location; and in such a country the political system would be unlikely to include an important agrarian party.
1. where , why , how , what , whether
2. from , to , of , on , with
3. as , in , for , to , by
4. Meanwhile , Moreover , Thus , However , Nevertheless
5. higher , lower , rather , other , fewer
questions.full:
Agrarian parties are political parties chiefly representing the interests of peasants or, more broadly, the rural sector of society.
The extent to which they are important, or ______ they even exist, depends mainly on two factors.
One, obviously, is the size of an identifiable peasantry, or the size of the rural relative ______ the urban population.
The other is a matter of social integration: ______ agrarian parties to be important, the representation of countryside or peasantry must not be integrated with the other major sections of society.
  ______ , a country might possess a sizable rural population, but have an economic system in which the interests of the voters were predominantly related to their incomes, ______ than their occupations or location; and in such a country the political system would be unlikely to include an important agrarian party.

1. where , why , how , what , whether
2. from , to , of , on , with
3. as , in , for , to , by
4. Meanwhile , Moreover , Thus , However , Nevertheless
5. higher , lower , rather , other , fewer

答案:

2. to
3. for
4. Thus

sense_groups.chinese: 农业政党是主要代表农民利益，或更广泛地说，代表社会农村部门利益的政党。

sense_groups.english: The extent to which they are important, or whether they even exist, depends mainly on two factors.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们的重要程度，甚至是否存在，主要取决于两个因素。

sense_groups.english: One, obviously, is the size of an identifiable peasantry, or the size of the rural relative to the urban population.
sense_groups.chinese: 其一，显然是可识别的农民群体的规模，或者农村人口相对于城市人口的规模。

sense_groups.chinese: 另一个是社会整合问题：要使农业政党重要，农村或农民的代表性不能与社会其他主要部分整合在一起。

sense_groups.chinese: 在这样的国家，政治体系不太可能包括一个重要的农业政党。

questions.name: #57 Retirement
questions.en:
For a start, we need to change our ( 1 ) of 'retirement', and we need to change mind-sets arising from earlier government policy which, in the face of high unemployment levels, encouraged mature workers to take early retirement. Today, government encourages them to ( 2 ) their retirement.

We also need to recognise the broader change that is occurring in how people work, learn, and live. Increasingly we are moving away from a linear relationship between education, training, work, and retirement, as people move in and out of jobs, careers, caregiving, study, and leisure. Employers of choice remove the ( 4 ) between the different segments of people's lives, by creating flexible conditions of work and a range of leave entitlements. questions.name: #58 National Responsibility
questions.en:
The principal and most consistently ______ recommendation of the world conferences was that countries must take full responsibility for their own development.

The automatic ______ of that principle is that each country must be free to determine its own development strategy.
It is essential that all donors and lenders accept the principle of country ownership of national development strategies.
This implies the acceptance of the principle that development strategies should not only be ______ to country circumstances, but also be prepared and implemented under the leadership of the governments of the countries themselves.
The 2005 World Summit also acknowledged, in this regard, that all countries must recognize the need for developing countries to ______ a balance between their national policy priorities and their international commitments.

2. diplomacy , sovereignty , bureaucracy , authority
3. overlapped , overemphasized , overwhelmed , overcharged
4. collage , correlation , corollary , assortment
5. atoned , attuned , affixed , attached
6. exchange , stage , strike , bridge

3. overemphasized
4. corollary

questions.name: #59 Lucy
questions.en:
Lucy was a single hominid skeleton found in Ethiopia.
First, she was a bunch of broken fragments lying in Ethiopia.
She was found by Donald Johanson and Tom Gray, who headed out to the area looking for rocks, and then drove back.

The discovery was so important because it entirely ______ our understanding of the process of evolution.
She showed that people had been wrong to think that we became intelligent before we stood up-- Lucy and her contemporaries were better suited for walking ______ than we were, but appeared to have been much less ______ advanced.

2. represent , reproduce , present , count
3. upset , discharged , assimilated , undermined
4. outright , upright , upper , vertical
5. intentionally , instantaneously , intellectually , technologically

sense_groups.chinese: 最常被观测的天体是月球、木星（其大卫星用好的双筒望远镜可见）和土星。

sense_groups.english: I once trained a cheap telescope on Saturn and some friends were so amazed at the site of the rings they seriously looked at the other end of the scope to see if I had doctored it.
sense_groups.chinese: 我曾经用一台便宜的望远镜对准土星，一些朋友看到土星环的景象非常惊讶，他们认真地看向望远镜的另一端，看我是否做了手脚。

sense_groups.english: Sidewalk Astronomy Night is indeed an international event, with dozens of public viewing sites from Beijing to the corner of 81st Street and Central Park West in Manhattan.
sense_groups.chinese: sidewalk 天文之夜确实是一个国际性活动，从北京到曼哈顿第81街和中央公园西的拐角处，有几十个公共观测点。

sense_groups.english: For more info and to find a site near you, just go to the official website.
sense_groups.chinese: 更多信息以及查找你附近的观测点，只需访问官方网站。

sense_groups.english: And if there's no organized site near you, feel free to go outside and look at the stars anyway.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你附近没有组织好的观测点，尽管出去看星星吧。

questions.name: #66 UNEP
questions.en:
Equitable and sustainable management of water resources is a major global challenge.
About one third of the world’s population lives in countries with moderate to high water stress, with ______ high impacts on the poor.
With respect to the ______ projected human population growth, industrial development and the expansion of irrigated agriculture in the next two years, water demand is expected to rise to levels that will make the task of providing water for human ______ more difficult.
Since its establishment, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has worked to promote sustainable water resources management practices through ______ approaches at the national, regional and global levels.
After more than 30 years, water resources management continues to be a strong pillar of UNEP’s work.
UNEP is actively participating in addressing water issues together with partner UN ______ , other organizations and donors; they facilitate and catalyze water resource assessments in various developing countries; implement projects that assist countries in developing integrated water resource management plans; create awareness of innovative alternative technologies and assist the development, implementation and enforcement of water resource management policies, laws and regulations.
1. proportionately , disproportionately , largely , scarcely
2. reactionary , current , few , past
3. substitute , sustenance , substance , sustainable
4. operation , cooperating , collaborative , collaborating
5. sectors , agencies , factors , segments
questions.full:
Equitable and sustainable management of water resources is a major global challenge.
About one third of the world’s population lives in countries with moderate to high water stress, with ______ high impacts on the poor.
With respect to the ______ projected human population growth, industrial development and the expansion of irrigated agriculture in the next two years, water demand is expected to rise to levels that will make the task of providing water for human ______ more difficult.
Since its establishment, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has worked to promote sustainable water resources management practices through ______ approaches at the national, regional and global levels.
After more than 30 years, water resources management continues to be a strong pillar of UNEP’s work.
UNEP is actively participating in addressing water issues together with partner UN ______ , other organizations and donors; they facilitate and catalyze water resource assessments in various developing countries; implement projects that assist countries in developing integrated water resource management plans; create awareness of innovative alternative technologies and assist the development, implementation and enforcement of water resource management policies, laws and regulations.

1. proportionately , disproportionately , largely , scarcely
2. reactionary , current , few , past
3. substitute , sustenance , substance , sustainable
4. operation , cooperating , collaborative , collaborating
5. sectors , agencies , factors , segments

答案:
1. disproportionately
2. current
3. sustenance
4. collaborative
5. agencies

sense_groups.english: Equitable and sustainable management of water resources is a major global challenge.
sense_groups.chinese: 公平且可持续的水资源管理是一个重大的全球挑战。

sense_groups.english: About one third of the world’s population lives in countries with moderate to high water stress,
sense_groups.chinese: 大约三分之一的世界人口生活在面临中度至高度水资源压力的国家，

sense_groups.english: with disproportionately high impacts on the poor.
sense_groups.chinese: 对贫困人口的影响尤为严重。

sense_groups.english: With respect to the current projected human population growth, industrial development and the expansion of irrigated agriculture in the next two years,
sense_groups.chinese: 考虑到当前预计的未来两年内人口增长、工业发展和灌溉农业的扩张，

sense_groups.english: water demand is expected to rise to levels that will make the task of providing water for human sustenance more difficult.
sense_groups.chinese: 水资源需求预计将上升到使人类生存用水供给任务更加困难的水平。

sense_groups.english: Since its establishment, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has worked to promote sustainable water resources management practices
sense_groups.chinese: 自成立以来，联合国环境规划署一直致力于推广可持续的水资源管理实践，

sense_groups.english: through collaborative approaches at the national, regional and global levels.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过在国家、区域和全球层面的合作方式。

sense_groups.english: After more than 30 years, water resources management continues to be a strong pillar of UNEP’s work.
sense_groups.chinese: 经过30多年，水资源管理仍然是联合国环境规划署工作的强大支柱。

sense_groups.english: UNEP is actively participating in addressing water issues together with partner UN agencies, other organizations and donors;
sense_groups.chinese: 联合国环境规划署正与联合国伙伴机构、其他组织和捐助方积极合作解决水问题；

sense_groups.english: they facilitate and catalyze water resource assessments in various developing countries;
sense_groups.chinese: 他们促进并推动各发展中国家的水资源评估；

sense_groups.english: implement projects that assist countries in developing integrated water resource management plans;
sense_groups.chinese: 实施项目协助各国制定综合水资源管理计划；

sense_groups.english: create awareness of innovative alternative technologies
sense_groups.chinese: 提高对创新替代技术的认识，

sense_groups.english: and assist the development, implementation and enforcement of water resource management policies, laws and regulations.
sense_groups.chinese: 并协助水资源管理政策、法律和法规的制定、实施和执行。

questions.name: #67 Neanderthals' Diet
questions.en:
When it comes to Neanderthal diets, the ______ has been: they ate meat.
Lots of meat.
But now it looks like Neanderthals chomped on a fair amount of veggies, too.
Researchers have had a tough time discerning the Neanderthals' diet.
They evaluated carbon and nitrogen isotopes in bones, but those only ______ to some general kinds of proteins.
Even plant remains in Neanderthal teeth could have gotten there because a tasty animal carcass itself contained traces of a last ______ meal.
So the researchers relied on ______ evidence—they studied Neanderthal fecal remains from a site in southern Spain called El Salt.
Neanderthals made it their home about 50,000 years ago.
The researchers analyzed the samples for chemical compounds that can only result from metabolizing cholesterol from meat or from metabolizing plants.
All five samples showed evidence of meat ______ .
But two revealed the digestion of plants.
Meaning that Neanderthals did try vegetation, likely tubers and nuts.
The study is in the journal PLoS ONE.
Ainara Sistiaga et al,
The scientists intend to use the same technique to examine soil samples at a 1.8 million-year-old site in Tanzania.
In the hopes that any remaining poop may deliver an ______ scoop.
1. Guttural , Grammatical , Neanderthal , Pronominal
2. resemblance , eyewitness , consensus , thickness
3. surged , plunge , correspond , overturned
4. requiem , vegetarian , communitarian , ferrymen
5. foolproof , schoolrooms , newsrooms , tubules
6. consumption , exaction , upperclassman , disjunction
7. ancestral-diet , cycled , diat , confided
questions.answer:
1. consensus
2. correspond
3. vegetarian
4. foolproof
5. consumption
6. ancestral-diet

sense_groups.english: When it comes to Neanderthal diets, the consensus has been: they ate meat.
sense_groups.chinese: 谈到尼安德特人的饮食，共识一直是：他们吃肉。

sense_groups.english: Lots of meat.
sense_groups.chinese: 大量的肉。

sense_groups.english: But now it looks like Neanderthals chomped on a fair amount of veggies, too.
sense_groups.chinese: 但现在看来，尼安德特人也吃了不少蔬菜。

sense_groups.english: Researchers have had a tough time discerning the Neanderthals' diet.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员一直难以辨别尼安德特人的饮食。

sense_groups.english: They evaluated carbon and nitrogen isotopes in bones, but those only correspond to some general kinds of proteins.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们评估了骨骼中的碳和氮同位素，但这些只对应某些一般类型的蛋白质。

sense_groups.english: Even plant remains in Neanderthal teeth could have gotten there because a tasty animal carcass itself contained traces of a last vegetarian meal.
sense_groups.chinese: 即使尼安德特人牙齿中的植物残留，也可能是因为美味的动物尸体本身含有最后一餐素食的痕迹。

sense_groups.english: So the researchers relied on foolproof evidence—they studied Neanderthal fecal remains from a site in southern Spain called El Salt.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，研究人员依靠了确凿的证据——他们研究了来自西班牙南部一个名为埃尔萨尔特的地点发现的尼安德特人粪便残留。

sense_groups.english: Neanderthals made it their home about 50,000 years ago.
sense_groups.chinese: 尼安德特人大约在5万年前将其作为家园。

sense_groups.english: The researchers analyzed the samples for chemical compounds that can only result from metabolizing cholesterol from meat or from metabolizing plants.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员分析了样本中的化合物，这些化合物只能来自代谢肉类中的胆固醇或代谢植物。

sense_groups.english: All five samples showed evidence of meat consumption.
sense_groups.chinese: 所有五个样本都显示出肉类消费的证据。

sense_groups.english: But two revealed the digestion of plants.
sense_groups.chinese: 但有两个样本揭示了植物的消化。

sense_groups.english: Meaning that Neanderthals did try vegetation, likely tubers and nuts.
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着尼安德特人确实尝试了植物，很可能是块茎和坚果。

sense_groups.english: The study is in the journal PLoS ONE.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《公共科学图书馆·综合》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: Ainara Sistiaga et al,
sense_groups.chinese: 作者是Ainara Sistiaga等人。

sense_groups.english: The scientists intend to use the same technique to examine soil samples at a 1.8 million-year-old site in Tanzania.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们打算使用同样的技术检查坦桑尼亚一个180万年前遗址的土壤样本。

sense_groups.english: In the hopes that any remaining poop may deliver an ancestral-diet scoop.
sense_groups.chinese: 希望任何残留的粪便能提供关于祖先饮食的独家新闻。

questions.name: #68 MBA Programs
questions.en:
Deciding to go to business school is perhaps the simplest part of what can be a complicated process.
With nearly 600 accredited MBA programs on ______ around the world, the choice of where to study can be overwhelming.
Here we explain how to ______ the right school and course for you and unravel the application and funding process.

sense_groups.english: Deciding to go to business school is perhaps the simplest part of what can be a complicated process.
sense_groups.chinese: 决定去商学院可能是复杂过程中最简单的一部分。

sense_groups.english: With nearly 600 accredited MBA programs on offer around the world, the choice of where to study can be overwhelming.

questions.name: #69 Amount of Sleep
questions.en:
The amount of sleep you need depends on many ______ , especially your age.
Newborns sleep between 16 and 18 hours a day and preschool children should sleep between 10 and 12 hours.
Older children and teens need at least nine hours to be well rested.
For most adults, seven to eight hours a night appears to the best amount of sleep.
However, for some people" enough sleep" may be as few as five hours or as many as 10 hours of sleep.
As you get older, your sleeping ______ change.
Older adults tend to sleep more lightly and awaken more frequently in the night than younger adults.
This can have many causes including medical conditions and medications used to treat them.
But there's no evidence that older adults need less sleep than younger adults.
Getting enough sleep is ______ to your health because it boosts your ______ system, which makes your body better able to fight disease.
Sleep is necessary for your nervous system to work properly.
Too little sleep makes you drowsy and unable to concentrate.
It also impairs memory and physical performance.
So how many hours of sleep are enough for You?
Experts say that if you feel drowsy during the day - even during boring activities - you are not getting enough sleep.
Also, quality of sleep is just as important as quantity.
People whose sleep is frequently interrupted or cut short are not getting quality sleep.
If you experience frequent daytime sleepiness, even after increasing the amount of quality sleep you get, talk to your doctor.
He or she may be able to ______ the cause of sleep problems and offer advice on how to get a better night's sleep.
1. reasons , possibilities , fractions , factors
2. durations , structures , distributions , patterns
3. benevolent , important , additional , luxurious
4. ecological , immune , medical , psychological
5. discharge , identify , dismiss , tout

2. patterns

4. immune

sense_groups.english: The amount of sleep you need depends on many factors, especially your age.
sense_groups.chinese: 你需要的睡眠量取决于许多因素，尤其是你的年龄。

sense_groups.english: Newborns sleep between 16 and 18 hours a day and preschool children should sleep between 10 and 12 hours.
sense_groups.chinese: 新生儿每天睡16到18小时，学龄前儿童应该睡10到12小时。

sense_groups.english: Older children and teens need at least nine hours to be well rested.
sense_groups.chinese: 年龄较大的儿童和青少年至少需要九小时才能休息充分。

sense_groups.english: For most adults, seven to eight hours a night appears to the best amount of sleep.
sense_groups.chinese: 对大多数成年人来说，每晚七到八小时似乎是最佳睡眠量。

sense_groups.english: However, for some people "enough sleep" may be as few as five hours or as many as 10 hours of sleep.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，对一些人来说，“足够的睡眠”可能少至五小时或多至十小时。

sense_groups.english: As you get older, your sleeping patterns change.
sense_groups.chinese: 随着年龄增长，你的睡眠模式会改变。

sense_groups.english: Older adults tend to sleep more lightly and awaken more frequently in the night than younger adults.
sense_groups.chinese: 老年人往往比年轻人睡得更浅，夜间醒来的次数更多。

sense_groups.english: This can have many causes including medical conditions and medications used to treat them.
sense_groups.chinese: 这可能有多种原因，包括医疗状况和用于治疗它们的药物。

sense_groups.english: But there's no evidence that older adults need less sleep than younger adults.
sense_groups.chinese: 但没有证据表明老年人比年轻人需要更少的睡眠。

sense_groups.english: Getting enough sleep is important to your health because it boosts your immune system, which makes your body better able to fight disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 获得足够的睡眠对你的健康很重要，因为它能增强你的免疫系统，使你的身体更好地抵抗疾病。

sense_groups.english: Sleep is necessary for your nervous system to work properly.
sense_groups.chinese: 睡眠对你的神经系统正常工作至关重要。

sense_groups.english: Too little sleep makes you drowsy and unable to concentrate.
sense_groups.chinese: 睡眠太少会让你昏昏欲睡，无法集中注意力。

sense_groups.english: It also impairs memory and physical performance.
sense_groups.chinese: 它还会损害记忆力和身体表现。

sense_groups.english: So how many hours of sleep are enough for You?
sense_groups.chinese: 那么，多少小时的睡眠对你来说才够呢？

sense_groups.english: Experts say that if you feel drowsy during the day - even during boring activities - you are not getting enough sleep.
sense_groups.chinese: 专家说，如果你白天感到困倦——即使在无聊的活动中——说明你睡眠不足。

sense_groups.english: Also, quality of sleep is just as important as quantity.
sense_groups.chinese: 此外，睡眠质量与数量同样重要。

sense_groups.english: People whose sleep is frequently interrupted or cut short are not getting quality sleep.
sense_groups.chinese: 睡眠经常被打断或缩短的人无法获得高质量的睡眠。

sense_groups.english: If you experience frequent daytime sleepiness, even after increasing the amount of quality sleep you get, talk to your doctor.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你经常白天嗜睡，即使增加了优质睡眠的量，也要咨询医生。

sense_groups.english: He or she may be able to identify the cause of sleep problems and offer advice on how to get a better night's sleep.
sense_groups.chinese: 他或她可能能够找出睡眠问题的原因，并就如何获得更好的夜间睡眠提供建议。

questions.en:

sense_groups.english: The electrons that are farther away from the pull of nucleus can be forced out of their orbits.
sense_groups.chinese: 离原子核引力较远的电子可以被强制脱离轨道。

sense_groups.english: These are called free electrons.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些被称为自由电子。

sense_groups.english: Free electrons can move from one atom to another.
sense_groups.chinese: 自由电子可以从一个原子移动到另一个原子。

sense_groups.english: This movement is known as electron flow.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种运动被称为电子流。

sense_groups.english: Electricity is the movement or flow of electrons from one atom to another.
sense_groups.chinese: 电是电子从一个原子到另一个原子的运动或流动。

sense_groups.english: A condition of imbalance is necessary to have a movement of electrons.

sense_groups.english: In a normal atom, the positively charged nucleus balances the negatively charged electrons.
sense_groups.chinese: 在正常原子中，带正电的原子核平衡了带负电的电子。

sense_groups.english: This holds them in orbit.
sense_groups.chinese: 这使它们保持在轨道上。

sense_groups.chinese: 它吸引更多电子以恢复平衡。

sense_groups.english: A good conductor must be made of atoms that give off free electrons easily.

sense_groups.english: They allow good electron flow.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们允许良好的电子流动。

questions.name: #80 Very Old Paris
questions.en:

But the great boulevards we admire today are relatively new, and were constructed to prevent any more barricades ______ ______ by the rebellious population; that work was carried out in the middle 19th century.
The earlier Paris had been ______ ______ a maze of narrow streets and alleyways.
But you can imagine that the work was not only highly expensive, but caused great distress among the half a million or so residents whose houses were ______ razed, and whose neighbourhoods disappeared.
What is done cannot usually be undone, especially when buildings are torn ______ .

2. as if , in part , just as , relative
3. evenly , rarely , simply , equally
4. up , across , between , down

2. created
3. in
4. part
5. simply
6. down

questions.name: #81 Moving
questions.en:
For every action, there's a ______ .
And for many movements we make, there's an ______ : we think about moving, and we move.
Now a study published in the May 8th issue of the journal Science suggests that the experience of moving is all in your mind.
Because the part of the brain that's active when you intend to move is the same part that lets you feel like you did.

The scientists found that zapping one ______ part of the brain made their patients feel like they wanted to move their arms, lips or tongue.

sense_groups.english: For every action, there's a reaction .
sense_groups.chinese: 每个动作都有一个反应。

sense_groups.english: And for many movements we make, there's an intention : we think about moving, and we move.
sense_groups.chinese: 对于我们做出的许多动作，都有一个意图：我们想着要移动，然后就移动了。

sense_groups.english: Now a study published in the May 8th issue of the journal Science suggests that the experience of moving is all in your mind.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，一项发表在《科学》杂志5月8日刊上的研究表明，移动的体验完全在于你的大脑。

sense_groups.english: Because the part of the brain that's active when you intend to move is the same part that lets you feel like you did.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为当你意图移动时活跃的大脑区域，与让你感觉自己已经移动了的区域是同一个。

sense_groups.english: Two separate brain regions are involved in moving your body.
sense_groups.chinese: 移动身体涉及两个不同的大脑区域。

sense_groups.english: One part provides the intention, and the other powers the actual movement.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个部分提供意图，另一个部分驱动实际运动。

sense_groups.chinese: 但研究人员不知道是哪个部分让你知道自己确实移动了。

sense_groups.english: In the new study, scientists were working with patients undergoing surgery to remove a brain tumor.
sense_groups.chinese: 在这项新研究中，科学家们与正在接受脑肿瘤切除手术的患者合作。

sense_groups.english: Surgeons often electrically stimulate the area around the tumor while the patient is awake and can provide feedback, so they can avoid damaging critical tissue.
sense_groups.chinese: 外科医生通常在患者清醒并能提供反馈时，用电刺激肿瘤周围的区域，以避免损伤关键组织。

sense_groups.english: The scientists found that zapping one particular part of the brain made their patients feel like they wanted to move their arms, lips or tongue.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们发现，刺激大脑的一个特定区域会让患者感觉他们想要移动手臂、嘴唇或舌头。

sense_groups.english: And ramping up the stimulation to that spot made them feel like they'd done it.
sense_groups.chinese: 而增加对该区域的刺激则让他们感觉已经移动了。

sense_groups.english: But when the team poked at the region that actually caused motion, the patients didn't know they moved—a finding that's oddly moving.
sense_groups.chinese: 但当团队刺激实际引起运动的区域时，患者并不知道自己移动了——这一发现令人莫名感动。

questions.en:

sense_groups.chinese: 但只适合那些能忍受辣的人。

questions.name: #84 Origin of Species
questions.en:
In The Origin of Species, Darwin provided abundant evidence that life on Earth has evolved over time, and he proposed natural selection as the primary mechanism for that change.
He observed that individuals ______ in their inherited traits and that selection acts on such differences, leading to ______ change.
Although Darwin realized that variation in heritable traits is a prerequisite for ______ , he did not know precisely how organisms pass heritable traits to their offspring.
Just ______ ______ years after Darwin published The Origin of Species, Gregor Mendel wrote a groundbreaking paper on inheritance in pea plants.
  ______ that paper, Mendel proposed a model of inheritance in which organisms transmit discrete heritable units (now called genes) to their offspring.
  ______ Darwin did not know about genes, Mendel’s paper set the stage ______ understanding the genetic differences on which evolution is based.
1. differ , difference , differing , differentiate
2. evolving , evolutionary , evolve , evolved
3. evolution , development , growth , maturity
4. a few , little , a little , few
5. Of , In , At , With
6. Although , Despite , However , Even
7. for , as , by , on
questions.answer:
1. differ
2. evolutionary
3. evolution
4. few
5. In
6. Although
7. for

sense_groups.english: In The Origin of Species, Darwin provided abundant evidence that life on Earth has evolved over time,
sense_groups.chinese: 在《物种起源》中，达尔文提供了大量证据表明地球上的生命随时间进化，

sense_groups.english: and he proposed natural selection as the primary mechanism for that change.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且他提出自然选择是这种变化的主要机制。

sense_groups.english: He observed that individuals differ in their inherited traits
sense_groups.chinese: 他观察到个体在遗传特征上存在差异，

sense_groups.english: and that selection acts on such differences, leading to evolutionary change.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且选择作用于这些差异，导致进化性变化。

sense_groups.english: Although Darwin realized that variation in heritable traits is a prerequisite for evolution,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管达尔文意识到遗传特征的变异是进化的前提，

sense_groups.english: he did not know precisely how organisms pass heritable traits to their offspring.
sense_groups.chinese: 但他并不确切知道生物体如何将遗传特征传递给后代。

sense_groups.english: Just a few years after Darwin published The Origin of Species,
sense_groups.chinese: 就在达尔文发表《物种起源》几年后，

sense_groups.english: Gregor Mendel wrote a groundbreaking paper on inheritance in pea plants.
sense_groups.chinese: 格雷戈尔·孟德尔写了一篇关于豌豆植物遗传的开创性论文。

sense_groups.english: In that paper, Mendel proposed a model of inheritance
sense_groups.chinese: 在那篇论文中，孟德尔提出了一个遗传模型，

sense_groups.chinese: 其中生物体将离散的遗传单位（现在称为基因）传递给后代。

sense_groups.english: Although Darwin did not know about genes,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管达尔文不知道基因的存在，

sense_groups.english: Mendel’s paper set the stage for understanding the genetic differences on which evolution is based.
sense_groups.chinese: 但孟德尔的论文为理解进化所基于的遗传差异奠定了基础。

questions.name: #85 Smartwatches
questions.en:
More than half of all Americans carry smartphones.
Smartwatches and smartglasses may not be far behind.
What's not all that smart are the rigid ______ that power our gadgets.
But some may soon be replaced by ultra-thin, flexible batteries, sewn right into your clothes.
Researchers built a prototype out of conductive, nickel-coated ______ fabric.
They applied lithium compounds to create the anode and cathode, and separated them with a spandex-like material.
The ______ battery was just half a millimeter thick, with a capacity of 510 milliampere-hours per cubic inch—about a quarter that of the battery in an iPhone 5.
And the tighter the knit, the higher the capacity.
Of course, fabric ______ .
But this battery can too.
Even after being folded 5,500 times, the battery kept trucking.
Thin foil batteries, on the other hand, took just 70 folds to become really foiled.
The findings appear in the journal Nano Letters.
You don't even have to disrobe to charge this ______ battery.
Researchers tacked flexible solar cells to it, so it can charge on the go.
Might be just the thing to make polyester current again.

sense_groups.english: More than half of all Americans carry smartphones.
sense_groups.chinese: 超过一半的美国人携带智能手机。

sense_groups.chinese: 智能手表和智能眼镜可能也不远了。

sense_groups.english: What's not all that smart are the rigid batteries that power our gadgets.
sense_groups.chinese: 不太智能的是为我们的设备供电的刚性电池。

sense_groups.english: But some may soon be replaced by ultra-thin, flexible batteries, sewn right into your clothes.
sense_groups.chinese: 但有些可能很快就会被超薄、灵活的电池取代，直接缝进你的衣服里。

sense_groups.english: Researchers built a prototype out of conductive, nickel-coated polyester fabric.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员用导电的镀镍聚酯纤维织物制作了一个原型。

sense_groups.english: They applied lithium compounds to create the anode and cathode, and separated them with a spandex-like material.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们使用锂化合物来制造阳极和阴极，并用类似氨纶的材料将它们隔开。

sense_groups.chinese: 成品电池只有半毫米厚，每立方英寸容量为510毫安时——大约是iPhone 5电池的四分之一。

sense_groups.english: And the tighter the knit, the higher the capacity.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且编织得越紧，容量越高。

sense_groups.english: Even after being folded 5,500 times, the battery kept trucking.

sense_groups.chinese: 相比之下，薄箔电池只需折叠70次就彻底失效了。

sense_groups.english: The findings appear in the journal Nano Letters.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《纳米快报》上。

sense_groups.english: You don't even have to disrobe to charge this wearable battery.
sense_groups.chinese: 你甚至不需要脱衣服就能给这种可穿戴电池充电。

sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员将柔性太阳能电池附着在上面，这样它就可以在移动中充电。

sense_groups.english: Might be just the thing to make polyester current again.
sense_groups.chinese: 这或许正是让聚酯纤维再次流行起来的东西。

questions.name: #86 Alligators' Lungs
questions.en:
If you've ever been to the ______ , or tuned into the Animal Planet, you know that 'gators can move through the water so ______ , barely ______ a ripple.
It almost looks like they surface and sink, twist and turn, without so much as moving a muscle.
Well, it turns out they are moving some muscles.
Just ones you can't see.
According to a study from the University of Utah, American ______ navigate ______ through the murky water by shifting the location of their lungs.

And using a set of four muscles, including the alligator equivalent of our diaphragm, a gator can basically steer just by moving those floats around.
When they want to surface, they shift their lungs forward.
To dive, they push 'em back.
And to roll off in another ______ , they just shift those babies to one side or the other.
The ______ will appear in the April issue of the Journal of Experimental Biology.
This ability to slice silently through the water without actually having to swim no doubt helps alligators sneak up on unsuspecting prey.
Who never knew what hit them.
And so will never have a chance to say: "See you later, alligator…after a while, crocodile."

questions.name: #87 Global Textile Industry
questions.en:
The environmental impact of the global textile industry is hard to overstate.
One-third of the water used worldwide is spent fashioning fabrics.
For every ton of cloth ______ , 200 tons of water is polluted with chemicals and heavy metals.
An estimated 1 trillion kilowatt-hours of electricity powers the factories that card and comb, spin and weave, and cut and stitch materials into everything from T-shirts to towels, ______ behind mountains of solid waste and a massive carbon footprint.
'Where the industry is today is not really sustainable for the long term,' says Shreyaskar Chaudhary, chief executive of Pratibha Syntex, a textile manufacturer based outside Indore, India.
With something of an 'if you build it, they will come' attitude, Mr.Chaudhary has steered Pratibha ______ the leading edge of eco-friendly textile production.
Under his direction, Pratibha began making clothes with organic cotton in 1999.
Initially, the company couldn't find enough organic farms growing cotton in central India ______ ______ its factories.
To meet production demands, Chaudhary's team had to convince conventional cotton farmers to change their growing methods.
Pratibha provided seeds, cultivation instruction, and a guarantee of fair-trade prices for ______ crops.
Today, Pratibha has a network of 28,000 organic cotton growers across the central states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Orissa.
1. produced , has produced , producing , is produced
2. moving , leaving , processing , looking into
3. against , over , toward , behind
4. have supplied , supplying , to supply , is supplied
5. their , some , mine , them
questions.answer:
1. produced
2. leaving
3. toward
4. to
5. supply
6. their

questions.name: #110 When to Revise?
questions.en:
Timing is important for revision.
Have you noticed that during the school day you get times when you just don't care any longer?
I don't mean the lessons you don't like, but the ones you usually find OK, but on some occasions, you just can't be bothered with it.
You ______ have other things on your mind, be tired, restless or looking forward to what comes next.
Whatever the reason, that particular lesson doesn't get 100 percent ______ from you.
The same is true of revision.
Your mental and physical ______ is important.
If you try to revise when you are tired or totally occupied with something else, your revision will be inefficient and just about worthless.
If you approach it feeling fresh, alert and happy, it will be so much easier, and you will learn more, faster.
However, if you make no plans and just slip in a little bit of revision when you feel like it, you probably won't do much revision!
You need a revision timetable, so you don't keep ______ ______ ______ .
1. may , never , do , hardly
2. effort , satisfaction , affect , effect
3. support , concern , attitude , health
4. stopping , putting it off , giving it up , putting out
questions.answer:
1. may
2. effort
3. attitude
4. putting
5. it
6. off

questions.en:
Developing computational thinking helps students to better understand the world around them.

Paleontologists had previously thought that some dinos' small forelimbs had served to catch insects or rip flesh.
But this new research shows dinosaurs may have used their forelimbs to help with quickness, ______ and agility.
Further study in this field could lead to more accurate ideas of what it once looked like when dinosaurs went dashing through their prehistoric landscape.

2. receivables , grievances , priestesses , researchers

5. findings , sermonizes , portraitists , temporizes
6. Ventricle , Accidental , Experimental , Civil
7. impermeability , wickedly , stability , impenetrability

2. researchers
3. observed
4. hand-raised
5. findings

sense_groups.english: Sometimes it seems there's only so much we can learn about dinosaurs .
sense_groups.chinese: 有时候，我们能了解的恐龙知识似乎很有限。

sense_groups.english: We can't know what their coloration looked like, we can't watch them interact with each other.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们无法知道它们的颜色，也无法观察它们之间的互动。

sense_groups.english: We can only extrapolate from their remains.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们只能从它们的遗骸中推断。

sense_groups.english: But now scientists say we can discern a hint of dinosaur movement - from ostriches.
sense_groups.chinese: 但现在科学家说，我们可以从鸵鸟身上窥见恐龙运动的一点端倪。

sense_groups.english: The giant, flightless birds still have feathered forelimbs that scientists assumed were now solely used for display and temperature regulation.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些巨大的、不会飞的鸟仍然有羽毛覆盖的前肢，科学家曾认为这些前肢现在仅用于展示和调节体温。

sense_groups.english: But researchers from Germany and Belgium carefully hand-raised ostriches, and modeled their movement in the surrounding air streams.
sense_groups.chinese: 但来自德国和比利时的研究人员精心人工饲养了鸵鸟，并模拟了它们在周围气流中的运动。

sense_groups.english: They found that far from being useless in movement, the leftover wings help ostriches break quickly, turn, and zig-zag.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现，这些残留的翅膀在运动中并非无用，反而帮助鸵鸟快速刹车、转弯和曲折行进。

sense_groups.english: The scientists presented their findings at the Society for Experimental Biology's annual conference in Prague.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们在布拉格举行的实验生物学学会年会上展示了他们的发现。

sense_groups.english: Ostriches are descendants of dinosaurs, and the researchers liken ostrich movements to those of bipedal dinosaurs.
sense_groups.chinese: 鸵鸟是恐龙的后裔，研究人员将鸵鸟的运动比作两足恐龙的运动。

sense_groups.english: Paleontologists had previously thought that some dinos' small forelimbs had served to catch insects or rip flesh.
sense_groups.chinese: 古生物学家此前认为，一些恐龙的小前肢用于捕捉昆虫或撕扯肉食。

sense_groups.english: But this new research shows dinosaurs may have used their forelimbs to help with quickness, stability and agility.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这项新研究表明，恐龙可能用前肢来帮助提高速度、稳定性和敏捷性。

sense_groups.english: Further study in this field could lead to more accurate ideas of what it once looked like when dinosaurs went dashing through their prehistoric landscape.
sense_groups.chinese: 该领域的进一步研究可能会让我们更准确地了解恐龙在史前景观中奔跑时的样子。

questions.name: #116 Bacteria Sinus Infections
questions.en:
This is the season when ______ sinus infections run rampant.

Cilia lining our sinuses beat faster, to sweep away germs.
And bacteria-killing nitric oxide gets released into our nasal ______ .
Better bitter sensing means a bigger response.
It's one reason researchers at the Monell Chemical Senses Center are trying to come up with a universal taste test—a standardized measurement of how well we sense flavors.
Because one key to living healthier could be on the tip of your tongue.

4. purposelessly , actually , diagonally , providently

6. causalities , localities , infirmities , cavities

questions.name: #123 Doctors' Messages
questions.en:
The messages doctors give can ______ some treatments' effectiveness.
For example, it seems that information from a doctor affects outcomes for migraine ______ — whether they got a real drug or a placebo.
Researchers studied 66 people with recurring migraines over the course of seven attacks.
During the first ______ , the ______ received no treatment.
For the next six, they were given either a placebo or a drug.

Overall, the drug did work better than the placebo.
But the placebo worked, too—both when the patients were told it was a placebo, and even better when the doctors told them that they were getting the drug.
That is, when the docs set their expectations high.
Meanwhile, the actual drug was least effective when the patients thought it was a placebo.

questions.name: #129 Natural-born Runners
questions.en:
You've probably had the feeling.
Your running shoes are pounding the pavement — then suddenly your pain fades away, and you're feeling euphoric.
The runner's high.
But that biological perk may be limited to mammals that evolved for endurance ______ — like us.
So says a study in the Journal of Experimental Biology.
Researchers had humans and dogs — both natural-born runners — jog a half hour on a treadmill.
Then they sampled their blood for endocannabinoids, some of the ______ thought to trigger the runner's high.
As expected, humans and dogs had much higher levels after the run.
But when ferrets — a ______ species — took the same 30-minute trot, they had no spike in those ______ molecules.
The authors say that's because long-distance running could have helped our hunter-gatherer ancestors find more food — thus increasing their reproductive success.
And they speculate that natural selection may have linked up a feel-good reward to that beneficial ______ .
These days of course, this ancient trait won't help us find extra calories — but it may encourage us to run 'em off.
1. dykes , personalize , classifies , exercise
2. almshouse , turnarounds , compounds , foxhounds
3. excellency , merely , faerie , sedentary
4. groaned , feel-good , inchoate , loaned
5. wager , exchanger , behavior , regulator

sense_groups.english: You've probably had the feeling.

sense_groups.chinese: 你的跑鞋正敲击着路面——然后突然疼痛消失，你感到无比愉悦。

sense_groups.chinese: 但这种生理福利可能仅限于进化出耐力运动的哺乳动物——比如我们。

sense_groups.english: So says a study in the Journal of Experimental Biology.

sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员让人类和狗——都是天生的跑者——在跑步机上慢跑半小时。

sense_groups.english: Then they sampled their blood for endocannabinoids, some of the compounds thought to trigger the runner's high.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后他们抽取血液样本，检测内源性大麻素，这些化合物被认为会引发跑者高潮。

sense_groups.english: As expected, humans and dogs had much higher levels after the run.
sense_groups.chinese: 不出所料，人类和狗在跑步后这些物质的水平要高得多。

sense_groups.english: The authors say that's because long-distance running could have helped our hunter-gatherer ancestors find more food — thus increasing their reproductive success.

sense_groups.english: And they speculate that natural selection may have linked up a feel-good reward to that beneficial behavior.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们推测，自然选择可能将一种愉悦的奖励与这种有益的行为联系在了一起。

sense_groups.english: These days of course, this ancient trait won't help us find extra calories — but it may encourage us to run 'em off.
sense_groups.chinese: 当然，如今这种古老的特质不会帮我们找到额外的卡路里——但它可能会鼓励我们把它们跑掉。

questions.name: #133 Gorongosa
questions.en:
" Gorongosa , which was a jewel of Southern Africa…had great populations of lions, elephants, hippos, buffalo, etcetera.
Absolutely decimated.
So if you went there in the early part of the last decade, in the early 2000s, you might drive for five or six hours and see one warthog, one baboon, maybe."
Biologist Sean B. Carroll, of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
He spoke March 15th in the Great Hall of the Cooper Union here in New York City about his latest book The Serengeti Rules: The Quest to Discovery How Life Works, and Why It Matters.
Gorongosa National Park was ravaged during the Mozambique war for independence from Portugal and then the civil war that followed.
"And a ______ , Greg Carr…was looking for a project to really sink his teeth into and to work on human ______ , became also really interested in conservation, learned about Mozambique…and in 2004 committed a sizeable fortune to helping to restore Gorongosa in partnership with the Mozambique ______ .
And in 2004 surveys showed there were fewer than one ______ large animals in the entire park, and this is a massive place.
So that's all antelope and elephants, all combined, fewer than a thousand of all types combined.
"And I was there last summer as the new survey came in.
A decade later: 72,000 large animals.
Dramatic change.
I'm looking at elephant herds with lots of youngsters.
I'm looking at hippos, groups of hippos….
"So the point is this: the habitat was all there.
The large animals had been shot, poached, used for food, whatever, but the habitat was still there and still ______ .

It is by manipulating the restricted acts through licensing arrangements that rights owners establish and ______ commercial markets.
In contrast to commercial markets, the growth of open source and open content licensing models has challenged established business models.
