questions.name: #135 Paleoanthropologist
questions.en:
Forty years ago yesterday, November 24, 1974, paleoanthropologist Donald Johanson found in Ethiopia what's arguably the most famous and important fossil of a human ______ : Lucy.
Last month, at the ScienceWriters2014 meeting in Columbus, Ohio, Johanson talked about the moment he laid eyes on Lucy.
"On that eventful day in 1974 I was out, with a graduate student, Tom Gray, and we were walking back to our Land Rover to go back to camp to enjoy a swim in the river with the crocodiles and enjoy a nice little lunch.
And I am always looking at the ground.
I find more quarters by parking meters than anybody I know, I think.
And you know how it is you find what you're looking for, right?
"Because a year before the ______ a geologist had left his footprints four-to-five feet away from the ______ , because he was looking for rocks.
I was looking for bones.
And I found a little piece of elbow, that little ______ that allows us to flex and extend our arm.
And I knew from my studies of osteology, of comparative anatomy and so on, that this had to be from a human ancestor.
"And as I looked up the slope, I saw other ______ eroding out.
And we recovered over a two-week-long excavation operation roughly, not counting hand and foot bones, 40 percent of a skeleton.
And this was important because first of all it broke the three-million-year time barrier.
All the fossils older than three million years at that point in the history of paleoanthropology would fit in the palm of your hand…we didn't know it was a new species really until a few years later when we finally ______ in 1978 the name Australopithecus afarensis."
For more, check out the blog item on our Web site by Scientific American's Kate Wong who, with Johanson, co-authored the book Lucy's Legacy.
Kate's blog is titled The Fossil That Revolutionized the Search for Human Origins: A Q&A with Lucy Discoverer Donald Johanson.

3. hinge , axis , pulley , knot
3. ancestor , dulcimer , mantissa , cullender
4. skeleton , singleton , insulin , chairperson
5. malice , deterrence , fragments , ballots
6. published , object , encampment , eructed

questions.name: #151 Mass Extinction
questions.en:
Scientists have discovered the cause of a mass extinction of sea-floor marine organisms 800,000 years ago — which also provides insight into how climate change can impact ______ deep ocean biota.

sense_groups.chinese: 相反，他们发现灭绝是由海洋表面浮游生物的全球变化引起的。

questions.name: #152 Psychology

2. exceed , excel , separate , explore
3. brains , skins , minds , senses
4. assumptions , correlations , investigations , stimulations

questions.answer:

2. explore
3. senses
4. investigations

sense_groups.english: The study of objects constitutes a relatively new field of academic enquiry,
sense_groups.chinese: 物品研究构成了一个相对较新的学术领域，

sense_groups.english: commonly referred to as material culture studies.
sense_groups.chinese: 通常被称为物质文化研究。

sense_groups.english: In certain disciplines, it reigns supreme.
sense_groups.chinese: 在某些学科中，它占据主导地位。

sense_groups.english: Even where written documents survive,

sense_groups.english: In analyzing the physical remains of societies, both past and present,
sense_groups.chinese: 在分析过去和现在的社会的物理遗存时，

sense_groups.chinese: 历史学家、考古学家、人类学家和其他人一直谨慎地提醒我们，物品对不同的人意味着不同的东西。

questions.name: #158 Facial Appearance
questions.en:
Research demonstrates that facial appearance affects social perceptions.
The current research investigates the reverse ______ : Can social perceptions influence facial appearance?
We examine a social tag that is associated with us early in life — our given name.
The hypothesis is that name stereotypes can be manifested in facial appearance, producing a face-name matching effect, ______ both a social perceiver and a computer are able to accurately match a person’s name to his or her face.
In 8 studies we demonstrate the ______ of this effect, as participants examining an unfamiliar face accurately select the person’s true name from a list of several names, significantly above chance level.
We replicate the effect in 2 countries and find that it extends ______ the limits of socioeconomic cues.
We also find the effect using a computer-based paradigm and 94,000 faces.
In our exploration of the underlying mechanism, we show that existing name stereotypes produce the effect, as its occurrence is culture-dependent.
A self-fulfilling prophecy seems to be at work, as initial evidence shows that facial appearance regions that are controlled by the individual (e.g., hairstyle) are sufficient to produce the effect, and socially using one’s given name is necessary to generate the effect.
Together, these studies suggest that facial appearance represents social expectations of how a person with a specific name should look.
In this way a social tag may influence one’s facial appearance.

2. notwithstanding , ever , whereby , despite
3. indolence , evanescence , existence , transience

sense_groups.english: Research demonstrates that facial appearance affects social perceptions.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究表明，面部外观影响社会认知。

sense_groups.english: The current research investigates the reverse possibility : Can social perceptions influence facial appearance?
sense_groups.chinese: 当前研究探讨了相反的可能性：社会认知能否影响面部外观？

sense_groups.english: We examine a social tag that is associated with us early in life — our given name.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们考察了一个与我们早年生活相关的社会标签——我们的名字。

sense_groups.english: The hypothesis is that name stereotypes can be manifested in facial appearance, producing a face-name matching effect, whereby both a social perceiver and a computer are able to accurately match a person’s name to his or her face.
sense_groups.chinese: 假设是名字刻板印象可以体现在面部外观上，产生一种面孔-名字匹配效应，通过这种效应，社会观察者和计算机都能准确地将一个人的名字与其面孔匹配。

sense_groups.english: In 8 studies we demonstrate the existence of this effect, as participants examining an unfamiliar face accurately select the person’s true name from a list of several names, significantly above chance level.
sense_groups.chinese: 在8项研究中，我们证明了这种效应的存在，参与者观察一张陌生面孔时，能从几个名字列表中准确选出该人的真实名字，显著高于随机水平。

sense_groups.english: We replicate the effect in 2 countries and find that it extends beyond the limits of socioeconomic cues.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们在两个国家重复了这一效应，并发现它超越了社会经济线索的限制。

sense_groups.english: We also find the effect using a computer-based paradigm and 94,000 faces.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们还通过计算机范式和94,000张面孔发现了这一效应。

sense_groups.english: In our exploration of the underlying mechanism, we show that existing name stereotypes produce the effect, as its occurrence is culture-dependent.
sense_groups.chinese: 在探索潜在机制时，我们表明现有的名字刻板印象产生了这一效应，因为它的出现依赖于文化。

sense_groups.english: A self-fulfilling prophecy seems to be at work, as initial evidence shows that facial appearance regions that are controlled by the individual (e.g., hairstyle) are sufficient to produce the effect, and socially using one’s given name is necessary to generate the effect.
sense_groups.chinese: 一种自我实现的预言似乎起了作用，初步证据表明，由个体控制的面部外观区域（如发型）足以产生这一效应，而社会性地使用一个人的名字是产生该效应的必要条件。

sense_groups.english: Together, these studies suggest that facial appearance represents social expectations of how a person with a specific name should look.
sense_groups.chinese: 总之，这些研究表明，面部外观代表了社会对拥有特定名字的人应该长什么样的期望。

sense_groups.english: In this way a social tag may influence one’s facial appearance.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过这种方式，社会标签可能影响一个人的面部外观。

questions.name: #166 Edible Insects
questions.en:
Fancy a locust for lunch?
Probably not, if you live in the west, but elsewhere it's a different story.

These caterpillars of the tequila giant-skipper butterfly ______ around $250 a kilogram.
Eating insects makes nutritional sense.

The female gypsy moth, for instance, is about 80 percent protein.
Insects can be a good ______ of vitamins and minerals too: a type of caterpillar (Usta Terpsichore) eaten in Angola is rich in iron, zinc, and thiamine.
What do they taste like?
Ants have a lemon tang, apparently, whereas giant water bugs taste of mint and fire ant pupae of watermelon.
You have probably, inadvertently, already tasted some of these things, as insects are often accidental tourists in other types of food.
The US Food and Drug Administration even issues guidelines for the number of insect parts allowed in certain foods.
For example, it is acceptable for 225 grams of macaroni to contain up to 225 insect fragments.

questions.name: #186 Welfare Morality
questions.en:

Since some people don't contribute and many are irresponsible, the choices of those who do contribute and are responsible are either to ______ the free riders, refuse to pay for the ______ of their irresponsibility or trust the state to ______ them.

questions.name: #188 Migrating Birds

questions.full:

sense_groups.english: For birdwatchers in southern New Mexico, September can be highly entertaining.

sense_groups.english: Good numbers of many diverse species are on the move during this time,

questions.name: #197 Salmon
questions.en:
Each fall, thousands of coho salmon flock to ______ rivers to spawn.
But many never get the chance, especially near big cities like Seattle.
"And in some of these urban areas, up to 90 percent of the females were dying before they spawned, which is not a good thing for a population long term." Julann Spromberg , a toxicologist affiliated with the Northwest Fisheries Science Center.
Researchers suspected these deaths were partly a matter of bad timing.
The fish often reach streams during the first showers of the rainy season, which flush chemicals from roads and parking lots into the water.
Now, Spromberg and her colleagues have produced the first direct evidence that this runoff kills coho salmon.
Their study is in the Journal of Applied Ecology.
The researchers found that fish exposed to storm water from Seattle-area highways quickly grew sick and died.
Surprisingly, though, the salmon did not seem to mind taking a dip in a cocktail of common road pollutants, including ______ and metals.
That detail suggests the killer ingredient in runoff may be a different kind of chemical or a lethal combination of several ______ .
"There's a whole lot of stuff in here that we haven't been able to measure or don't have the capabilities of ______ at this point."
However, Spromberg says there's a way to help the fish even before scientists hunt down the culprit.
Her team also found that ______ runoff through just a few feet of soil made storm water safe for salmon.
Cities can ______ this simple form of clean water technology by building more systems, including roadside rain gardens, to collect runoff from paved areas and pass it through soil before it enters urban waterways.
Literally a quick and dirty solution.
1. Protect , Meant , Rebuilt , Northwest
2. hydrocarbons , carcass , mothers , harness
3. compounds , bloodhounds , knockouts , dropouts
4. frittering , measuring , glistening , heralding
5. stencilling , pressuring , pensioning , filtering
6. polemicist , littlest , implement , dissonant
questions.answer:
1. Northwest
2. hydrocarbons
3. compounds
4. measuring
5. filtering
6. implement

questions.name: #201 Paraphrasing (B)
questions.en:
We define paraphrasing as putting a passage from an author into your own words.
However, what are your own words?
How different must your paraphrase be from the original ?
The answer is it should be considerably different.
The whole point of paraphrasing is to show you have read and understood another person's ideas, and can summarize them in your own writing style rather than borrowing their phrases.
If you just change a few words, or add some bits of your own to an otherwise reproduced passage, you will probably be penalized for plagiarism .
You should aim to condense and simplify a writer's ideas and describe them using different sentence structures and expressions.
1. original , conventional , concept , rule
2. whole , single , odd , singular
3. borrowing , renewing , changing , charging
4. otherwise , unnecessarily , either , often
5. donation , plagiarism , compilation , contribution
6. fix , simplify , concoct , mix
7. to use , using , used , use

questions.name: #212 Cell Template
questions.en:
One of the great promises of stem-cell biology is to use a patient's own cells as a template to build a real, working organ or tissue in the lab.
One prime example: a ______ for diabetes by turning stem cells into working pancreatic beta cells, which release insulin.
"The existing beta cells that our lab and others had created were 90 percent of the way there.
But 90 percent still means not functional." Ron Evans, a molecular ______ at the Salk Institute.
Evans compares the stem-cell-derived beta cells they first made to a darkened room.
"If you walk into that room, there may be everything in it that you need to be a complete room, with furniture and chairs and everything else.
But it's dark.
And the key is: what do you need to turn on the light?"
That light switch, Evans discovered, is a gene—called estrogen-related receptor gamma.
Flip it on, and it ______ a genetic circuit that ramps up mitochondria production, powers up the cell, and endows the almost-functional beta cells with the ability to sense glucose and release insulin in ______ .
Evans's team recently used that trick to transform stem cells into beta cells that worked just like they would in a healthy pancreas.
When they transplanted those cells into mice with a mouse version of diabetes, blood glucose fell to normal levels in half the rodents.
The results are in the journal Cell Metabolism.
Next, Evans says he'll replicate the test in diabetic primates.
"Primates get diabetes in a fashion that's very similar to people.
So if it works in a primate, very high probability that it's going to work in people." If it does, we might someday replace a shot of insulin with a shot of cells.

2. incompetent , biologist , ethologist , conglomerate
3. dais , renegades , situates , activates
4. drops , calms , response , aristocrats

questions.name: #215 Marshmallow Test
questions.en:
Mischel is the creator of the marshmallow test, one of the most famous experiments in the history of psychology, which is often cited as evidence of the importance of self-control.
In the original test, which was administered at the Bing Nursery School, at Stanford, in the nineteen-sixties, Mischel's team would present a child with a treat (marshmallows were just one option) and tell her that she could either eat the one treat ______ or wait alone in the room for several minutes until the researcher returned, at which point she could have two treats.
The promised treats were always visible and the child knew that all she had to do to stop the agonizing ______ was ring a bell to call the experimenter back--although in that ______ , she wouldn't get the second treat.
The longer a child delayed gratification, Mischel found--that is, the longer she was able to wait--the better she would fare later in life at numerous measures of what we now call executive function.
She would ______ better academically, earn more money, and be healthier and happier.
She would also be more likely to avoid a number of negative outcomes, including jail time, obesity, and drug use.
1. ironically , impressively , immediately , imaginatively
2. sleep , wait , walk , time
3. quantity , case , span , consumption
4. slump , heave , slumber , perform

questions.name: #216 Gunpowder and Fireworks
questions.en:
Gunpowder and fireworks might have been invented independently in Europe, but they probably reached Europe via the Mongols, who spread west from China as far as central Europe by the mid-13th century.
In 1267, the English monk Roger Bacon ______ ______ what were very likely firecrackers, which he compared with the flash of lightning and growl of thunder.
In 1377 fireworks accompanied a religious mystery play by the bishop's palace in Vicenza, and were soon used to add sparks to figures of doves, representing the Holy Spirit, or angels, made to ascend and descend from the heavens on ropes.
By the 15th century, rockets were being used in Europe for military and peaceful purposes.
Italian and Spanish cities in particular ______ ______ ______ fireworks for outdoor celebrations.
The Italian metallurgist Vannoccio Biringuccio described festivities in Florence and Siena for feast days.
These included 'girandoles' or whirling decorated wheels packed with fireworks which ______ ______ ______ a rope hung across a street or square.
Fireworks were also used in the German lands.
An elaborate colour-painted book ______ the Schembart carnival of Nuremberg, which saw men dressed in brightly-coloured costumes parading through the town.
Often these included some kind of pyrotechnics.
One image shows a man wearing a hat in the form of a castle with fireworks and smoke shooting up from the towers, and interestingly, what looks like a smoking artichoke.

2. initially using , began use , began to use , beginning to using
3. were suspending by , was suspended within , was suspended from , suspending from
4. souvenirs , commemorates , calculates , communicates

questions.name: #218 PIE
questions.en:
No matter whether you speak English or Urdu, Waloon or Waziri, Portuguese or Persian, the roots of your language are the same.
Proto-Indo-European (PIE) is the mother tongue — shared by several hundred contemporary languages, as well as many now extinct, and spoken by people ______ lived from about 6,000 to 3,500 BC on the steppes to the north of the Caspian Sea.
They left no written texts and ______ historical linguists have, since the 19th century, painstakingly reconstructed the language from daughter languages, the question of how it actually sounded was assumed to be permanently out of reach.
Now, researchers at the Universities of Cambridge and Oxford have developed a sound-based method to move back through the family tree of languages that stem from PIE.
They can simulate how certain words ______ ______ ______ when they were spoken 8,000 years ago.
Remarkably, at the ______ of the technology is the statistics of shape.
'Sounds have shape,' explains Professor John Aston, from Cambridge's Statistical Laboratory.
'As a word is uttered it vibrates air, and the shape of this soundwave can be measured and turned into a series of numbers.
Once we have these stats, and the stats of another spoken word, we can start asking how similar they are and what it would take to shift from one to another.'
1. where , which , what , who
2. despite , until , however , although
3. would have sounded , would sound , have sounded , sound
4. cost , heart , end , moment
questions.answer:
1. who
2. although
3. would
4. have
5. sounded
6. heart

'As a word is uttered it vibrates air, and the shape of this soundwave can be measured and turned into a series of numbers.

questions.name: #225 Hibernation
questions.en:

Animals in hot climates also ______ a form of hibernation called aestivation.
This works in a similar way and enables them to survive extreme heat, drought or lack of food.

Depending on the species, it can vary from long, deep unconsciousness to light spells of inactivity.

1. Instead , So , Therefore , However
2. undermine , undergo , transform , undo
3. oblivious , profound , pressing , professional
4. disgusting , delivered , vulnerable , equal

questions.name: #228 Manga
questions.en:
If Japan's rise to economic superpower dominated U.S. academic discussions in the 1980s, the last 15 years or so have been ______ by an intense fascination, both in academic and popular discourse, with the country's perceived increase in global cultural influence.
As Pokémon and Hello Kitty invaded U.S. TV screens and supermarket aisles at a time when, paradoxically, Japanese economic influence was on the decline, U.S. scholars started to point to the emergence of a new kind of Japanese superpower.
The discussion shifted from Japan's Gross National Product to its "Gross National Cool".
The characters in Japanese animated cartoon series and in the related genre of manga (Japanese-style comic books or graphic novels), along with their video game cousins, came to symbolize a new order in millennial capitalism ______ by a decline in U.S. cultural hegemony and the fragmentation of global powers.
Thus, Japanese animation provides a logical starting point to an analysis aimed at decentralizing the role of the United States as the world’s most significant global cultural producer.
This chapter will demonstrate, however, that while intending to point to Japan's growing influence and to a ______ relative decline in U.S. power, the academic and popular discourse about Japanese animation's "global" popularity has paradoxically resulted in the re-centralizing of the United States as both a global cultural producer and a consumer of globalized cultural forms.
Turning a translocal lens to the genre's transnational spread, this chapter illustrates the multiple ways in which this discourse is problematic.
Throughout the chapter, the names of a few scholars will frequently reappear.
These scholars are most assertively critiqued here not because their work is particularly problematic but, ______ ______ ______ , because they have produced the most comprehensive and sophisticated studies of Japanese animation and/or comics.
Their works have become seminal texts in the academic study of Japanese popular culture in general and have greatly contributed to our understanding of its influence in the U.S. context.
The chapter's deconstruction of these scholars' characterization of global processes is offered in an effort to illustrate the productive potential of a more translocal approach.
It does not invalidate their ______ positive contributions to the field of Japanese studies.
1. marked , dedicated , made , inspired
2. pocessed , characterized , opposed , tangled
3. concomitant , discrete , proportional , legitimate
4. however , on the contrary , in addition , on the whole
5. otherwise , likewise , likely , unlikely

1. marked
2. characterized
3. concomitant
4. on
5. the
6. contrary
7. otherwise

sense_groups.english: The chapter's deconstruction of these scholars' characterization of global processes is offered in an effort to illustrate the productive potential of a more translocal approach.

questions.name: #229 FIB
questions.en:

Because beneath their rocky ______ , some terrestrial planets may be half diamond.
So said ______ at the fall meeting of the American Geophysical Union.
The ______ were fixing to study how diamonds form here on Earth, under the conditions found in the planet's lower mantle.
So they took a tiny sample of iron, carbon, and oxygen, ______ abundant in Earth's ______ , and cooked it up at about 3,800 degrees Fahrenheit and 9.5 million pounds of pressure per square inch.
What they saw was that iron hooks up with oxygen to produce rust, and leaves behind pockets of carbon, which become diamond.
Now, what happens if they look not at Earth but at a planet in a solar system where there's even more carbon?
According to the model, the carbon merges with iron to form a core made of steel, leaving a carbon mantle rich with diamond.
Whether the Milky Way harbors such gems is still an open question.
One thing is for sure: they probably wouldn't harbor life.
Because diamonds readily transfer heat.
So a planet made of diamond would be one cold stone.

questions.name: #238 Babies
questions.en:
How can you tell the difference between a French baby and a German baby?
No, it's not that one is wearing a saucy little beret while the other is tucked into tiny pair of lederhosen.
Well, maybe that's part of it.
But a new study in the journal Current Biology shows that the babies actually sound different.
Because the melody of an infant's cry matches its mother tongue.
We all know that babies start ______ while they're still in the womb.
So when they come out, they know their mother's voice.
When they're older, they start to imitate the sounds they hear.
Eventually they babble, and then start to speak, and then you never hear the end of it.
But long before that first burble or coo, babies are learning the ______ of language.
A team of scientists recorded the cries of 60 ______ : 30 born into ______ families and 30 that heard German.
And they found that French infants wail on a rising note while the Germans favor a falling melody .
Those ______ match the rhythms of their native languages.
So next time you hear a baby cry, listen closely.
He could be telling you where he's from.
1. cantilevering , eavesdropping , reasoning , peopling
2. portentousness , relentlessness , hydrocephalus , elements
3. roomfuls , goofballs , newborns , dessertspoonfuls
4. Mechanizing , Surceasing , French-speaking , Grieving
5. patterns , sponges , assassins , actions

sense_groups.english: How can you tell the difference between a French baby and a German baby?
sense_groups.chinese: 你怎么区分法国婴儿和德国婴儿？

sense_groups.english: No, it's not that one is wearing a saucy little beret while the other is tucked into tiny pair of lederhosen.
sense_groups.chinese: 不，不是其中一个戴着俏皮的小贝雷帽，而另一个穿着小皮裤。

sense_groups.english: Well, maybe that's part of it.

sense_groups.english: But a new study in the journal Current Biology shows that the babies actually sound different.

sense_groups.english: Because the melody of an infant's cry matches its mother tongue.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为婴儿哭声的旋律与其母语相匹配。

sense_groups.english: We all know that babies start eavesdropping while they're still in the womb.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们都知道婴儿还在子宫里时就开始偷听了。

sense_groups.english: So when they come out, they know their mother's voice.

sense_groups.english: When they're older, they start to imitate the sounds they hear.
sense_groups.chinese: 当他们长大一点，他们开始模仿听到的声音。

sense_groups.english: Eventually they babble, and then start to speak, and then you never hear the end of it.
sense_groups.chinese: 最终他们咿呀学语，然后开始说话，然后你就再也听不到尽头了。

sense_groups.english: But long before that first burble or coo, babies are learning the elements of language.
sense_groups.chinese: 但在第一次咕咕声之前很久，婴儿就在学习语言的要素了。

sense_groups.english: A team of scientists recorded the cries of 60 newborns: 30 born into French-speaking families and 30 that heard German.
sense_groups.chinese: 一组科学家记录了60名新生儿的哭声：30名出生在讲法语的家庭，30名听到德语。

sense_groups.english: And they found that French infants wail on a rising note while the Germans favor a falling melody.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现法国婴儿的哭声音调上升，而德国婴儿则偏爱下降的旋律。

sense_groups.english: Those patterns match the rhythms of their native languages.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些模式与他们母语的节奏相匹配。

sense_groups.english: So next time you hear a baby cry, listen closely.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以下次你听到婴儿哭时，仔细听。

sense_groups.english: He could be telling you where he's from.
sense_groups.chinese: 他可能正在告诉你他来自哪里。

questions.name: #239 Ants
questions.en:
Ants are known for working together, operating as a unit for the good of the colony.
But not so fast, say researchers from the Universities of Leeds and Copenhagen.
It turns out that ants can scheme like a stage mom.
  ______ say that some ants hide out to ensure that their offspring become child-bearing queens instead of barren workers.
The ______ hypothesis had been that random ants were fed certain foods that would allow them to develop into queens.
But DNA tests on five ______ of leaf-cutting ants ______ that certain males have a better genetic chance of producing royal progeny.
Scientists believe these rare males stay anonymous, and thus avoid any problems with other ants that might otherwise lose their "one-for-all, all-for-one" attitude.
In fact, the number of males carrying royal genes to those who aren't may have settled at a low ratio through evolution —which cobbled together the best way for the ant gene pool to expand, while at the same time keeping the lucky males hidden from their possibly jealous rivals.
1. Elephantiasis , Contrivances , Retroviruses , Scientists
2. preexisted , chairlift , accepted , intermarriage
3. anthologies , colonies , velocities , aristocracies
4. critiqued , teed , kneeled , revealed
5. carrying , birdying , disembodying , lobbying
6. ablution , occlusion , prosecution , evolution

sense_groups.english: Ants are known for working together, operating as a unit for the good of the colony.
sense_groups.chinese: 蚂蚁以协同工作而闻名，为了蚁群的利益而像一个整体一样运作。

sense_groups.english: But not so fast, say researchers from the Universities of Leeds and Copenhagen.
sense_groups.chinese: 但利兹大学和哥本哈根大学的研究人员说，别这么快下结论。

sense_groups.english: It turns out that ants can scheme like a stage mom.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实证明，蚂蚁可以像舞台妈妈一样耍心机。

sense_groups.english: Scientists say that some ants hide out to ensure that their offspring become child-bearing queens instead of barren workers.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家说，有些蚂蚁躲藏起来，以确保它们的后代成为能生育的蚁后，而不是不育的工蚁。

sense_groups.english: The accepted hypothesis had been that random ants were fed certain foods that would allow them to develop into queens.
sense_groups.chinese: 之前被接受的假设是，随机蚂蚁被喂食某些食物，使它们能够发育成蚁后。

sense_groups.english: But DNA tests on five colonies of leaf-cutting ants revealed that certain males have a better genetic chance of producing royal progeny.
sense_groups.chinese: 但对五个切叶蚁群落的DNA测试揭示，某些雄性有更好的遗传机会产生王室后代。

sense_groups.english: Scientists believe these rare males stay anonymous, and thus avoid any problems with other ants that might otherwise lose their 'one-for-all, all-for-one' attitude.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家认为，这些稀有的雄性保持匿名，从而避免与其他蚂蚁产生任何问题，否则其他蚂蚁可能会失去它们‘我为人人，人人为我’的态度。

sense_groups.english: In fact, the number of males carrying royal genes to those who aren't may have settled at a low ratio through evolution —which cobbled together the best way for the ant gene pool to expand, while at the same time keeping the lucky males hidden from their possibly jealous rivals.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，携带王室基因的雄性数量与不携带的相比，可能通过进化稳定在一个低比例——这拼凑出了蚂蚁基因库扩展的最佳方式，同时让这些幸运的雄性躲过可能嫉妒的竞争对手。

4. raise , rise , enlarge , uphold

questions.name: #242 Motorcyclist Accident
questions.en:
May 15, 2008 When motorcyclists have an accident they roll a dice, with escaping ______ on one side and very severe consequences on the other.
And for those unlucky enough to ______ severe and permanent injuries like paraplegia, there's often one huge regret - that they may never ride again on a real bike.
A chance encounter with a paraplegic ex-motorcross champion in a hospital carpark inspired West Australian Darren Lomman to put together an audacious project: a motorcycle for paraplegic riders - and his working prototype, a heavily modified Honda CBR250RR, is now road licensed and ______ .
With the right investment and profile, Lomman believes the Dreamfit bike isn't too far away from production potential - and after around 150 enquiries from all around the world, he would love to be able to put the bikes in the hands of more people for whom riding has become an impossible dream.
Started as a university project, the Dreamfit CBR250RR has been modified to ______ riders paralyzed from the chest down, with thumb-activated pneumatic rams for foot-free gear shifting, a combined braking system, custom-moulded ergonomic cups to hold the rider in place without any lower body strength, and a set of steel-braced "landing gear" wheels that drop to provide stability at very low speeds.

2. sustain , spend , forbid , expect
3. invented , expensive , operational , exempted
4. shape , suit , reform , avoid

sense_groups.english: To investigate, Liang Li and Edward Cox at Princeton University studied the movements of amoebas (Dictyostelium) in a Petri dish, recording the paths travelled by 12 amoebas, including every turn and movement straight ahead, for 8 to 10 hours per amoeba.

sense_groups.english: Immediately after an amoeba turned right, it was twice as likely to turn left as right again, and vice versa, they told a meeting of the American Physical Society meeting in Denver, Colorado, last week.
sense_groups.chinese: 上周，他们在科罗拉多州丹佛市举行的美国物理学会会议上报告说，变形虫向右转后，向左转的可能性是再次向右转的两倍，反之亦然。

sense_groups.english: Using less energy saves money and lowers greenhouse gas emissions .
sense_groups.chinese: 使用更少的能源可以省钱并减少温室气体排放。

sense_groups.english: And various studies have looked at ways to get households to use less energy.
sense_groups.chinese: 各种研究已经探索了让家庭减少能源使用的方法。

sense_groups.english: Now there's evidence that people in such a study use less energy…because they're in a study.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在有证据表明，参与此类研究的人会减少能源使用……因为他们正在被研究。

sense_groups.english: The general phenomenon is called the Hawthorne effect: study subjects change their behavior because they're being observed.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一普遍现象被称为霍桑效应：研究对象因为被观察而改变行为。

sense_groups.english: So researchers collaborated with a utility to test for the Hawthorne effect in electricity use.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，研究人员与一家公用事业公司合作，测试电力使用中的霍桑效应。

sense_groups.english: They monitored almost 5,600 randomly selected households.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们监测了近5600个随机选择的家庭。

sense_groups.english: Half received a postcard saying that their energy use would be monitored for a month for research purposes.
sense_groups.chinese: 一半家庭收到明信片，告知他们的能源使用将因研究目的被监测一个月。

sense_groups.english: They also got four follow-up reminder postcards over the month.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们还在一个月内收到了四张后续提醒明信片。

sense_groups.english: They received no other information, instructions or incentives.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们没有收到其他信息、指示或激励。

sense_groups.english: The control group monitored for the study got no notifications.
sense_groups.chinese: 作为研究对照组的监测家庭没有收到任何通知。

sense_groups.english: That group continued using the same amount of electricity.
sense_groups.chinese: 该组继续使用相同数量的电力。

sense_groups.english: But the families being tracked reduced energy use 2.7 percent.
sense_groups.chinese: 但被追踪的家庭减少了2.7%的能源使用。

sense_groups.english: And when the study period ended, their energy use shot back up.
sense_groups.chinese: 当研究期结束时，他们的能源使用量又回升了。

sense_groups.english: The report is in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
sense_groups.chinese: 该报告发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

sense_groups.english: Clearly, mindful consumers can find ways to easily lower their energy consumption.
sense_groups.chinese: 显然，有意识的消费者可以找到轻松降低能源消耗的方法。

sense_groups.english: Perhaps policy makers can find a way to use the Hawthorne effect to everyone's advantage.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许政策制定者可以找到一种方法，利用霍桑效应造福所有人。

questions.name: #262 Flexibility
questions.en:
Engineers would love to embed flexible ______ into things like paper, or surgical gloves or conventional clothing.
But the wiring usually gets twisted and damaged.
Now M.I.T. ______ have found inspiration in an ______ place—the annoying air pockets that pop up in parking pass stickers on car windows.
Those bubbles arise because the thin sticker film expands at a different rate than the window glass when they both heat up.
And the opposite is also true—the material can compress differently than the glass until it separates and blisters form.
The scientists were ______ this kind of wrinkling behavior.
They developed a model that predicted the formation, size and evolution of the bubbles that depends on three things: the elasticity of the film and the glass, and the strength of the bond between them.
Then they realized that carefully controlled delamination could be applied to make elastic electronics.
Wires in the bubbly elastic material would start out only partially attached to a surface.
So there'd be some slack allowing for safe stretching and ______ .
The work appears in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, and shows that a different ______ can make a tough problem less sticky.

2. receivables , alveolars , timeservers , researchers
3. divinely , benignly , blimey , unlikely
4. studying , dallying , flurrying , lobbying
5. twisting , sending , interconnecting , unwilling
6. guffawed , shoed , approach , emote
questions.answer:

2. researchers
3. unlikely
4. studying
5. twisting
6. approach

questions.en:

The study is in the Journal of Experimental Biology.

So before you break out the bibs and melted butter, it might be nice to put your future dinner on a little anesthetic ice.

Another third covered complaints, criticisms and gossip.

questions.name: #268 Flower Color
questions.en:
A flower's color, however, isn't a full-proof guide to a good lunch.
That's because the color can change depending on the angle at which sunlight hits its petals.
A yellow flower, for example, may look somewhat blue from one angle and red from another.
Scientists call this kind of color change iridescence.
'It's the same phenomenon that makes a rainbow appear in a soap bubble or on a CD,' says Beverley Glover.
She studies plants at the University of Cambridge in England.
In 2009, Glover and her colleagues showed that even when petals look shimmery, bees can still tell which flowers likely hold food.
But she and others noticed something odd about ______ .
It's not quite as flashy in plants as in other life forms, Glover says.
The backs of jewel, beetles, or the wings of certain butterflies, for instance, shine and shimmer a lot more.
The researchers tested their hypothesis in the lab.
They trained a group of bees to associate fake purple flowers with getting more nectar.
Then the team ______ the bees.
They added non-shimmery fake flowers with purple-blue and purple-red hues to the bees' flight path.
The bees passed the test, ignoring flowers that weren't ______ purple.
The second group of bees was ______ to drink from fully flashy, 'perfectly iridescent' purple flowers.
But when the team added perfectly iridescent flowers in different hues, the insects checked them for nectar too.
1. pattern , shape , texture , iridescence
2. challenged , circled , tested , cursed
3. surprisingly , perfectly , roughly , narrowly
4. threatened , described , trained , persuaded

sense_groups.english: But doctors, nurses, and other hospital staff may devote extra time and attention to the needs of families whose loved ones are near the end.

sense_groups.english: That compassion is what families who lose a loved one are responding to when they report a more satisfactory ICU experience.
sense_groups.chinese: 正是这种同情心，让失去亲人的家庭在报告更满意的ICU体验时做出了回应。

sense_groups.english: Just having someone who'll explain what's going on, answer their questions and offer emotional support makes all the difference.

sense_groups.english: An observation that, in the end, is maybe not so surprising.
sense_groups.chinese: 这个观察结果，最终也许并不那么令人惊讶。

questions.name: #271 Behavior Segments
questions.en:
One of the most ______ of psychologists, Clark Hull, claimed that the essence of reasoning lies in the putting together of two 'behavior segments' in some ______ way, never actually performed before, so as to reach a ______ .
Two followers of Clark Hull, Howard and Tracey Kendler, devised a test for children that was ______ based on Clark Hull's principles.

In order to succeed they had to go through a two-stage sequence.
1. radical , eminent , elementary , ideal
2. novel , broad , stingy , ordinary
3. goal , category , description , rate
4. collectively , explicitly , approximately , randomly
5. multiplication , task , area , volume
questions.full:
One of the most ______ of psychologists, Clark Hull, claimed that the essence of reasoning lies in the putting together of two 'behavior segments' in some ______ way, never actually performed before, so as to reach a ______ .

1. radical , eminent , elementary , ideal
2. novel , broad , stingy , ordinary
3. goal , category , description , rate
4. collectively , explicitly , approximately , randomly
5. multiplication , task , area , volume

答案:
1. eminent
2. novel
3. goal
4. explicitly
5. task

sense_groups.english: One of the most eminent of psychologists, Clark Hull, claimed that the essence of reasoning lies in the putting together of two 'behavior segments' in some novel way, never actually performed before, so as to reach a goal.
sense_groups.chinese: 最杰出的心理学家之一克拉克·赫尔声称，推理的本质在于以某种新颖的方式将两个‘行为片段’组合在一起，这种方式以前从未实际执行过，以便达到一个目标。

sense_groups.english: Two followers of Clark Hull, Howard and Tracey Kendler, devised a test for children that was explicitly based on Clark Hull's principles.
sense_groups.chinese: 克拉克·赫尔的两位追随者霍华德和特雷西·肯德勒设计了一项针对儿童的测试，该测试明确基于克拉克·赫尔的原则。

sense_groups.english: The children were given the task of learning to operate a machine so as to get a toy.
sense_groups.chinese: 孩子们被赋予学习操作一台机器以获取玩具的任务。

sense_groups.english: In order to succeed they had to go through a two-stage sequence.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了成功，他们必须经历一个两阶段的序列。

questions.name: #272 Supply and Demand
questions.en:
The supply of a thing, in the phrase "supply and demand", is the amount that will be offered for sale at each of a series of prices; the demand is the amount that will be bought at each of a series of prices.
The principle that value depends on supply and demand means that in the case of nearly every commodity, more will be bought if the price is lowered, less will be bought if the price is ______ .
Therefore sellers, if they wish to induce buyers to ______ more of a commodity than they are already doing, must reduce its price; if they raise its price, they will sell less.
If there is a general falling off, if in demand — due, say, to trade depression — sellers will either have to ______ prices or put less on the ______ ; they will not be able to sell the same ______ at the same price.
1. higher , kept , folded , raised
2. remove , judge , hide , take
3. trade , treat , describe , reduce
4. store , way , market , panel
5. quality , patch , amount , deal
questions.full:
The supply of a thing, in the phrase "supply and demand", is the amount that will be offered for sale at each of a series of prices; the demand is the amount that will be bought at each of a series of prices.
The principle that value depends on supply and demand means that in the case of nearly every commodity, more will be bought if the price is lowered, less will be bought if the price is ______ .
Therefore sellers, if they wish to induce buyers to ______ more of a commodity than they are already doing, must reduce its price; if they raise its price, they will sell less.
If there is a general falling off, if in demand — due, say, to trade depression — sellers will either have to ______ prices or put less on the ______ ; they will not be able to sell the same ______ at the same price.

1. higher , kept , folded , raised
2. remove , judge , hide , take
3. trade , treat , describe , reduce
4. store , way , market , panel
5. quality , patch , amount , deal

答案:
1. raised
2. take
3. reduce
4. market
5. amount

sense_groups.english: The supply of a thing, in the phrase "supply and demand", is the amount that will be offered for sale at each of a series of prices;
sense_groups.chinese: 在“供求关系”这个短语中，一种物品的供给是指在一系列价格下愿意出售的数量；

sense_groups.english: the demand is the amount that will be bought at each of a series of prices.
sense_groups.chinese: 需求是指在一系列价格下愿意购买的数量。

sense_groups.english: The principle that value depends on supply and demand means that in the case of nearly every commodity, more will be bought if the price is lowered, less will be bought if the price is raised.
sense_groups.chinese: 价值取决于供求关系的原则意味着，对于几乎每一种商品，价格降低时购买量会增加，价格提高时购买量会减少。

sense_groups.english: Therefore sellers, if they wish to induce buyers to take more of a commodity than they are already doing, must reduce its price;
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，如果卖家希望促使买家购买比现有更多的商品，就必须降低价格；

sense_groups.english: if they raise its price, they will sell less.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果提高价格，销量就会减少。

sense_groups.english: If there is a general falling off in demand — due, say, to trade depression — sellers will either have to reduce prices or put less on the market;
sense_groups.chinese: 如果需求普遍下降——比如由于贸易萧条——卖家要么必须降价，要么减少投放市场的数量；

sense_groups.english: they will not be able to sell the same amount at the same price.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们将无法以同样的价格卖出同样的数量。

questions.name: #273 Conservationists
questions.en:
Conservationists have long debated whether the koala should go on the Australian national threatened species list.
  ______ the koala is clearly in trouble in some parts of the country – in Queensland, for example, high numbers ______ ______ by disease – in other parts such as Victoria and South Australia the problem is not that koala populations ______ ______ , but that they have grown to the point where they are almost too numerous.
For a species to be classed as vulnerable, its population ______ ______ ______ by more than 30 percent over the last three generations or 10 years.
The problem is that when such a stipulation is applied to koalas, the Victorian boom offsets the Queensland bust, and the species stays off the list.
This has repercussions because northern koalas are different to southern ones.
They are smaller, for example, and they contain a genetic ______ not represented in the South.
  ______ ______ ______ , a split listing has been devised koalas from New South Wales, the ACT and Queensland are now officially 'Vulnerable'; those from Victoria and South Australia are not considered threatened.
1. But , While , Like , Because
2. have afflicted , are afflicted , are afflicting , afflicted
3. are falling , are fallen , falls , fallen
4. must have decreased , decreased , decrease , must decrease
5. expansion , extension , explanation , variation
6. Nonetheless , For example , As an addition , For this reason
questions.answer:
1. While
2. are
3. afflicted
4. falling
5. must
6. have
7. decreased
8. variation
9. For
10. this
11. reason

sense_groups.english: Conservationists have long debated whether the koala should go on the Australian national threatened species list.
sense_groups.chinese: 环保主义者长期以来一直在争论考拉是否应该被列入澳大利亚国家濒危物种名单。

sense_groups.english: While the koala is clearly in trouble in some parts of the country – in Queensland, for example, high numbers are afflicted by disease –
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然考拉在该国某些地区明显陷入困境——例如在昆士兰，大量考拉受到疾病困扰——

sense_groups.english: in other parts such as Victoria and South Australia the problem is not that koala populations are falling,
sense_groups.chinese: 但在维多利亚和南澳大利亚等其他地区，问题不在于考拉数量在下降，

sense_groups.english: but that they have grown to the point where they are almost too numerous.
sense_groups.chinese: 而是它们已经增长到几乎过多的程度。

sense_groups.english: For a species to be classed as vulnerable, its population must have decreased by more than 30 percent over the last three generations or 10 years.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个物种要被列为易危，其数量必须在过去三代或10年内减少超过30%。

sense_groups.english: For this reason, a split listing has been devised: koalas from New South Wales, the ACT and Queensland are now officially 'Vulnerable'; those from Victoria and South Australia are not considered threatened.
sense_groups.chinese: 出于这个原因，人们设计了一种分列名单：来自新南威尔士州、首都领地和昆士兰州的考拉现在被正式列为“易危”；来自维多利亚州和南澳大利亚州的考拉不被视为受威胁。

questions.name: #274 Research Ship
questions.en:
The modern research ship takes its origins from the early exploration voyages such as HMS Endeavour and HMS Challenger, both of which were converted vessels, fitted with a range of research facilities to sample and measure across a range of disciplines in extreme environments.
Early research vessels were fairly basic and simplistic compared to the state-of-the-art ships we see being developed today.
Gradually, the trend of converting other vessels into research ships ______ ______ by the challenging demands of investigating increasingly complex areas of oceanographic research, such as physical, biological and chemical oceanography; marine geology and geophysics; ocean engineering and atmospheric science in one expedition.
In order to carry ______ multi-disciplinary research in extreme environments, specially designed research vessels became a requirement.
Research ships are the primary source of oceanographic observations and ______ ______ so for the foreseeable future.
As time goes on ,science is likely to be conducted in increasingly remote and environmentally challenging areas, including the polar seas, so the ability to operate with minimal interruptions from the natural elements remains unchanged from the days of the Challenger Expedition.
1. was challenged , was a challenge , were challenged , will have been challenged
2. over , out , of , through
3. will have remained , remaining , remains , will remain
4. flies away , goes on , disappears , moves

2. challenged
3. out
4. will

sense_groups.english: The modern research ship takes its origins from the early exploration voyages such as HMS Endeavour and HMS Challenger,
sense_groups.chinese: 现代研究船起源于早期的探险航行，比如HMS奋进号和HMS挑战者号，

sense_groups.english: both of which were converted vessels, fitted with a range of research facilities
sense_groups.chinese: 这两艘船都是改装船，配备了一系列研究设施，

sense_groups.english: to sample and measure across a range of disciplines in extreme environments.
sense_groups.chinese: 用于在极端环境中跨学科采样和测量。

sense_groups.english: Early research vessels were fairly basic and simplistic
sense_groups.chinese: 早期的研究船相当基础和简单，

sense_groups.english: compared to the state-of-the-art ships we see being developed today.
sense_groups.chinese: 与我们今天看到正在开发的尖端船舶相比。

sense_groups.english: Gradually, the trend of converting other vessels into research ships was challenged
sense_groups.chinese: 逐渐地，将其他船只改装成研究船的趋势受到了挑战，

sense_groups.english: by the challenging demands of investigating increasingly complex areas of oceanographic research,
sense_groups.chinese: 因为调查越来越复杂的海洋研究领域的要求具有挑战性，

sense_groups.english: such as physical, biological and chemical oceanography; marine geology and geophysics; ocean engineering and atmospheric science in one expedition.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如物理、生物和化学海洋学；海洋地质学和地球物理学；海洋工程和大气科学在一次考察中。

sense_groups.english: In order to carry out multi-disciplinary research in extreme environments,
sense_groups.chinese: 为了在极端环境中进行多学科研究，

sense_groups.english: specially designed research vessels became a requirement.
sense_groups.chinese: 专门设计的研究船成为必需。

sense_groups.english: Research ships are the primary source of oceanographic observations
sense_groups.chinese: 研究船是海洋观测的主要来源，

sense_groups.english: and will remain so for the foreseeable future.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且在可预见的未来仍将如此。

sense_groups.english: As time goes on, science is likely to be conducted in increasingly remote and environmentally challenging areas, including the polar seas,
sense_groups.chinese: 随着时间的推移，科学可能会在越来越偏远和环境挑战性大的地区进行，包括极地海域，

sense_groups.english: so the ability to operate with minimal interruptions from the natural elements remains unchanged from the days of the Challenger Expedition.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，从挑战者号探险时代起，在自然因素干扰最小的情况下运行的能力一直未变。

questions.name: #275 Modern Humans
questions.en:
Modern humans are masters of multitasking.
We eat while driving, watch TV while ______ , and of course talk on our cell phones while doing, well, ______ .
How do we do it?
A study in the July 16th issue of Neuron suggests that though we can train our brains to work faster as we juggle, we never ______ manage to do more than one thing at a time.
Our brains aren't really built to handle the sort of ______ processing we think we're capable of.
The good news is: studies have shown that extensive training can make us better at doing two things at once.
But how?
One theory is that with lots of ______ some routines become "automatic." And if we don't need to run every little thing past the part of the brain that spends time ______ about stuff, we can multitask just fine.
But this new study finds that that's not the way it works.
Turns out that multitaskers still consult the prefrontal cortex, but training gets the "Thinking Brain" to think a little faster.
So we're switching tasks quickly enough to appear to be doing them simultaneously.
Which is still nothing to shake a stick and sneeze at.
1. volleying , studying , couriering , lobbying
2. antonym , rpm , everything , sen
3. intramuscularly , incorrigibly , dispassionately , actually
4. smear , parallel , clientele , noel
5. disservice , practice , audits , comforts
6. dipping , gripping , deflecting , thinking
questions.answer:
1. studying
2. everything
3. actually
4. parallel
5. practice
6. thinking

sense_groups.english: Modern humans are masters of multitasking.
sense_groups.chinese: 现代人类是多任务处理的大师。

sense_groups.english: We eat while driving, watch TV while studying,
sense_groups.chinese: 我们边开车边吃东西，边看电视边学习，

sense_groups.english: and of course talk on our cell phones while doing, well, everything.

sense_groups.english: How do we do it?
sense_groups.chinese: 我们是怎么做到的呢？

sense_groups.english: A study in the July 16th issue of Neuron suggests that though we can train our brains to work faster as we juggle,
sense_groups.chinese: 《神经元》杂志7月16日刊的一项研究表明，尽管我们可以通过训练让大脑在同时处理多项任务时运转得更快，

sense_groups.english: The good news is: studies have shown that extensive training can make us better at doing two things at once.
sense_groups.chinese: 好消息是：研究表明，大量训练能让我们更擅长同时做两件事。

sense_groups.chinese: 但训练能让“思考的大脑”运转得更快一些。

questions.name: #276 Virus Mutation

However, the nation is still battling one of Africa's most severe ______ , with more than 46,000 people dead.

sense_groups.chinese: 随着人口增长，对清洁水的需求也增加了。

sense_groups.chinese: 试图通过管道在地下输送大量水是不可能的，因为铅管太脆弱，而青铜管太昂贵。

sense_groups.chinese: 山谷通过使用高架渠跨越。

sense_groups.chinese: 其中最著名的是法国南部尼姆的加尔桥高架渠。

sense_groups.chinese: 在可能的情况下，罗马人确实通过隧道引水，但这需要山丘相对较小才能成功。

sense_groups.chinese: 它由一个管理数千台风车和数十万客户的电网输送。

sense_groups.english: and provides a real time power balance.
sense_groups.chinese: 并提供实时的电力平衡。

sense_groups.english: Far more complex than anything in existence today,

sense_groups.english: This technology is a new frontier in power supply

sense_groups.english: and seen as a green solution to current outdated management systems.

sense_groups.english: When introduced smart grids will result in energy savings

sense_groups.english: and to be able to select the cheapest time slots.

sense_groups.english: and the power companies cannot experiment with existing supplies.

sense_groups.chinese: 而且它有效。

questions.name: #291 Food Minding
questions.en:
At supper Johnson talked of good eating with uncommon ______ .
"Some people," said he, "have a foolish way of not minding, or pretending not to mind, what they eat.
For my part, I mind my belly very ______ , and very carefully; for I look upon it, that he who does not mind his belly will hardly mind anything else," He was, for the moment, not only serious but ______ .
Yet I have heard him, upon other occasions, talk with great contempt of people who were anxious to gratify their palates; and the 206th number of his Rambler is a masterly essay against ______ .
His practice, indeed, I must acknowledge, may be considered as casting the balance of his different opinions upon this subject; for I never knew any man who ______ good eating more than he did.
1. superstition , convention , satisfaction , classification
2. excessively , hilariously , studiously , proportionally
3. challenging , depressed , obvious , vehement
4. gulosity , deity , fullness , degree
5. refreshed , disliked , relished , spoilt

sense_groups.english: At supper Johnson talked of good eating with uncommon satisfaction .
sense_groups.chinese: 晚餐时，约翰逊以非同寻常的满足感谈论美食。

sense_groups.english: "Some people," said he, "have a foolish way of not minding, or pretending not to mind, what they eat.

sense_groups.chinese: 因为我认为，不关心自己肚子的人几乎不会关心其他任何事情。”

sense_groups.english: His practice, indeed, I must acknowledge, may be considered as casting the balance of his different opinions upon this subject;

sense_groups.chinese: 因为我从未见过比他更享受美食的人。

questions.name: #292 Smoking Happiness
questions.en:
On March 18th, we told you that smoking doesn't make people happy.
Well, we hear you ask, what will make me happy?
What?
What?
Ok, first, relax.
Then, take out your wallet.
Because ______ to a study published in the March 21st issue of Science, giving money to other people is what brings us joy.
Scientists from Boston and British Columbia got to wondering whether money really can buy happiness.
They were ______ by the fact that over the past 20 or 30 years, people in the US and other developed countries have been making much more money—yet our happiness has pretty much ______ .
What they found is that money can buy happiness.
But only when you spend it on someone else.
In one experiment, the scientists asked volunteers to ______ their happiness.
Then they gave each subject some cash, either 5 or 20 dollars.
Half the ______ were told to spend the money on themselves.
The others were asked to give it away.
At the end of the day, the folks who got the biggest boost were the ones who spread the wealth, even if it was only five bucks.
So if you want to be happy, here's a big tip: always leave a big tip.

2. disentangled , adapted , charted , bothered

sense_groups.english: On March 18th, we told you that smoking doesn't make people happy.
sense_groups.chinese: 3月18日，我们告诉过你吸烟不会让人快乐。

sense_groups.english: Well, we hear you ask, what will make me happy?

sense_groups.english: What?
sense_groups.chinese: 什么？

sense_groups.english: What?
sense_groups.chinese: 什么？

sense_groups.english: Ok, first, relax.
sense_groups.chinese: 好，首先，放松。

sense_groups.english: Then, take out your wallet.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后，拿出你的钱包。

sense_groups.english: Because according to a study published in the March 21st issue of Science, giving money to other people is what brings us joy.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为根据3月21日《科学》杂志发表的一项研究，把钱给别人会给我们带来快乐。

sense_groups.english: Scientists from Boston and British Columbia got to wondering whether money really can buy happiness.
sense_groups.chinese: 来自波士顿和不列颠哥伦比亚的科学家开始思考金钱是否真的能买到幸福。

sense_groups.english: They were bothered by the fact that over the past 20 or 30 years, people in the US and other developed countries have been making much more money—yet our happiness has pretty much flatlined.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们被一个事实困扰：在过去二三十年里，美国和其他发达国家的人赚了更多钱，但我们的幸福感却几乎停滞不前。

sense_groups.english: What they found is that money can buy happiness.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现金钱确实能买到幸福。

sense_groups.chinese: 但只有当你把钱花在别人身上时才行。

sense_groups.english: In one experiment, the scientists asked volunteers to rate their happiness.
sense_groups.chinese: 在一项实验中，科学家让志愿者评估自己的幸福感。

sense_groups.english: Then they gave each subject some cash, either 5 or 20 dollars.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后他们给每个受试者一些现金，5美元或20美元。

sense_groups.english: Half the participants were told to spend the money on themselves.
sense_groups.chinese: 一半的参与者被告知把钱花在自己身上。

sense_groups.english: The others were asked to give it away.
sense_groups.chinese: 其他人被要求把钱送出去。

sense_groups.chinese: 一天结束时，幸福感提升最大的是那些分享财富的人，哪怕只有五美元。

sense_groups.english: So if you want to be happy, here's a big tip: always leave a big tip.
sense_groups.chinese: 所以如果你想快乐，这里有个重要建议：总是给大额小费。

questions.name: #294 FIB
questions.en:
The scientific ______ needs to be involved in promoting science education, ______ evolution.
So says the January issue of the FASEB Journal.
FASEB is the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology.
Sixteen other organizations also signed on to the recommendation, including the ______ Academy of Sciences and the American Institute of Physics.

Said journal editor Gerald, "The bottom line is that the world is round, humans evolved from an extinct species, and Elvis is dead.

sense_groups.chinese: 这项调查对任何支持基于证据而非猜测或希望来教授信息的人都是一个警钟；人们想听到真相，而且他们想从科学家那里听到真相。”

questions.name: #295 Poker Face
questions.en:
A good "poker face" can hide the quality of your cards.
But your arms might still be giving away your hands.
That's the finding of a study to come out in the journal Psychological Science.
Volunteers watched videos of the World Series of Poker.
The videos were edited so the subjects saw one of three different views of the players: the poker players' entire bodies from the table up, or just the players' faces or just the players' arms pushing chips into the pot.
"When ______ were ______ chips being pushed into the center of the table by the players, it was only then could they ______ perceive how good a hand was better than chance.
They couldn't do it for the whole body and if ______ they were worse from just watching the face." Michael Slepian, a psychology doctoral student at Stanford ______ , and a co-author of the study.
No pros were among the video watchers.
But there's some ______ that, as might be expected, they'd be even better at ______ arm cues.
"In one of our studies, the more participants were familiar with poker—even though they were all novices—the better they did."
1. sycophants , redevelopments , participants , steadfastness
2. watching , twirling , backing , researching
3. accurately , botanically , rancorously , demonology
4. hen , anything , violin , min
5. Hardily , University , Dichotomy , Snobbery
6. evidence , processionals , tepidness , experiments
7. catching , conversing , distracting , awning
questions.answer:
1. participants
2. watching
3. accurately
4. anything
5. University
6. evidence
7. catching

questions.name: #296 Desert Ants
questions.en:
There comes a time in a desert ant's life when a piece of food is too large to ignore, but too heavy to lift, and the only way to get it home is to adopt a new style of walking.
The long-legged and speedy Cataglyphis fortis normally covers ground with a three-legged stride that moves two legs forwards on one side, and one on the other.
For the next step, the insect mirrors the move with ______ other three legs.
But recordings of ants in the Tunisian desert reveal that when faced with oversized lumps of food 10 times their own weight, the forward 'tripod' walking style is ______ .
Unable to lift the morsels in their mandibles, the ants drag the food backwards instead, moving all six legs independently.
'This is the first time we ______ ______ this in any ants,' said lead author Sarah Pfeffer at the University of Ulm in Germany.
The ants' long legs already help keep their bodies away from the ______ desert floor and enable them to speed around at up to 60 cm per second.
The researchers, who publish the findings on ant locomotion and navigation in the Journal of Experimental Biology, believe that robotics will be one of the first technologies ______ ______ from the discovery.
1. its , own , that , their
2. abandons , abandon , abandoning , abandoned
3. saw , seen , having seen , have seen
4. emotional , stuck , uncensored , scorching
5. benefited , to benefit , benefit , benefits
questions.answer:
1. its
2. abandoned
3. have
4. seen
5. scorching
6. to
7. benefit

questions.name: #299 Civil War
questions.en:
A Civil War reenactment is in part a memorial service.
It is partly, too, a leisure activity.
Furthermore most reenactors assert an educational import to the performance, and to develop their roles many pursue archival research with a rare dedication.
On the other hand Civil War reenactments are increasingly commercial spectacles , with as many as fifty thousand Americans
routinely gathering at (or near) historical Civil War battlefields in order to stage performances that purport to recreate the conflict, while hundreds of thousands more spectate (Hadden 1996:5).
I will show how theoretical issues of authenticity arise as practical problems in the Civil War reenactment community by presenting my own observations from the 2006 Gettysburg reenactment and by relying on a number of texts produced by participant-observers.
In particular I will refer to Robert Lee Hodge, who was made famous by Tony Horwitz's 1996 book, Confederates in the Attic, and who served as a kind of Virgil to the author on his journey through a Confederate Valhalla.
From these sources I will argue that 'Living History' performances require an interpretive apparatus that takes genuine history as its authority, while remaining external to both participants and tourists, who may well be unaware of how closely their own involvement approximates genuine historical events.
1. points , costs , spectacles , areas
2. velocity , authenticity , ability , intensity
3. exercising , researching , building , relying
4. depose , deny , argue , suggest

sense_groups.chinese: 虽然电极对于将灯泡直接插入照明系统无疑很方便，

questions.name: #312 Father's Role
questions.en:
The father's role in society has changed during the last 20 years, with a trend towards acceptance of a nurturant father who is more involved in child care responsibilities.
With the birth of a child, father-child issues may ______ from the family in which the father was born and raised.
The healthy, ______ father is able to put these issues in perspective and resolve them.

While fathers contribute to their own psychosocial development, they also have an important impact on their children from infancy ______ adulthood.

Infants can ______ fathers from other adults early.
1. resurface , restrict , restore , resuscitate
2. adjusted , mistrusted , entrusted , maladjusted
3. increment , abatement , resentment , alignment
4. through , besides , above , over
5. forgive , distinguish , forget , respect
questions.full:
The father's role in society has changed during the last 20 years, with a trend towards acceptance of a nurturant father who is more involved in child care responsibilities.
With the birth of a child, father-child issues may ______ from the family in which the father was born and raised.

Infants can ______ fathers from other adults early.

3. increment , abatement , resentment , alignment

sense_groups.chinese: 父亲在社会中的角色在过去20年里发生了变化，

sense_groups.chinese: 趋势是接受养育型父亲，

sense_groups.english: who is more involved in child care responsibilities.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们更多地参与育儿责任。

sense_groups.english: With the birth of a child, father-child issues may resurface from the family
sense_groups.chinese: 随着孩子的出生，父子问题可能从家庭中重新浮现，

sense_groups.english: in which the father was born and raised.
sense_groups.chinese: 父亲出生和成长的家庭。

sense_groups.english: The healthy, adjusted father is able to put these issues in perspective
sense_groups.chinese: 健康、适应良好的父亲能够正确看待这些问题，

sense_groups.english: and resolve them.
sense_groups.chinese: 并解决它们。

sense_groups.english: does not spill into the immediate family.

sense_groups.chinese: 他们也对孩子从婴儿期到成年期产生重要影响。

sense_groups.chinese: 其婴儿在一岁时认知发展更好，

questions.name: #313 Road to Success
questions.en:
It is well that young men should begin at the beginning and occupy the most subordinate positions.
Many of the leading businessmen of Pittsburgh had a serious responsibility thrust upon them at the very ______ of their career.
They were introduced to the broom, and spent the first hours of their business lives sweeping out the office.
I notice we have janitors now in offices, and our young men unfortunately miss that ______ branch of business education.
But if by chance the professional sweeper is ______ any morning, the boy who has the ______ of the future partner in him will not hesitate to try his hand at the broom.
It does not hurt the newest comer to sweep out the office if necessary.
I was one of those sweepers myself.
1. limitation , terminal , threshold , midpoint
2. voluntary , sanitary , sedentary , salutary
3. assent , consent , absent , present
4. genius , radius , eyesight , faith

Many of the leading businessmen of Pittsburgh had a serious responsibility thrust upon them at the very ______ of their career.

It does not hurt the newest comer to sweep out the office if necessary.
I was one of those sweepers myself.

sense_groups.english: It is well that young men should begin at the beginning and occupy the most subordinate positions.
sense_groups.chinese: 年轻人从基层做起，担任最卑微的职位，这是件好事。

sense_groups.chinese: 匹兹堡的许多商界领袖在职业生涯之初就被赋予了重大的责任。

sense_groups.chinese: 我注意到现在办公室有清洁工，不幸的是，我们的年轻人错过了那有益的商业教育环节。

sense_groups.english: But if by chance the professional sweeper is absent any morning, the boy who has the genius of the future partner in him will not hesitate to try his hand at the broom.
sense_groups.chinese: 但如果某天早上清洁工碰巧缺席，那个具有未来合伙人天赋的男孩会毫不犹豫地拿起扫帚试试。

sense_groups.english: It does not hurt the newest comer to sweep out the office if necessary.

sense_groups.chinese: 我自己也曾是那些扫地者之一。

questions.name: #314 Love of Beauty

The love of beauty is an essential part of all healthy human nature.

It waves in the branches of trees and the green blades of grass.
It ______ from the hues of the shell and the precious stone.

1. quality , quantity , qualification , qualifier
2. absence , presence , contrary , opposite
3. attained , entertained , detained , sustained
4. gleams , screams , streams , steams
5. overflow , overfeed , overfly , overfill

sense_groups.chinese: 它是一种道德品质。

sense_groups.chinese: 缺乏它并非必然的谴责理由，但拥有它则是心灵善良的不变标志。

sense_groups.chinese: 感受到它的程度很可能与品格的高贵和美丽达到的程度成正比。

sense_groups.english: The universe is its temple.

sense_groups.chinese: 它在树枝和绿叶中摇曳。

sense_groups.chinese: 不仅这些微小物体，还有海洋、山脉、云彩、星辰、日出和日落——全都洋溢着美。

questions.name: #315 Work and Pleasure
questions.en:
To be really happy and really safe, one ______ to have at least two or three hobbies, and they must all be real.
It is no use starting late in life to say: "I will take an interest in this or that." Such an attempt only ______ the strain of mental effort.
A man may ______ great knowledge of topics unconnected with his daily work, and yet hardly get any benefit or relief.

2. alleviates , aggravates , aggregates , agglomerates
3. acquire , deny , lack , know
4. Kindly , Grandly , Sadly , Broadly

To be really happy and really safe, one ______ to have at least two or three hobbies, and they must all be real.

sense_groups.english: To be really happy and really safe,

sense_groups.chinese: 一个人应该至少有两三个爱好，

sense_groups.chinese: 而且它们都必须是真正的爱好。

sense_groups.english: It is no use starting late in life to say:

sense_groups.chinese: 那些劳累至死的人，

sense_groups.english: those who are worried to death,
sense_groups.chinese: 那些忧虑至死的人，

sense_groups.chinese: 和那些无聊至死的人。

questions.name: #316 Olympics
questions.en:
The Olympics ______ the noble ideal of sports overcoming the ______ of politics with champion athletes of all nations gathering in the spirit of sportsmanship.

Shortly after each competition, nations begin to vie afresh for the bid to host the next game.

It also spins revenue from the ______ of tourists, participants and Olympic related paraphernalia.

The capital is expecting to pour billions of dollars into sports facilities and related upgrades ______ ______ roads, public transport, landscaping and sanitation.
For the bustling city of bicycles and traffic jams tucked among imperial relics, the Olympics is an opportunity for urban renewal.

2. jam , benefits , barriers , connection
3. efflux , afflux , reflux , influx
4. flutters , loiters , glitters , jitters
5. by far , as for , such as , in favor of
questions.answer:
1. represents
2. barriers
3. influx
4. glitters
5. such
6. as

The Olympics ______ the noble ideal of sports overcoming the ______ of politics with champion athletes of all nations gathering in the spirit of sportsmanship.

sense_groups.english: to warn ships of icebergs in the North Atlantic.
sense_groups.chinese: 以警告船只北大西洋的冰山。

sense_groups.english: The International Ice Patrol uses airplanes and radars

questions.name: #320 Patent
questions.en:

questions.name: #321 Odorous House Ant
questions.en:
A common response to seeing an ant inside your house is to stomp on it.
But if you crush a member of the ant species Tapinoma sessile, you might catch a whiff of a strange smell—a smell that reminds some people of blue cheese, rancid butter or rotten coconut.
In fact, the smell is so noticeable that the insect's common name is the "odorous house ant." And many people call it the coconut ant.
In an effort to figure out why people have these reactions, ______ enlisted ______ at an event called the North Carolina BugFest.
One-hundred-forty-three volunteers smelled smushed ants and were asked to identify the scent from four choices: blue cheese, rancid butter, rotten coconut or just other.
Although Web sites overwhelmingly call the smell rotten coconut, almost 40 percent of the human judges picked blue cheese and about 25 percent picked rotten coconut.
More than 30 percent went with the choice of other.
The scientists then analyzed the chemicals ______ for the ant odor, as well as the smelly chemicals in blue cheese, fresh coconut and coconut buried underground for three days.
It turns out that the chemistry of the ants' scent is indeed similar to that of blue cheese and rotten coconut.
But not to fresh coconut.
And the researchers note that the Penicillium ______ that turn coconut oil rancid are also ______ in the production of blue cheese.
The study is in the journal American Entomologist.
The researchers also noted that the most common write-in candidate as a description for the ants' aroma was "cleaning spray." And one little girl told them that the ants "smelled exactly like her doctor."

questions.name: #322 Christmas Cards
questions.en:
A few years ago, a university professor tried a little experiment.
He sent Christmas cards to a sample of perfect strangers.
Although he expected some reaction, the ______ he received was amazing — holiday cards ______ to him came pouring back from the people who had never met nor heard of him.
The great majority of those who returned a card never inquired ______ the identity of the unknown professor.
They received his holiday greeting card, and they automatically sent one in return.
This study shows the action of one of the most powerful of the weapons of influence around us — the rule for ______ .
The rule says that we should try to repay, in kind, what another person has provided us.
If a woman does us a favor, we should do her one in return; if a man sends us a birthday present, we should remember his birthday with a gift of our own; if a couple invites us to a party, we should be sure to invite them to one of ours.

questions.en:

Lubricants.
Enzymes for breaking down food.

And using just that data, they found that they could estimate the ages of their saliva contributors to within five years.
This technique might help in crime scene ______ —recovered saliva could tell the age of a perpetrator.
So if you're worried about anyone knowing how old you are, be careful where you spit.
1. groping , guffawing , consoling , according
2. affirmation , purification , mortification , methylation
3. priestesses , weaknesses , inveiglers , researchers
4. instantiated , hatred , correlated , undomesticated

6. foreshortened , strongest , pronest , noticed
7. dispensations , investigations , phrases , celebrations

2. methylation

sense_groups.english: Saliva contains many useful components.
sense_groups.chinese: 唾液含有许多有用的成分。

sense_groups.english: Lubricants.
sense_groups.chinese: 润滑剂。

sense_groups.chinese: 分解食物的酶。

sense_groups.chinese: 而现在，还有能揭示一个人年龄的化合物。

sense_groups.english: That's according to a study in the journal Public Library of Science ONE.
sense_groups.chinese: 这是根据《公共科学图书馆·综合》期刊上的一项研究得出的。

sense_groups.chinese: 在正常发育过程中，你体内的DNA会发生所谓的甲基化。

questions.name: #330 Preface
questions.en:
Science is a dominant theme in our culture.
Since it touches almost every facet of our life, educated people need at least some ______ with its structure and operation.

The book can be used to ______ a course in any science, to accompany any course that attempts to give an understanding of the modern world, or independently of any course — simply to provide a better understanding of science.
We hope this book will lead readers to a broader perspective on scientific attitudes and a more ______ view of what science is, who scientists are, and what they do.

questions.name: #331 Catholics
questions.en:
Catholics venerate the saints and look to them as examples of lives well lived in the faith.
Many find comfort in the ______ that holy people shared in their same struggles, sins, doubts, or hardships and ask specific saints to pray for them.
Some saints are the patrons of certain occupations or causes, and these saints are often invoked to aid people in those professions or situations.
For example, St. Judas (Jude) is the patron saint of impossible or ______ causes, and many Catholics ask him to pray on their behalf for the ______ of seemingly impossible situations in their lives.
Additionally, many Catholics take or are given a saint's name for their confirmation.
A confirmation saint is often seen as having an invested interest in ______ a new Catholic's spiritual growth and is usually chosen because his or her life story ______ with the neophyte.
Most saints have feast days observed by the Catholic Church in which their lives and contributions are formally celebrated, and some have large followings of devotees and even religious orders in their honor.
1. relief , knowledge , disappointment , illusion
2. complacent , insidious , desperate , satisfactory
3. devolution , resolution , convolution , absolution
4. fostering , forgiving , forging , foreseeing
5. abominates , culminates , hallucinates , resonates
questions.full:
Catholics venerate the saints and look to them as examples of lives well lived in the faith.
Many find comfort in the ______ that holy people shared in their same struggles, sins, doubts, or hardships and ask specific saints to pray for them.

sense_groups.english: Catholics venerate the saints and look to them as examples of lives well lived in the faith.
sense_groups.chinese: 天主教徒敬仰圣徒，将他们视为信仰中美好生活的榜样。

sense_groups.english: Many find comfort in the knowledge that holy people shared in their same struggles, sins, doubts, or hardships and ask specific saints to pray for them.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多人因知道圣人们也曾经历同样的挣扎、罪恶、怀疑或苦难而感到安慰，并请特定的圣徒为他们祈祷。

sense_groups.english: Some saints are the patrons of certain occupations or causes, and these saints are often invoked to aid people in those professions or situations.
sense_groups.chinese: 一些圣徒是特定职业或事业的守护者，人们常祈求这些圣徒帮助从事那些职业或处于那些处境的人。

sense_groups.english: For example, St. Judas (Jude) is the patron saint of impossible or desperate causes, and many Catholics ask him to pray on their behalf for the resolution of seemingly impossible situations in their lives.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，圣犹达是无望或绝望事业的守护圣徒，许多天主教徒请他代祷，以求解决生活中看似无望的困境。

sense_groups.english: Additionally, many Catholics take or are given a saint's name for their confirmation.
sense_groups.chinese: 此外，许多天主教徒在坚振礼上选择或被赐予一位圣徒的名字。

sense_groups.english: A confirmation saint is often seen as having an invested interest in fostering a new Catholic's spiritual growth and is usually chosen because his or her life story resonates with the neophyte.
sense_groups.chinese: 坚振圣徒常被视为对新天主教徒的灵性成长有特别的兴趣，通常因其生平故事与新信徒产生共鸣而被选中。

sense_groups.english: Most saints have feast days observed by the Catholic Church in which their lives and contributions are formally celebrated, and some have large followings of devotees and even religious orders in their honor.
sense_groups.chinese: 大多数圣徒都有天主教会的瞻礼日，正式庆祝他们的生平和贡献，有些圣徒拥有大量追随者，甚至以他们命名的修会。

questions.en:

On the new moon, a female coconut crab ______ larvae (which she's been carrying around in her abdomen since they were just fertilized eggs) into the ocean, and the babies ______ around in the currents for a month or so before dropping to the seafloor and finding nice, cozy snail shells to move into.
Just like your childhood hermit crab friend, young coconut crabs move in and out of shells as they ______ up and get used to living on land.
Sometimes a juvenile coconut crab will use a coconut husk or empty sea shell as ______ until its own shell gets harder.
After about a year, the teens of the species eventually find there are no shells left on the beach large enough to ______ their bulk, so they move out altogether.
From here on out, they live the rest of their lives out of the water — coconut crabs will drown if totally submerged.

2. bloat , afloat , float , gloat
3. follow , bulk , brush , sum
