sense_groups.english: Coconut crabs spend most of their lives on land, but they start out in the ocean.
sense_groups.chinese: 椰子蟹一生大部分时间在陆地上，但它们最初是在海洋中开始的。

sense_groups.english: On the new moon, a female coconut crab deposits larvae (which she's been carrying around in her abdomen since they were just fertilized eggs) into the ocean,
sense_groups.chinese: 在新月时，雌性椰子蟹将幼虫（从受精卵开始就一直携带在腹部）释放到海洋中，

sense_groups.chinese: 幼体在海流中漂浮大约一个月，然后沉到海底，找到舒适的小蜗牛壳住进去。

sense_groups.english: Just like your childhood hermit crab friend, young coconut crabs move in and out of shells as they bulk up and get used to living on land.
sense_groups.chinese: 就像你小时候的寄居蟹朋友一样，年轻的椰子蟹随着体型增大并适应陆地生活，会不断更换外壳。

sense_groups.english: Sometimes a juvenile coconut crab will use a coconut husk or empty sea shell as armor until its own shell gets harder.
sense_groups.chinese: 有时，幼年椰子蟹会使用椰子壳或空海螺壳作为盔甲，直到自己的外壳变硬。

sense_groups.english: After about a year, the teens of the species eventually find there are no shells left on the beach large enough to accommodate their bulk, so they move out altogether.
sense_groups.chinese: 大约一年后，这种生物的青少年最终发现海滩上没有足够大的壳来容纳它们庞大的身躯，于是它们完全搬离了。

sense_groups.english: From here on out, they live the rest of their lives out of the water — coconut crabs will drown if totally submerged.
sense_groups.chinese: 从此以后，它们一生都生活在水中之外——椰子蟹如果完全浸没在水中会淹死。

questions.name: #333 Rainbow
questions.en:
A rainbow is most often viewed as a circular arc in the sky.
An observer on the ground observes a half-circle of color with red being the color ______ on the outside or top of the bow.
Those who are fortunate enough to have seen a rainbow from an airplane in the sky may know that a rainbow can ______ be a complete circle.
Observers on the ground only view the top half of the circle since the bottom half of the circular arc is prevented by the presence of the ground.
Yet observers in an airborne plane can often look both upward and downward to view the complete circular bow.
The circle results because there are a ______ of suspended droplets in the atmosphere that are capable of concentrating the dispersed light at angles of ______ of 40-42 degrees relative to the original path of light from the sun.
These droplets actually form a circular arc, with each droplet within the arc ______ light and reflecting it back towards the observer.
1. deceived , conceived , believed , perceived
2. mutually , annually , actually , intellectually
3. conception , connection , competition , collection
4. illuviation , abbreviation , aviation , deviation
5. pervading , submersing , traversing , dispersing

sense_groups.english: A rainbow is most often viewed as a circular arc in the sky.
sense_groups.chinese: 彩虹通常被视为天空中的一道圆弧。

sense_groups.chinese: 地面上的观察者看到半圆形的色彩，红色被感知为彩虹的外侧或顶部。

sense_groups.english: Those who are fortunate enough to have seen a rainbow from an airplane in the sky may know that a rainbow can actually be a complete circle.
sense_groups.chinese: 那些有幸从飞机上看到彩虹的人可能知道，彩虹实际上可以是一个完整的圆。

sense_groups.english: Observers on the ground only view the top half of the circle since the bottom half of the circular arc is prevented by the presence of the ground.
sense_groups.chinese: 地面上的观察者只能看到圆的上半部分，因为圆弧的下半部分被地面遮挡了。

sense_groups.english: Yet observers in an airborne plane can often look both upward and downward to view the complete circular bow.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，在空中的飞机上的观察者可以同时向上和向下看，看到完整的圆形彩虹。

sense_groups.chinese: 这个圆之所以形成，是因为大气中有一组悬浮的水滴，它们能够将分散的光汇聚到相对于太阳原始光路偏离40-42度的角度上。

sense_groups.english: These droplets actually form a circular arc, with each droplet within the arc dispersing light and reflecting it back towards the observer.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些水滴实际上形成了一个圆弧，弧内的每个水滴都分散光线并将其反射回观察者。

questions.name: #334 Oliver Smithies
questions.en:
Oliver Smithies won the Nobel Prize in ______ or Medicine in 2007.
On June 27th, he spoke to students about what he learned from his thesis ______ , which ______ developing a new method to measure the osmotic pressures of mixes of proteins:

And I was rather proud of this method.
And I ______ it with great delight.
This paper has a record, you know: nobody ever quoted it.
And nobody ever used the method again.
And I didn't use the method again.
So I have to ask you, what was the point of it all?
Well, the answer is really a very serious answer.
The answer is I learned to do good science.
But it didn't matter what I did when I was learning to do good science.
So it doesn't matter what you do when you're doing a thesis, you see.
But it's very important that you enjoy it.
Because if you don't enjoy it, you won't do a good job and you won't learn science.
So all of this comes around to the fact that if you don't enjoy what you're doing, ask your advisors to let you do something else.
And if your advisor won't do that, there's another ______ : change your advisor."

2. shad , sherd , research , watt
3. involved , mad , evolved , allot
4. experiment , magnificent , measurement , belligerent
5. cohabit , disulphide , annexed , published
6. solution , brougham , futon , union

2. research
3. involved
4. measurement
5. published

questions.name: #340 Animal Dialect
questions.en:
We humans are social ______ —we stick together.
Family traditionally came first.
Then more distant relatives.
Then larger groups of unrelated individuals, connected by culture.
But it turns out the same could be said for sperm whales.
"So usually you find the female, and their mom and the grandmas and their aunts, and they all stay together for many years."
Maurício Cantor, a biologist at Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia.
He says those closely related family groups then seek out other families with similar behavior: "They tend to hang out or stay together with those who produce the same kinds of sounds." Meaning whale cliques are based on ______ similar clicks.
And similarly clicking whales don't just hang out together, he says.
They also emulate each other's songs, or codas.
Meaning clans of whales evolve their own ______ —their own form of culture.

sense_groups.english: The researchers analyzed 247 books written for children 5 years old and younger from the Wisconsin Children's Book Corpus.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员分析了来自威斯康星儿童图书语料库的247本为5岁及以下儿童编写的书籍。

sense_groups.english: The books with female protagonists had more gendered language than the books with male protagonists.
sense_groups.chinese: 有女性主角的书籍比有男性主角的书籍包含更多性别化语言。

sense_groups.english: The researchers attribute this finding to "male" being historically seen as the default gender.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员将这一发现归因于“男性”在历史上被视为默认性别。

sense_groups.english: Female-coded words and phrases are more outside of the norm and more notable.
sense_groups.chinese: 女性编码的词汇和短语更偏离常规，也更引人注目。

sense_groups.chinese: 具体来说，研究人员考察了女性与善良、家庭、语言和艺术相关联的频率，而男性则与邪恶、职业和数学相关联。

questions.en:

That means ______ to renewable sources of energy — and, importantly, decarbonizing transportation, a sector that is now responsible for about a quarter of the world's carbon dioxide emissions.
But the path to that cleaner future is ______ , clogged with political and societal roadblocks, as well as scientific ______ .
Perhaps that's one reason why the electric vehicle — already on the road, already navigating many of these roadblocks — swerved so dramatically into the climate solutions spotlight in 2021.
Just a few years ago, many automakers thought electric vehicles (EVs) might be a passing ______ , says Gil Tal, director of the Plug-in Hybrid & Electric Vehicle Research Center at the University of California.
1. grafting , drafting , crafting , shifting
2. daunting , daunted , daunt , dauntless
3. spectacles , obstacles , tentacles , receptacles
4. fad , gad , tad , lad

sense_groups.english: Just a few years ago, many automakers thought electric vehicles (EVs) might be a passing fad,

questions.en:
With omicron spreading globally at a dizzying pace, scientists are scrambling to learn as much as they can about the latest worrisome variant of the coronavirus.
First ______ in South Africa and Botswana at the end of November, omicron is already ______ to soon become the dominant variant — dethroning delta — in some regions, public health officials warn.
In a few places, it already has.
So answers, including how sick does omicron make people and how well do vaccines ______ it, can't come fast enough.

And with many people preparing to gather with family and friends for holidays, experts are ______ for yet more case surges, compounded by already high infection rates in some countries linked to the still-prevalent delta variant.
Omicron's collision with the holidays and travel is "a perfect storm".

questions.name: #353 Coral's Genetic Diversity
questions.en:
Using a combination of scuba gear and remotely operated vehicles, marine biologists in California ______ more than 1,400 corals from the ocean surface.
The samples looked identical, and their internal structures were indistinguishable in scanning electron microscope images.
Yet, their genomes — their full genetic ______ books — revealed the corals had diverged millions of years ago.
That made sense for one of the species in the Red Sea's Gulf of Aqaba, which was geographically separated from the others.
But the other three newly ______ species lived together on the same reefs in the waters off South Asia.
If the corals were living together, why didn't one overtake the other two, the team wondered.
Examining habitat data from their dives, the researchers found the three distinct coral species ______ different water depths, with one abundant in the top 10 meters and the other two flourishing deeper down.
The three coral species also had different concentrations of photosynthetic algae and pigments, suggesting they had distinct strategies for hosting their algae partners that provide food.
1. sampled , stapled , rumpled , tripled
2. destruction , construction , obstruction , instruction
3. identified , certified , fortified , gratified
4. endeavored , savored , despised , favored
questions.full:
Using a combination of scuba gear and remotely operated vehicles, marine biologists in California ______ more than 1,400 corals from the ocean surface.
The samples looked identical, and their internal structures were indistinguishable in scanning electron microscope images.

sense_groups.english: Using a combination of scuba gear and remotely operated vehicles, marine biologists in California sampled more than 1,400 corals from the ocean surface.
sense_groups.chinese: 使用水肺装备和遥控潜水器的组合，加利福尼亚的海洋生物学家从海洋表面采集了超过1400个珊瑚样本。

sense_groups.english: The samples looked identical, and their internal structures were indistinguishable in scanning electron microscope images.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些样本看起来一模一样，在扫描电子显微镜图像中它们的内部结构也无法区分。

sense_groups.english: Yet, their genomes — their full genetic instruction books — revealed the corals had diverged millions of years ago.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，它们的基因组——完整的遗传指令手册——揭示了这些珊瑚在数百万年前就已经分化。

sense_groups.english: That made sense for one of the species in the Red Sea's Gulf of Aqaba, which was geographically separated from the others.
sense_groups.chinese: 这对于红海亚喀巴湾的一个物种来说是有道理的，该物种在地理上与其他物种分离。

sense_groups.english: But the other three newly identified species lived together on the same reefs in the waters off South Asia.
sense_groups.chinese: 但其他三个新鉴定的物种共同生活在南亚海域的同一珊瑚礁上。

sense_groups.english: If the corals were living together, why didn't one overtake the other two, the team wondered.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果这些珊瑚生活在一起，为什么没有一个物种超越其他两个？研究团队感到疑惑。

sense_groups.english: Examining habitat data from their dives, the researchers found the three distinct coral species favored different water depths, with one abundant in the top 10 meters and the other two flourishing deeper down.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过检查潜水时的栖息地数据，研究人员发现这三个不同的珊瑚物种偏爱不同的水深，其中一个在表层10米内丰富，另外两个在更深的水域繁茂。

sense_groups.english: The three coral species also had different concentrations of photosynthetic algae and pigments, suggesting they had distinct strategies for hosting their algae partners that provide food.
sense_groups.chinese: 这三个珊瑚物种还含有不同浓度的光合藻类和色素，表明它们有独特的策略来容纳提供食物的藻类伙伴。

questions.name: #354 Robot Fish
questions.en:
Invasive mosquito fish are often fearless.
Free from the predators of their native range, these mosquito fish run ______ , throwing naive ecosystems from Europe to Australia out of whack.
To keep the problematic fish in check, scientists are trying to ______ fear back into the hearts of these swimmers with a high-tech tool: robots.
In a laboratory experiment, a robotic fish designed to ______ one of mosquito fish’s natural predators increased fear and stress responses in mosquito fish, impairing their survival and reproduction, researchers report December 16 in iScience.
While robofish won't be deployed in the wild anytime soon, the research highlights that there are more creative ways of preventing ______ behavior from a species than simply killing them, says Michael Culshaw-Maurer, an ecologist at the University of Arizona in Tucson who wasn't involved in the study.
"It’s just wonderful seeing work in this area."
1. occupant , flippant , rampant , concordant
2. accept , spike , strike , drake
3. bequest , mimic , battle , conquest
4. unprivileged , unprecedented , uncharted , unwanted

sense_groups.english: Invasive mosquito fish are often fearless.
sense_groups.chinese: 入侵的食蚊鱼通常无所畏惧。

sense_groups.english: Free from the predators of their native range,
sense_groups.chinese: 由于没有原生地的天敌，

sense_groups.english: these mosquito fish run rampant,
sense_groups.chinese: 这些食蚊鱼泛滥成灾，

sense_groups.english: throwing naive ecosystems from Europe to Australia out of whack.
sense_groups.chinese: 从欧洲到澳大利亚，脆弱的生态系统被搅得天翻地覆。

sense_groups.english: To keep the problematic fish in check,
sense_groups.chinese: 为了控制这些麻烦的鱼，

sense_groups.english: scientists are trying to strike fear back into the hearts of these swimmers
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们正试图用高科技工具——机器人——重新唤起这些游泳者的恐惧。

sense_groups.english: with a high-tech tool: robots.
sense_groups.chinese: 这个工具就是机器人。

sense_groups.english: In a laboratory experiment,
sense_groups.chinese: 在一项实验室实验中，

sense_groups.english: a robotic fish designed to mimic one of mosquito fish’s natural predators
sense_groups.chinese: 一种设计用来模仿食蚊鱼天敌的机器鱼，

sense_groups.english: increased fear and stress responses in mosquito fish,
sense_groups.chinese: 增加了食蚊鱼的恐惧和应激反应，

sense_groups.english: impairing their survival and reproduction,
sense_groups.chinese: 损害了它们的生存和繁殖能力，

sense_groups.english: researchers report December 16 in iScience.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员在12月16日的《iScience》上报告。

sense_groups.english: While robofish won't be deployed in the wild anytime soon,
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然机器鱼不会很快在野外部署，

sense_groups.english: the research highlights that there are more creative ways of preventing unwanted behavior from a species
sense_groups.chinese: 但这项研究强调，有比简单杀死它们更创造性的方法来防止物种的不良行为，

sense_groups.english: than simply killing them,
sense_groups.chinese: 而不是简单地杀死它们，

sense_groups.english: says Michael Culshaw-Maurer, an ecologist at the University of Arizona in Tucson who wasn't involved in the study.
sense_groups.chinese: 图森亚利桑那大学的生态学家迈克尔·卡尔肖-毛雷尔说，他没有参与这项研究。

sense_groups.english: "It’s just wonderful seeing work in this area."
sense_groups.chinese: “看到这个领域的工作真是太棒了。”

questions.name: #355 Atomic Nuclei
questions.en:
Atomic nuclei come in a dizzying number of varieties.
Scientists have discovered 118 chemical elements, ______ by the number of protons in their nuclei.
Each of those elements has a variety of isotopes, different versions of the element formed by switching up the number of neutrons inside the nucleus.
Scientists have predicted the ______ of about 8,000 isotopes of known elements, but only about 3,300 have made an appearance in detectors.
Researchers expect FRIB will make a ______ dent in the missing isotopes.
It may identify 80 percent of possible isotopes for all the elements up through uranium, including many never seen before.
The most familiar nuclei are those of the roughly 250 isotopes that are stable: they don't ______ to other types of atoms.
The ranks of stable isotopes include the nitrogen-14 and oxygen-16 in the air we breathe and the carbon-12 found in all known living things.
The number following the element's name ______ the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
1. anguished , vanquished , languished , distinguished
2. existence , persistence , nonexistence , consistence
3. sizable , quotable , portable , sociable
4. decay , stray , array , foray
5. indicates , had indicated , indicating , indication

Atomic nuclei come in a dizzying number of varieties.

2. existence

sense_groups.english: Atomic nuclei come in a dizzying number of varieties.
sense_groups.chinese: 原子核的种类多得令人眼花缭乱。

sense_groups.english: Scientists have discovered 118 chemical elements, distinguished by the number of protons in their nuclei.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家已经发现了118种化学元素，它们通过原子核中的质子数量来区分。

sense_groups.english: Each of those elements has a variety of isotopes, different versions of the element formed by switching up the number of neutrons inside the nucleus.
sense_groups.chinese: 每种元素都有多种同位素，这些同位素是通过改变原子核内中子数量形成的不同版本。

sense_groups.english: Scientists have predicted the existence of about 8,000 isotopes of known elements, but only about 3,300 have made an appearance in detectors.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家预测已知元素大约有8000种同位素存在，但只有约3300种在探测器中出现过。

sense_groups.english: Researchers expect FRIB will make a sizable dent in the missing isotopes.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员预计FRIB将大幅减少缺失的同位素数量。

sense_groups.english: It may identify 80 percent of possible isotopes for all the elements up through uranium, including many never seen before.
sense_groups.chinese: 它可能识别出直到铀的所有元素中80%的可能同位素，包括许多前所未见的。

sense_groups.english: The most familiar nuclei are those of the roughly 250 isotopes that are stable: they don't decay to other types of atoms.
sense_groups.chinese: 最熟悉的原子核是大约250种稳定同位素的原子核：它们不会衰变成其他类型的原子。

sense_groups.english: The ranks of stable isotopes include the nitrogen-14 and oxygen-16 in the air we breathe and the carbon-12 found in all known living things.
sense_groups.chinese: 稳定同位素包括我们呼吸空气中的氮-14和氧-16，以及所有已知生物中发现的碳-12。

sense_groups.english: The number following the element's name indicates the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
sense_groups.chinese: 元素名称后面的数字表示原子核中质子和中子的总数。

questions.name: #356 Ryukyu Islands
questions.en:
Long ago, ancient mariners successfully navigated a perilous ocean journey to arrive at Japan's Ryukyu Islands, a new study suggests.
Archaeological sites on six of these isles — part of a 1,200-kilometer-long chain — indicate that migrations to the islands ______ 35,000 to 30,000 years ago, both from the south via Taiwan and from the north via the Japanese island of Kyushu.
But whether ancient humans navigated there on purpose or ______ there by accident on the Kuroshio ocean current, one of the world's largest and strongest currents, is unclear.
The answer to that question could ______ light on the proficiency of these Stone Age humans as mariners and their mental capabilities overall.
Now, satellite-tracked buoys that ______ a wayward raft suggest that there's little chance that the seafarers reached the isles by accident.
1. incurred , concurred , spurred , occurred
2. drifted , airlifted , sifted , shifted
3. drop , shed , place , embrace
4. insulated , simulated , stimulated , regulated

sense_groups.english: Archaeological sites on six of these isles — part of a 1,200-kilometer-long chain — indicate that migrations to the islands occurred 35,000 to 30,000 years ago, both from the south via Taiwan and from the north via the Japanese island of Kyushu.

sense_groups.english: But whether ancient humans navigated there on purpose or drifted there by accident on the Kuroshio ocean current, one of the world's largest and strongest currents, is unclear.

sense_groups.english: The answer to that question could shed light on the proficiency of these Stone Age humans as mariners and their mental capabilities overall.

sense_groups.english: Now, satellite-tracked buoys that simulated a wayward raft suggest that there's little chance that the seafarers reached the isles by accident.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，模拟了漂流筏的卫星追踪浮标表明，这些航海者意外到达这些岛屿的可能性很小。

questions.name: #357 Rationing
questions.en:
Rationing may be of several types.
Informal rationing, which precedes the imposition of formal controls, may consist of admonitions to consumers to reduce their ______ or of independent action taken by suppliers in allocating scarce supplies.
Rationing according to use prohibits the less important uses of a commodity.
Rationing by quantity may limit the hours during ______ the commodity is available or may assign quotas of a commodity to all known and approved claimants.
Rationing by value limits the amount consumers may spend on commodities that cannot be ______ , consumers being allowed to make their own selections within the value limits imposed.
Point rationing assigns a point value to each commodity and allocates a certain number of points to each consumer; this system is employed during periods of critical and increasing shortages when individuals begin ______ unrationed for rationed items, thereby spreading shortages.
Consumers in a rationed economy are usually ______ to save by purchasing government bonds or by increasing their deposits in savings banks so that unspent money will not be used for increased purchases of unrationed items or for purchases on the black market.
1. presumption , consumption , assumption , subscription
2. what , which , where , when
3. standardized , propagandized , jeopardized , subsidized
4. instituting , persecuting , substituting , constituting
5. retorted , deported , exhorted , distorted
questions.full:
Rationing may be of several types.

3. standardized , propagandized , jeopardized , subsidized

1. consumption
2. which
3. standardized
4. substituting
5. exhorted

sense_groups.english: Rationing may be of several types.
sense_groups.chinese: 配给可能有几种类型。

sense_groups.english: Informal rationing, which precedes the imposition of formal controls,
sense_groups.chinese: 非正式配给，在实施正式控制之前，

sense_groups.english: may consist of admonitions to consumers to reduce their consumption
sense_groups.chinese: 可能包括劝告消费者减少他们的消费

sense_groups.english: or of independent action taken by suppliers in allocating scarce supplies.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者供应商在分配稀缺物资时采取的独立行动。

sense_groups.english: Rationing according to use prohibits the less important uses of a commodity.
sense_groups.chinese: 按用途配给禁止商品的不太重要的用途。

sense_groups.english: Rationing by quantity may limit the hours during which the commodity is available
sense_groups.chinese: 按数量配给可能限制商品可用的时间

sense_groups.english: or may assign quotas of a commodity to all known and approved claimants.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者将商品的配额分配给所有已知和批准的申请者。

sense_groups.english: Rationing by value limits the amount consumers may spend on commodities that cannot be standardized,
sense_groups.chinese: 按价值配给限制消费者在无法标准化的商品上的花费金额，

sense_groups.english: consumers being allowed to make their own selections within the value limits imposed.
sense_groups.chinese: 允许消费者在规定的价值限制内自行选择。

sense_groups.english: Point rationing assigns a point value to each commodity and allocates a certain number of points to each consumer;
sense_groups.chinese: 积分配给为每种商品分配一个积分值，并为每个消费者分配一定数量的积分；

sense_groups.english: this system is employed during periods of critical and increasing shortages
sense_groups.chinese: 该系统在严重且日益短缺的时期使用，

sense_groups.english: when individuals begin substituting unrationed for rationed items,
sense_groups.chinese: 当个人开始用非配给品替代配给品时，

sense_groups.english: thereby spreading shortages.
sense_groups.chinese: 从而加剧短缺。

sense_groups.english: Consumers in a rationed economy are usually exhorted to save

sense_groups.chinese: 通过购买政府债券或增加他们在储蓄银行的存款

sense_groups.english: so that unspent money will not be used for increased purchases of unrationed items

sense_groups.english: or for purchases on the black market.
sense_groups.chinese: 或用于黑市购买。

questions.name: #358 Naming Storms
questions.en:
The practice of giving storms personal names appears to have ______ with Clement Wragge, an Australian meteorologist who in the 1890s entertained himself by naming storms after women, mythical ______ , and politicians that he didn't like.
The modern system of using personal names developed during World War II, when meteorologists began using women's names — often those of wives or girlfriends — instead of ______ designations based on latitude and longitude.
Short and quickly understood, names were easier to ______ over the radio and easier to keep straight if there was more than one storm in a given area.
The system was ______ in 1953 when the National Weather Service put together an alphabetical list of female names to be used for storms in the Atlantic basin.
Male names were added to the list in 1979 when women's groups pointed out the sexism of using only female names.
1. originated , laminated , contaminated , vaccinated
2. figures , figuration , figurative , configures
3. worrisome , cumbersome , awesome , wholesome
4. transmit , transform , transfuse , transect
5. rationalized , decentralized , formalized , immortalized

sense_groups.english: The practice of giving storms personal names appears to have originated with Clement Wragge,
sense_groups.chinese: 给风暴取人名的做法似乎起源于克莱门特·拉格，

sense_groups.english: an Australian meteorologist who in the 1890s entertained himself by naming storms after women, mythical figures, and politicians that he didn't like.
sense_groups.chinese: 一位澳大利亚气象学家，他在19世纪90年代以用他不喜欢的女性、神话人物和政治家的名字来命名风暴自娱自乐。

sense_groups.english: The modern system of using personal names developed during World War II,
sense_groups.chinese: 现代使用人名的系统是在第二次世界大战期间发展起来的，

sense_groups.english: when meteorologists began using women's names — often those of wives or girlfriends — instead of cumbersome designations based on latitude and longitude.
sense_groups.chinese: 当时气象学家开始使用女性的名字——通常是妻子或女友的名字——而不是基于经纬度的繁琐名称。

sense_groups.english: Short and quickly understood, names were easier to transmit over the radio
sense_groups.chinese: 名字简短易懂，更容易通过无线电传输

sense_groups.english: and easier to keep straight if there was more than one storm in a given area.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且在某个区域有多个风暴时更容易区分清楚。

sense_groups.english: The system was formalized in 1953
sense_groups.chinese: 该系统于1953年正式确立，

sense_groups.english: when the National Weather Service put together an alphabetical list of female names to be used for storms in the Atlantic basin.
sense_groups.chinese: 当时美国国家气象局整理了一份按字母顺序排列的女性名字列表，用于大西洋盆地的风暴。

sense_groups.english: Male names were added to the list in 1979
sense_groups.chinese: 1979年，男性名字被添加到列表中，

sense_groups.english: when women's groups pointed out the sexism of using only female names.
sense_groups.chinese: 当时女性团体指出只使用女性名字是性别歧视。

questions.name: #360 Social Ties
questions.en:
Many types of scientific evidence show that involvement in social relationships benefits health.
The most striking evidence comes from prospective studies of mortality ______ industrialized nations.
These studies ______ show that individuals with the lowest level of involvement in social relationships are more likely to die than those with greater involvement.
The risk of death among men and women with the fewest social ties was more than twice as high as the risk for adults with the most social ties.
Social ties also reduce ______ risk among adults with documented medical conditions.
Among adults with coronary artery disease, the socially isolated had a risk of subsequent cardiac death 2.4 times greater than their more socially connected ______ .
In addition to mortality, involvement in social relationships has been associated with specific health conditions as well as biological markers indicating risk of preclinical conditions.
Several recent review articles provide consistent and ______ evidence linking a low quantity or quality of social ties with a host of conditions.
1. off , beneath , on , across
2. impotently , consistently , competently , inadvertently
3. mentality , mortality , morality , mutuality
4. sneers , peers , careers , pioneers
5. dispelling , compelling , propelling , impelling

sense_groups.english: Many types of scientific evidence show that involvement in social relationships benefits health.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多科学证据表明，参与社会关系有益健康。

sense_groups.english: The most striking evidence comes from prospective studies of mortality across industrialized nations.
sense_groups.chinese: 最显著的证据来自对工业化国家死亡率的纵向研究。

sense_groups.english: These studies consistently show that individuals with the lowest level of involvement in social relationships are more likely to die than those with greater involvement.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些研究一致表明，社会关系参与度最低的人比参与度更高的人更有可能死亡。

sense_groups.english: The risk of death among men and women with the fewest social ties was more than twice as high as the risk for adults with the most social ties.
sense_groups.chinese: 社会关系最少的男性和女性的死亡风险是拥有最多社会关系的成年人的两倍以上。

sense_groups.english: Social ties also reduce mortality risk among adults with documented medical conditions.
sense_groups.chinese: 社会关系也降低了患有已知疾病的成年人的死亡风险。

sense_groups.english: Among adults with coronary artery disease, the socially isolated had a risk of subsequent cardiac death 2.4 times greater than their more socially connected peers.
sense_groups.chinese: 在患有冠状动脉疾病的成年人中，社交孤立者后续心脏死亡的风险是社交联系更紧密的同龄人的2.4倍。

sense_groups.english: In addition to mortality, involvement in social relationships has been associated with specific health conditions as well as biological markers indicating risk of preclinical conditions.
sense_groups.chinese: 除了死亡率，社会关系参与还与特定健康状况以及指示临床前疾病风险的生物标志物有关。

sense_groups.english: Several recent review articles provide consistent and compelling evidence linking a low quantity or quality of social ties with a host of conditions.
sense_groups.chinese: 最近的几篇综述文章提供了一致且令人信服的证据，将社会关系的数量或质量低下与多种疾病联系起来。

questions.name: #361 Idea of Beauty
questions.en:
When we are very concerned about certain of our physical ______ — a nose that is stubbornly a bit too large, eyes that are slightly too far apart, hair that is not as lustrous as it should be — we miss an overall point about our relationship to our appearance: how beautiful we feel has nothing to do with the ______ structure of our face or body.

There are people of ideal ______ and exceptional beauty who cannot bear what they see in the mirror and others who can contemplate a less than svelte stomach or a no longer so supple kind of skin with indifference and defiant good humor.
And at a tragic ______ , there are heart-breakingly fine-looking people who starve themselves to ill-health.

2. reflective , objective , conjunctive , subjective
3. called in , based on , ruled out , summed up
4. distortions , apportions , proportions , abortions
5. humanity , extreme , feeling , supreme

3. based
4. on
5. proportions

sense_groups.chinese: 从最早的文明开始，植物和动物就被描绘成理解和记录其潜在用途（如经济和药用价值）的一种方式。

sense_groups.english: From the first illustrated catalogue of medicinal plants, De Materia Medica by Dioscorides, in the first century through to the late fourteenth century the illustration of plants and animals changed very little.
sense_groups.chinese: 从公元一世纪迪奥斯科里德斯的《药物学》——第一部带插图的药用植物目录——到十四世纪末，植物和动物的插图几乎没有变化。

sense_groups.english: Woodcuts in instructional manuals and herbals were often repeatedly copied over the centuries, resulting in a loss of definition and accuracy so that they became little more than stylized decoration.
sense_groups.chinese: 几个世纪以来，教学手册和草药书中的木刻版画经常被反复复制，导致清晰度和准确性下降，最终它们几乎变成了程式化的装饰。

sense_groups.english: With the growing popularity of copperplate engravings, the traditional use of woodcuts declined and the representation of plants and animals became more accurate.
sense_groups.chinese: 随着铜版画越来越受欢迎，木刻版画的传统用途逐渐减少，植物和动物的描绘也变得更加准确。

sense_groups.english: Then, with the emergence of artists such as Albrecht Durer and Leonardo Da Vinci, naturalists such as Otto Brunfels, Leonhard Fuchs in botany and Conrad Gesner and Ulisse Aldrovandi in zoology, nature began to be depicted in a more realistic style.
sense_groups.chinese: 随后，随着阿尔布雷希特·丢勒和列奥纳多·达·芬奇等艺术家，以及植物学领域的奥托·布伦费尔斯、莱昂哈德·福克斯，动物学领域的康拉德·格斯纳和乌利塞·阿尔德罗万迪等博物学家的出现，自然开始以更写实的风格被描绘。

sense_groups.english: Individual living plants or animals were observed directly and their likeness rendered onto paper or vellum.
sense_groups.chinese: 个体活体植物或动物被直接观察，它们的形象被绘制在纸或羊皮纸上。

questions.name: #365 Why Students Forget
questions.en:
Teachers have long known that rote memorization can lead to a ______ grasp of material that is quickly forgotten.
But new research in the field of neuroscience is starting to ______ light on the ways that brains are wired to forget — highlighting the importance of strategies to retain knowledge and make learning stick.
In a recent article published in the journal Neuron, neurobiologists Blake Richards and Paul Frankland challenge the ______ view of memory, which holds that forgetting is a process of loss — the gradual washing away of critical information ______ our best efforts to retain it.
According to Richards and Frankland, the goal of memory is not just to store information accurately but to ‘optimize decision-making’ in chaotic, quickly changing environments.
In this model of cognition, forgetting is an evolutionary strategy, a ______ process that runs in the background of memory, evaluating and discarding information that doesn’t promote the survival of the species.
1. similar , comprehensive , solid , superficial
2. flow , stream , charge , shed
3. prevented , prehistoric , predominant , presidential
4. through , despite , yet , provided
5. purposeful , grateful , distrustful , thoughtful

questions.name: #366 Body Energy
questions.en:
If you've ever had to pick up and carry a tired child through the mall, you know that walking sometimes tuckers out the ______ .
Now scientists think they know why.
The results appear in the Journal of Experimental Biology.
Larger animals tend to use less energy per gram of body ______ than smaller ones do, even at rest.

Researchers ______ walkers of different ages and sizes, from a three-foot-tall kindergartner to a six-foot adult.

If you scaled a five-year-old up to be six-and-a-half feet tall, the giant child would lope along just like a similarly sized adult.
What's more, walkers of all heights use the same amount of energy per step.

sense_groups.english: If you've ever had to pick up and carry a tired child through the mall,

sense_groups.chinese: 你就知道走路有时会让小孩子筋疲力尽。

sense_groups.english: Now scientists think they know why.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在科学家们认为他们知道原因了。

sense_groups.chinese: 研究结果发表在《实验生物学杂志》上。

sense_groups.chinese: 科学家测量了他们的步幅和新陈代谢。

sense_groups.chinese: 他们只是需要更少的步数就能走完同样的距离。

questions.name: #368 Yellowstone Bison

questions.name: #379 Bird Food
questions.en:
If you've ever been to an all-you-can-eat buffet, you know how ______ it is to ______ weigh your options.
You don't want to fill up on salad when so many ______ delights await.
It seems some birds also weigh their mealtime choices—literally.
A study finds that Mexican Jays pick up and shake peanuts to assess their relative heft before choosing one.
That report is served up in the Journal of Ornithology.
Foods that hide their edible bits on the inside present a challenge to hungry diners.
How can you tell which fruits are ripe or which shells harbor the biggest nuts?
We humans knock on melons or squeeze avocados.
But how do other species select the highest quality snacks?
To find out how the jays do it, researchers fiddled with their feed.
First they doctored peanuts so that some contained three nuts while others had none.
When they offered these pods to some jays, the birds turned their beaks up at the empty shells and instead chose those that were full.
And when the jays were allowed to choose between normal peanuts and those that weighed just one gram more, because the researchers had stuffed them with clay, the birds again went for the heavier meal.
Videos ______ that the jays shake the nuts before ______ one, which apparently lets them gauge the nut's mass and perhaps also listen for the rattle of a well-packed shell.
Pretty clever for a bird brain.

4. doodling , tattooing , choosing , juicing
5. retrieved , conceit , bulletined , revealed
6. criticising , bringing , selecting , belching

sense_groups.chinese: 其中一些谎言很大（“我从未欺骗过你！”），但更常见的是，它们是用来______尴尬情况或照顾他人感受的小善意谎言（“那条裙子看起来不错”）。

sense_groups.english: Trust is the bedrock of social life at all levels, from romance and parenting to national government.
sense_groups.chinese: 信任是所有层面社会生活的基石，从恋爱、育儿到国家政府。

sense_groups.english: Deception always ______ it.
sense_groups.chinese: 欺骗总是______它。

sense_groups.english: Because truth is so essential to the human enterprise, which relies on a shared view of reality, the default assumption most people have is that others are truthful in their communications and dealings.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为真相对于依赖共享现实观的人类事业至关重要，大多数人默认假设他人在沟通和交往中是诚实的。

sense_groups.english: Most cultures have powerful social ______ against lying.
sense_groups.chinese: 大多数文化都有强大的社会______来反对说谎。

questions.name: #382 Micromanaging
questions.en:
Leaders need to avoid micromanaging and stay ______ to what is happening in order to spot a change in context.
By and large, line workers in a simple situation are more than capable of independently handling any issues that may ______ .
Indeed, those with years of experience also have deep ______ into how the work should be done.
Leaders should create a communication channel — an anonymous one, if necessary — that allows dissenters to provide early warnings about complacency.
It's important to remember that best practice is, by definition, past practice.
Using best practices is common, and often ______ , in simple contexts.
Difficulties arise, however, if staff members are ______ from bucking the process even when it's not working anymore.
Since hindsight no longer leads to foresight after a shift in context, a corresponding change in management style may be called for.
1. complied , connected , precise , concise
2. apprise , rise , encounter , arise
3. incursion , insight , indignity , indication
4. inappropriate , apprehensive , appropriate , forbidden
5. disarranged , disinclined , discouraged , disintegrated
questions.full:
Leaders need to avoid micromanaging and stay ______ to what is happening in order to spot a change in context.
By and large, line workers in a simple situation are more than capable of independently handling any issues that may ______ .
Indeed, those with years of experience also have deep ______ into how the work should be done.
Leaders should create a communication channel — an anonymous one, if necessary — that allows dissenters to provide early warnings about complacency.
It's important to remember that best practice is, by definition, past practice.
Using best practices is common, and often ______ , in simple contexts.
Difficulties arise, however, if staff members are ______ from bucking the process even when it's not working anymore.
Since hindsight no longer leads to foresight after a shift in context, a corresponding change in management style may be called for.

1. complied , connected , precise , concise
2. apprise , rise , encounter , arise
3. incursion , insight , indignity , indication
4. inappropriate , apprehensive , appropriate , forbidden
5. disarranged , disinclined , discouraged , disintegrated

答案:
1. connected
2. arise
3. insight
4. appropriate
5. discouraged

sense_groups.english: Leaders need to avoid micromanaging and stay connected to what is happening
sense_groups.chinese: 领导者需要避免微观管理，并与正在发生的事情保持联系

sense_groups.english: in order to spot a change in context.
sense_groups.chinese: 以便发现环境的变化。

sense_groups.english: By and large, line workers in a simple situation are more than capable of independently handling any issues that may arise.
sense_groups.chinese: 总的来说，在简单情境下，一线员工完全有能力独立处理任何可能出现的问题。

sense_groups.english: Indeed, those with years of experience also have deep insight into how the work should be done.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，那些有多年经验的人也对工作应该如何完成有深刻的见解。

sense_groups.english: Leaders should create a communication channel — an anonymous one, if necessary — that allows dissenters to provide early warnings about complacency.
sense_groups.chinese: 领导者应该建立一个沟通渠道——必要时可以是匿名的——让持不同意见者能够对自满情绪提供早期预警。

sense_groups.english: It's important to remember that best practice is, by definition, past practice.
sense_groups.chinese: 重要的是要记住，最佳实践从定义上讲是过去的实践。

sense_groups.english: Using best practices is common, and often appropriate, in simple contexts.
sense_groups.chinese: 在简单情境中，使用最佳实践很常见，而且通常是合适的。

sense_groups.english: Difficulties arise, however, if staff members are discouraged from bucking the process even when it's not working anymore.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，如果员工被劝阻不要违背流程，即使流程不再有效，困难就会出现。

sense_groups.english: Since hindsight no longer leads to foresight after a shift in context, a corresponding change in management style may be called for.
sense_groups.chinese: 由于环境变化后，后见之明不再能带来先见之明，可能需要进行相应的管理风格改变。

questions.name: #383 Bears
questions.en:
Among the biggest threats to all species of bears is habitat loss, especially from logging, agriculture, and growing human populations.

3. protected , prohibited , fattened , threatened
4. poached , squelched , coached , blenched
5. begot , foreseen , encountered , targeted
questions.full:
Among the biggest threats to all species of bears is habitat loss, especially from logging, agriculture, and growing human populations.

sense_groups.english: Among the biggest threats to all species of bears is habitat loss, especially from logging, agriculture, and growing human populations.
sense_groups.chinese: 对所有熊类来说，最大的威胁之一是栖息地丧失，尤其是来自伐木、农业和不断增长的人口。

sense_groups.english: Habitat loss reduces the amount of area bears have to hunt and means they're increasingly coming into contact with humans, which can lead to human-wildlife conflict.
sense_groups.chinese: 栖息地丧失减少了熊的狩猎面积，并意味着它们越来越多地与人类接触，这可能导致人与野生动物的冲突。

sense_groups.english: Bears are killed out of concern for human safety or in retaliation for hunting livestock or crop-raiding.
sense_groups.chinese: 熊被杀死是出于对人类安全的担忧，或是对它们捕食牲畜或破坏庄稼的报复。

sense_groups.english: Some species of bears, including Asiatic black bears and sun bears, are also threatened by the illegal wildlife trade.
sense_groups.chinese: 一些熊类，包括亚洲黑熊和马来熊，也受到非法野生动物贸易的威胁。

sense_groups.english: Bear bile, which is produced in the gall bladder, is an important ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine.
sense_groups.chinese: 熊胆，由胆囊产生，是中药中的重要成分。

sense_groups.english: Asiatic black bears and sun bears may be poached for their gall bladders, paws, skins, and other parts.
sense_groups.chinese: 亚洲黑熊和马来熊可能因它们的胆囊、熊掌、皮毛和其他部位而被偷猎。

sense_groups.english: Sometimes American black bears are also targeted for the same reasons.
sense_groups.chinese: 有时美洲黑熊也因同样的原因成为目标。

sense_groups.english: Climate change is also a significant threat, especially to polar bears.
sense_groups.chinese: 气候变化也是一个重大威胁，尤其是对北极熊。

sense_groups.english: They depend on finding seals on sea ice for their meals, and they’ll often pass the summer months without eating while they wait for ice to solidify.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们依赖在海冰上寻找海豹作为食物，并且常常在等待冰层凝固的整个夏季不进食。

questions.name: #384 Starvation
questions.en:
Over weeks and months, malnutrition can result in specific diseases, like anemia when people don't get enough iron or beriberi if they don't get adequate thiamine.
A ______ lack of food for a prolonged period — not enough calories of any sort to keep up with the body's energy needs — is starvation.

Metabolism slows; the body cannot regulate its temperature; kidney function is impaired and the immune system ______ .
When the body uses its reserves to provide basic energy needs, it can no longer supply necessary nutrients to vital organs and tissues.
The heart, lungs, ovaries and testes shrink.
Muscles shrink and people feel weak.
Body temperature drops and people can feel chilled.

sense_groups.english: Over weeks and months, malnutrition can result in specific diseases, like anemia when people don't get enough iron or beriberi if they don't get adequate thiamine.
sense_groups.chinese: 数周或数月内，营养不良可能导致特定疾病，如缺铁性贫血或缺乏硫胺素引起的脚气病。

sense_groups.english: A severe lack of food for a prolonged period — not enough calories of any sort to keep up with the body's energy needs — is starvation.
sense_groups.chinese: 长期严重缺乏食物——任何种类的热量都不足以满足身体能量需求——就是饥饿。

sense_groups.english: The body's reserve resources are depleted.
sense_groups.chinese: 身体的储备资源被耗尽。

sense_groups.english: The result is substantial weight loss, wasting away of the body's tissues and eventually death.
sense_groups.chinese: 结果是体重显著下降、身体组织萎缩，最终死亡。

sense_groups.english: When faced with starvation, the body fights back.
sense_groups.chinese: 面对饥饿，身体会反击。

sense_groups.english: The first day without food is a lot like the overnight fast between dinner one night and breakfast the next morning.
sense_groups.chinese: 没有食物的第一天很像前一晚晚餐到第二天早餐之间的夜间禁食。

sense_groups.english: Energy levels are low but pick up with a morning meal.
sense_groups.chinese: 能量水平很低，但早餐后会恢复。

sense_groups.english: Within days, faced with nothing to eat, the body begins feeding on itself.
sense_groups.chinese: 几天内，面对没有食物，身体开始自我消耗。

sense_groups.english: Metabolism slows; the body cannot regulate its temperature; kidney function is impaired and the immune system weakens.
sense_groups.chinese: 新陈代谢减慢；身体无法调节体温；肾功能受损，免疫系统减弱。

sense_groups.english: When the body uses its reserves to provide basic energy needs, it can no longer supply necessary nutrients to vital organs and tissues.
sense_groups.chinese: 当身体利用储备提供基本能量需求时，它无法再向重要器官和组织提供必要营养。

sense_groups.english: The heart, lungs, ovaries and testes shrink.
sense_groups.chinese: 心脏、肺、卵巢和睾丸萎缩。

sense_groups.english: Muscles shrink and people feel weak.
sense_groups.chinese: 肌肉萎缩，人感到虚弱。

sense_groups.english: Body temperature drops and people can feel chilled.
sense_groups.chinese: 体温下降，人会感到寒冷。

sense_groups.english: People can become irritable, and they become difficult to concentrate.
sense_groups.chinese: 人会变得易怒，难以集中注意力。

questions.name: #386 Product Selling
questions.en:
Once an organization has its product to sell, it must then determine the appropriate price to sell it at.
The price is set by ______ many factors including supply-and-demand, cost, desired profit competition, perceived value, and market behavior.
Ultimately, the final price is ______ by what the market is willing to ______ for the product.
Pricing theory can be quite complex because so many factors influence what the purchaser decides is a fair ______ .
It also should be ______ that, in addition to monetary exchange, price can be the exchange of goods or services as in a barter agreement, or an exchange of specific behavior, such as a vote in a political campaign.
1. tolerate , determine , fabricate , fancy
2. comparing , begetting , balancing , offsetting
3. consign , design , exchange , prepare
4. addition , shape , content , value
5. explained , enlarged , overrated , noted
questions.full:
Once an organization has its product to sell, it must then determine the appropriate price to sell it at.
The price is set by ______ many factors including supply-and-demand, cost, desired profit competition, perceived value, and market behavior.
Ultimately, the final price is ______ by what the market is willing to ______ for the product.
Pricing theory can be quite complex because so many factors influence what the purchaser decides is a fair ______ .
It also should be ______ that, in addition to monetary exchange, price can be the exchange of goods or services as in a barter agreement, or an exchange of specific behavior, such as a vote in a political campaign.

1. tolerate , determine , fabricate , fancy
2. comparing , begetting , balancing , offsetting
3. consign , design , exchange , prepare
4. addition , shape , content , value
5. explained , enlarged , overrated , noted

答案:
1. balancing
2. determined
3. exchange
4. value
5. noted

sense_groups.english: Once an organization has its product to sell,
sense_groups.chinese: 一旦一个组织有了要销售的产品，

sense_groups.english: it must then determine the appropriate price to sell it at.
sense_groups.chinese: 它就必须确定一个合适的销售价格。

sense_groups.english: The price is set by balancing many factors
sense_groups.chinese: 价格是通过平衡许多因素来确定的，

sense_groups.english: including supply-and-demand, cost, desired profit, competition, perceived value, and market behavior.
sense_groups.chinese: 包括供需、成本、期望利润、竞争、感知价值和市场行为。

sense_groups.english: Ultimately, the final price is determined by what the market is willing to exchange for the product.
sense_groups.chinese: 最终，最终价格是由市场愿意为产品交换什么来决定的。

sense_groups.english: Pricing theory can be quite complex
sense_groups.chinese: 定价理论可能相当复杂，

sense_groups.english: because so many factors influence what the purchaser decides is a fair value.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为有很多因素影响购买者认为什么是公平的价值。

sense_groups.english: It also should be noted that,
sense_groups.chinese: 还应该注意的是，

sense_groups.english: in addition to monetary exchange,
sense_groups.chinese: 除了货币交换之外，

sense_groups.english: price can be the exchange of goods or services as in a barter agreement,
sense_groups.chinese: 价格可以是商品或服务的交换，如在易货协议中，

sense_groups.english: or an exchange of specific behavior, such as a vote in a political campaign.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者是特定行为的交换，例如政治竞选中的投票。

questions.name: #388 Shrimp Farm
questions.en:
Over the past two decades around a third of the world’s mangrove swamps have been converted for human use, with many turned into valuable shrimp farms.
In 2007 an economic study of such shrimp farms in Thailand showed that the commercial profits per hectare were $9,632.
If that were the only ______ , conversion would seem an excellent idea.
However, proper ______ shows that for each hectare government subsidies formed $8,412 of this figure and there were costs, too: $1,000 for pollution and $12,392 for losses to ecosystem services.
These ______ damage to the supply of foods and medicines that people had taken from the forest, the loss of habitats for fish, and less buffering against storms.
And because a given shrimp farm only stays ______ for three or four years, there was the additional cost of restoring them afterwards: if you do so with mangroves themselves, add another $9,318 per hectare.
The overall lesson is that what looks ______ only does so because the profits are retained by the private sector, while the problems are spread out across society at large, appearing on no specific balance sheet.
1. rearranged , exchanged , conserved , converted
2. index , element , choice , factor
3. accounting , percentage , aggregation , division
4. comprised , uneven , neglected , augmented
5. productive , interactive , distinctive , collective
6. beneficial , immediate , moderate , modest
questions.full:
Over the past two decades around a third of the world’s mangrove swamps have been converted for human use, with many turned into valuable shrimp farms.
In 2007 an economic study of such shrimp farms in Thailand showed that the commercial profits per hectare were $9,632.

2. index , element , choice , factor
3. accounting , percentage , aggregation , division
4. comprised , uneven , neglected , augmented

2. accounting
3. comprised
4. productive

sense_groups.english: Over the past two decades around a third of the world’s mangrove swamps have been converted for human use,
sense_groups.chinese: 在过去的二十年里，全球约三分之一的红树林沼泽已被转为人类用途，

sense_groups.english: with many turned into valuable shrimp farms.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中许多被改造成了有价值的养虾场。

sense_groups.english: In 2007 an economic study of such shrimp farms in Thailand showed that the commercial profits per hectare were $9,632.
sense_groups.chinese: 2007年一项针对泰国此类养虾场的经济研究表明，每公顷的商业利润为9632美元。

sense_groups.english: If that were the only factor, conversion would seem an excellent idea.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果这是唯一的因素，那么转化似乎是个好主意。

sense_groups.english: However, proper accounting shows that for each hectare government subsidies formed $8,412 of this figure
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，适当的核算显示，每公顷中政府补贴占了8412美元，

sense_groups.english: and there were costs, too: $1,000 for pollution and $12,392 for losses to ecosystem services.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且还有成本：污染成本1000美元，生态系统服务损失12392美元。

sense_groups.english: These comprised damage to the supply of foods and medicines that people had taken from the forest,
sense_groups.chinese: 这些包括人们从森林中获取的食物和药品供应受损，

sense_groups.english: the loss of habitats for fish, and less buffering against storms.
sense_groups.chinese: 鱼类栖息地的丧失，以及抵御风暴能力的减弱。

sense_groups.english: And because a given shrimp farm only stays productive for three or four years,
sense_groups.chinese: 而且由于一个特定的养虾场只能维持三到四年的生产力，

sense_groups.english: there was the additional cost of restoring them afterwards:
sense_groups.chinese: 之后还有额外的恢复成本：

sense_groups.english: if you do so with mangroves themselves, add another $9,318 per hectare.

questions.name: #391 Ocean
questions.en:
Earth's surface is dominated by oceans.
But where did all that water come from?
  ______ and comets smashing into the early Earth have long been thought to be a promising source.
But measurements of Halley's Comet and five others threw cold water on the idea that comets ______ a large share of the oceans.
Because the chemical ______ of the comets did not match the oceans.

But now astronomers have gotten a glimpse of a comet with a different origin, and it matches the oceans much better.
They used the Herschel space telescope to examine Comet Hartley 2, which originated in the Kuiper Belt.
Halley and its ilk came from a distant swarm of comets called the Oort Cloud.
At a ______ science meeting last week in France, and in a study in Nature, the ______ ______ that Comet Hartley 2 has the same deuterium-to-hydrogen ratio as ocean water.

Something to ponder next time you have a day at the beach.

6. teacupfuls , cheeseburgers , sheepherders , researchers

sense_groups.english: Earth's surface is dominated by oceans.

questions.name: #396 Active Brain
questions.en:
Keeping the brain active and engaged appears to combat the cognitive decline associated with getting older.
Now a study has found a new, but related, factor in maintaining a sharp mind—the space in which we live.
Researchers recruited almost 1,300 senior citizens, none of whom showed any signs of clinical dementia at the start of the study.
The participants had their cognitive function tested annually for up to eight years.
And they also described their living space.
For example, maybe they mostly hung around their bedroom.
Perhaps they spent time in the yard.
Or frequently traveled.
By the end of the study, 180 people had Alzheimers.
And those whose ______ narrowed in on their immediate home were almost twice as likely to develop the ______ as those who ventured out.
The homebound folks also had an ______ risk of other cognitive impairments and a faster rate of cognitive decline.
The research was published in the American Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry.
The study's lead investigator, Bryan James of the Rush University Medical Center in Chicago, ______ that, "Perhaps life space is an indicator of how much we are ______ engaging and challenging our cognitive ______ ."
1. plagues , life-space , trails , manes
2. distension , condition , kitten , imperfection
3. repeat , screech , increased , elite
4. suggests , consents , questionnaires , neath
5. actively , gymnastically , candidly , underhandedly
6. antipathies , densities , abilities , affinities
questions.answer:
1. life-space
2. condition
3. increased
4. suggests
5. actively
6. abilities

sense_groups.english: Keeping the brain active and engaged appears to combat the cognitive decline associated with getting older.
sense_groups.chinese: 保持大脑活跃和投入似乎可以对抗与年龄增长相关的认知衰退。

sense_groups.english: Now a study has found a new, but related, factor in maintaining a sharp mind—the space in which we live.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在一项研究发现了一个新的但相关的因素，可以保持思维敏捷——我们生活的空间。

sense_groups.english: Researchers recruited almost 1,300 senior citizens, none of whom showed any signs of clinical dementia at the start of the study.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员招募了近1300名老年人，在研究开始时，他们都没有表现出任何临床痴呆的迹象。

sense_groups.english: The participants had their cognitive function tested annually for up to eight years.
sense_groups.chinese: 参与者的认知功能每年接受测试，持续长达八年。

sense_groups.english: And they also described their living space.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们还描述了自己的生活空间。

sense_groups.english: For example, maybe they mostly hung around their bedroom.

sense_groups.english: The homebound folks also had an increased risk of other cognitive impairments and a faster rate of cognitive decline.

sense_groups.english: The research was published in the American Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《美国老年精神病学杂志》上。

sense_groups.english: The study's lead investigator, Bryan James of the Rush University Medical Center in Chicago, suggests that, "Perhaps life space is an indicator of how much we are actively engaging and challenging our cognitive abilities."
sense_groups.chinese: 该研究的主要研究者、芝加哥拉什大学医学中心的布莱恩·詹姆斯建议说：“也许生活空间是我们积极投入和挑战认知能力的一个指标。”

questions.name: #397 Flowers and Bees
questions.en:
Most people assume, correctly, that flowers look the way they do to attract insects that pollinate them.
But that’s not the whole story.
Scientists have now discovered that plants have another ‘trick up their leaves’ to make themselves irresistible to even the most choosy insect.
Cambridge University’s Beverley Glover and her colleagues recently set up some fake flowers filled with a sugar solution, which they kept at different temperatures.
Unleashing a team of bumblebees on their floral ______ , they watched as the insects visited the flowers to drink the surrogate nectar.
Very quickly, it became obvious that the bees were concentrating on the flowers with the warmest nectar.
Just in case it was something to ______ with the color of the fake flowers, the scientists also tried a different color ______ and got the same result.
1. irresistible , expensive , explicit , false
2. friends , counterparts , researchers , colleagues
3. contours , shapes , organisms , offerings
4. make , do , have , go
5. consequence , tone , combination , appearance

sense_groups.english: Most people assume, correctly, that flowers look the way they do to attract insects that pollinate them.

sense_groups.chinese: 但这并不是全部。

sense_groups.english: Cambridge University’s Beverley Glover and her colleagues recently set up some fake flowers filled with a sugar solution, which they kept at different temperatures.
sense_groups.chinese: 剑桥大学的贝弗利·格洛弗和她的同事们最近设置了一些假花，里面装有糖溶液，并保持在不同温度。

sense_groups.english: Unleashing a team of bumblebees on their floral offerings, they watched as the insects visited the flowers to drink the surrogate nectar.

sense_groups.chinese: 很快，很明显，蜜蜂们集中在那些花蜜最温暖的花朵上。

sense_groups.english: Just in case it was something to do with the color of the fake flowers, the scientists also tried a different color combination and got the same result.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了以防这与假花的颜色有关，科学家们还尝试了不同的颜色组合，得到了相同的结果。

questions.name: #398 Security Footage
questions.en:
The introduction of security footage in courtrooms as evidence is increasingly common.
With the number of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras rising, the likelihood of images deemed relevant for criminal proceedings being recorded also increases.
However, while CCTV footage may arguably have assisted in achieving ______ in some high-profile cases, can it assist in the overall reduction of violence against women?
A well-known example in Australia of CCTV helping solve a crime is the footage pulled from a shop on Sydney Road the night Jill Meagher was raped and murdered by Adrian Bayley.
This footage was mentioned in his sentencing in 2013.
In the same year, Simon Gittany was found ______ of the murder of his partner Lisa Harnum.
CCTV footage – taken from his own security cameras – was again ______ as key evidence.
Beyond the courtroom, news media reports of crime are saturated with the use of CCTV footage.
In both contexts, it is often seen to be ______ – an authoritative and objective witness that can tell us “what really happened”.
While used in a range of offenses, its inclusion in instances of extreme (and public) violence against women can mean certain images receive significant and sustained media ______ , and may remain online indefinitely.
The strength of CCTV in our public consciousness is such that questions of privacy are often dismissed as inconsequential.
CCTV installed in the homes of family violence victims has even been considered.
1. convictions , discharges , disclaimers , connections
2. guilty , excessive , obsessive , abundant
3. interpreted , changed , disciplined , dictated
4. doubtful , decisive , inclusive , incisive
5. abortion , conception , abruption , attention

questions.name: #402 European Culture
questions.en:
Many people today think of culture in the way that it was thought of in Europe during the 18th and early 19th centuries.
This ______ of culture reflected inequalities within European societies and their colonies around the world.
This understanding of culture equates culture with civilization and contrasts both with nature or non-civilization.
According to this understanding of culture, some countries are more civilized than others, and some people are more cultured than others.
Anything that doesn’t fit into this category is labeled as chaos or anarchy.
From this perspective, culture is closely tied to cultivation, which is the progressive refinement of human ______ .
In practice, culture referred to elite goods and activities such as haute cuisine, high fashion or haute couture, museum-caliber art and classical music.
The word cultured referred to people who knew about and took part in these activities.
For example, someone who used culture in this sense might argue that classical music is more refined than music by working-class people, such as jazz or the indigenous music traditions of aboriginal peoples .
1. classification , concept , renovation , identity
2. cut , dismiss , fit , solve
3. blessing , curse , habit , behavior
4. argue , doubt , pretend , reveal
questions.full:

sense_groups.chinese: 如今许多人看待文化的方式，与18世纪及19世纪初欧洲的看法相同。

sense_groups.english: This concept of culture reflected inequalities within European societies and their colonies around the world.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种文化概念反映了欧洲社会及其全球殖民地内部的不平等。

sense_groups.english: This understanding of culture equates culture with civilization and contrasts both with nature or non-civilization.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种对文化的理解将文化等同于文明，并将两者与自然或非文明相对立。

sense_groups.english: According to this understanding of culture, some countries are more civilized than others, and some people are more cultured than others.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据这种文化理解，一些国家比其他国家更文明，一些人比其他人更有文化。

sense_groups.english: Anything that doesn’t fit into this category is labeled as chaos or anarchy.
sense_groups.chinese: 任何不符合这一类别的东西都被贴上混乱或无政府的标签。

sense_groups.chinese: 从这个角度看，文化与教养紧密相连，教养是人类行为的逐步完善。

sense_groups.english: In practice, culture referred to elite goods and activities such as haute cuisine, high fashion or haute couture, museum-caliber art and classical music.
sense_groups.chinese: 在实践中，文化指的是精英商品和活动，如高级烹饪、高级时装、博物馆级别的艺术和古典音乐。

sense_groups.english: The word cultured referred to people who knew about and took part in these activities.
sense_groups.chinese: “有教养的”一词指的是了解并参与这些活动的人。

sense_groups.english: For example, someone who used culture in this sense might argue that classical music is more refined than music by working-class people, such as jazz or the indigenous music traditions of aboriginal peoples.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，持这种文化观的人可能会争辩说，古典音乐比工人阶级的音乐（如爵士乐或原住民的土著音乐传统）更精致。

5. assume , discuss , prefer , acclaim

questions.answer:

2. meant
3. respect
4. According
5. assume
6. introduction

questions.name: #404 Heart Functions
questions.en:
The heart functions as a pump at the centre of the circulatory system.
In humans it is located in the chest cavity, between the lungs, ______ ______ to the left.
The heart consists of four chambers surrounded by a very strong muscular wall, the myocardium.
The upper chambers, the right and left atria, ______ blood entering the heart, and the lower chambers, the right and left ventricles pump the blood out of the heart, via the pulmonary and the systemic circulatory systems.
The two systems work as ______ .
Blood from the body enters the right atrium, ______ passed into the right ventricle and from there is propelled through the pulmonary artery to the lungs.
In the lungs the blood releases carbon dioxide and absorbs oxygen and is then ______ back to the heart into the left atrium.
From here it passes into the left ventricle, which pumps the oxygenated blood around the body.
1. compared , rather than , a bit , less than
2. lower , receive , repel , transfer
3. well , followed , follows , follow
4. being , is , has , had
5. transporting , transported , transport , having transported

sense_groups.english: The heart functions as a pump at the centre of the circulatory system.
sense_groups.chinese: 心脏在循环系统中充当泵的作用。

questions.name: #405 Light Energy
questions.en:
Light is usually described as a form of energy and it is indeed a kind of electromagnetic energy, not much different from radio waves, television signals, heat, and X-rays.
All of these are made up of waves that ______ , bend, interfere with one another, and react with obstacles in their path, rather like waves in water.
A physicist might tell you that light, along with all its electromagnetic relatives, is really a form of matter, little different from more ______ matter such as houses and, like them, it is made up of individual particles.
Light particles, called photons, travel in streams, similar to the way in which water pours through a hose.
To most people, this might sound paradoxical or illogical, as many things to do with physics seem to these days.
How can light be both energy and matter, wave and particle?
The reason it can be is, in fact, not at all ______ : all energy is a form of matter.
Almost everybody recognizes — even if they do not understand — Einstein’s famous equation, E =mc2, which spells it out: E refers to energy and m to the mass of matter.
Furthermore, all matter has some of the characteristics of waves and some of the particles, but the waves of such solid-seeming things as houses are not ______ and can generally be ignored because ordinary matter acts as if it were made up of particles.
1. spread , curve , occur , inflict
2. invisible , valuable , abstract , substantial
3. apparent , complicated , abrupt , implicit
4. responsible , accurate , discernible , consecutive

sense_groups.english: All of these are made up of waves that spread, bend, interfere with one another,
sense_groups.chinese: 所有这些都由波组成，这些波会扩散、弯曲、相互干扰

sense_groups.english: and react with obstacles in their path, rather like waves in water.
sense_groups.chinese: 并与路径上的障碍物相互作用，就像水中的波浪一样。

sense_groups.english: A physicist might tell you that light, along with all its electromagnetic relatives,
sense_groups.chinese: 物理学家可能会告诉你，光及其所有电磁相关物

sense_groups.english: is really a form of matter,
sense_groups.chinese: 实际上是一种物质形式

sense_groups.english: little different from more substantial matter such as houses
sense_groups.chinese: 与房屋等更实在的物质几乎没有区别

sense_groups.english: and, like them, it is made up of individual particles.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且像它们一样，由单个粒子组成。

sense_groups.english: Light particles, called photons, travel in streams,
sense_groups.chinese: 称为光子的光粒子以流的形式传播

sense_groups.english: similar to the way in which water pours through a hose.
sense_groups.chinese: 类似于水通过软管流出的方式。

sense_groups.english: To most people, this might sound paradoxical or illogical,
sense_groups.chinese: 对大多数人来说，这听起来可能自相矛盾或不合逻辑

sense_groups.english: as many things to do with physics seem to these days.
sense_groups.chinese: 就像如今许多与物理学相关的事情一样。

sense_groups.english: How can light be both energy and matter, wave and particle?
sense_groups.chinese: 光怎么能既是能量又是物质，既是波又是粒子呢？

sense_groups.english: The reason it can be is, in fact, not at all complicated:
sense_groups.chinese: 它之所以能这样，其实一点也不复杂：

sense_groups.english: all energy is a form of matter.
sense_groups.chinese: 所有能量都是物质的一种形式。

sense_groups.english: Almost everybody recognizes — even if they do not understand —
sense_groups.chinese: 几乎每个人都认识到——即使他们不理解——

sense_groups.english: Einstein’s famous equation, E =mc2, which spells it out:
sense_groups.chinese: 爱因斯坦的著名方程E=mc²，它清楚地说明了这一点：

sense_groups.english: E refers to energy and m to the mass of matter.
sense_groups.chinese: E代表能量，m代表物质的质量。

sense_groups.english: Furthermore, all matter has some of the characteristics of waves
sense_groups.chinese: 此外，所有物质都具有波的一些特性

sense_groups.english: and some of the particles,
sense_groups.chinese: 和粒子的一些特性

sense_groups.english: but the waves of such solid-seeming things as houses are not discernible
sense_groups.chinese: 但像房屋这样看似坚固的东西的波是不可辨别的

sense_groups.english: and can generally be ignored
sense_groups.chinese: 通常可以被忽略

sense_groups.english: because ordinary matter acts as if it were made up of particles.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为普通物质表现得好像它是由粒子组成的。

questions.name: #406 Computer Viruses
questions.en:
Computer viruses have been a ______ of life at least since the 1980s, if not before.
They can cause companies to lose hours of working time and they can also spread panic among computer users everywhere.
There are, however, several ______ types of computer infection – all loosely referred to as viruses – and they each work in a slightly different way.
A particularly nasty one is the worm, which is a program designed to sneak its way into an entire computer network, and reproduce itself over and over again.
Then there is the Trojan, which strictly ______ isn’t a virus, but a piece of software that appears to do one thing, but actually does something malicious instead.
When the 'unsuspecting' operator introduces it into the computer, the alien program will take over the machine.
With Trojans you have to be particularly careful because they can often be introduced by way of a message advertising an anti-virus product.
So what motivates someone to ______ a virus into the computer systems of innocent victims?
Perhaps it’s simply the desire to prove that it can be done.
Or because it gives the kind of pleasure you get from solving a difficult problem – nowadays people protect their computers with all sorts of security software, so it takes considerable ______ to break through all the defences and introduce a virus.
1. link , verge , fact , virtue
2. successive , distinct , discreet , opaque
3. speaking , doing , done , figured
4. deploy , deduce , introduce , imply
5. consumption , regret , skill , degree
questions.full:

There are, however, several ______ types of computer infection – all loosely referred to as viruses – and they each work in a slightly different way.

1. link , verge , fact , virtue
2. successive , distinct , discreet , opaque
3. speaking , doing , done , figured

5. consumption , regret , skill , degree

2. distinct
3. speaking
4. introduce

sense_groups.english: Computer viruses have been a fact of life at least since the 1980s, if not before.
sense_groups.chinese: 计算机病毒至少从20世纪80年代起就成为生活中的一个事实，甚至可能更早。

sense_groups.english: They can cause companies to lose hours of working time and they can also spread panic among computer users everywhere.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们可能导致公司损失数小时的工作时间，并在全球计算机用户中引发恐慌。

sense_groups.english: There are, however, several distinct types of computer infection – all loosely referred to as viruses – and they each work in a slightly different way.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，有几种不同类型的计算机感染——都笼统地称为病毒——每种的工作方式略有不同。

sense_groups.english: A particularly nasty one is the worm, which is a program designed to sneak its way into an entire computer network, and reproduce itself over and over again.
sense_groups.chinese: 一种特别讨厌的是蠕虫，它是一种旨在潜入整个计算机网络并不断自我复制的程序。

sense_groups.english: Then there is the Trojan, which strictly speaking isn’t a virus, but a piece of software that appears to do one thing, but actually does something malicious instead.
sense_groups.chinese: 然后是特洛伊木马，严格来说它不是病毒，而是一种看似做一件事但实际上做恶意事情的软件。

sense_groups.english: When the 'unsuspecting' operator introduces it into the computer, the alien program will take over the machine.
sense_groups.chinese: 当“毫无戒心的”操作员将其引入计算机时，这个外来程序将接管机器。

sense_groups.english: With Trojans you have to be particularly careful because they can often be introduced by way of a message advertising an anti-virus product.
sense_groups.chinese: 对于特洛伊木马，你必须特别小心，因为它们通常通过宣传防病毒产品的消息被引入。

sense_groups.english: So what motivates someone to introduce a virus into the computer systems of innocent victims?
sense_groups.chinese: 那么是什么促使某人将病毒引入无辜受害者的计算机系统呢？

sense_groups.english: Perhaps it’s simply the desire to prove that it can be done.
sense_groups.chinese: 也许只是证明可以做到这一点的欲望。

sense_groups.english: Or because it gives the kind of pleasure you get from solving a difficult problem – nowadays people protect their computers with all sorts of security software, so it takes considerable skill to break through all the defences and introduce a virus.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者因为它能带来解决难题的那种乐趣——如今人们用各种安全软件保护电脑，所以需要相当高的技能才能突破所有防御并引入病毒。

questions.name: #408 Left-handed Population
questions.en:
In any given population, about ten percent of the people are left-handed and this figure remains ______ stable over time.
So-called “handedness” runs in families, but what causes it and why the proportion of left-handed to right-handed people is a constant are still a mystery.
One thing we do know is that hand ______ is related to brain asymmetry; and it seems to be generally agreed that the human brain is profoundly asymmetric, and that understanding how this works will tell us much about who we are and how our brains work.
Brain (function) is ______ into the left and right hemispheres, and this is crucial for understanding language, thought, memory, and perhaps even creativity.
For right-handed people, language activity is mainly on the left side.
Many left-handers also have left-side language dominance, but a significant number may have language either more ______ distributed in both hemispheres or else predominantly on the right side of the brain.
Because left-handedness is seen as a key to the complex anatomy of the brain, scientists are searching for links to other ______ , including immune disorders, learning disabilities, and reduced life expectancy.
1. relative , closely , thus , relatively
2. dominance , proportion , strength , balance
3. figured , changed , distributed , added
4. largely , mainly , barely , evenly
5. conclusions , roundabouts , preferences , conditions

questions.name: #423 Amyloid Beta
questions.en:
It's like the molecular version of the Joker and the Riddler teaming up against Batman.
  ______ at Yale University have discovered that amyloid beta, a protein involved in Alzheimer's disease, can damage brain cells by binding to prion proteins, which are themselves infamous because, in their abnormal form, they cause things like mad cow disease.
Amyloid beta is best known as the protein that forms the giant plaques that riddle the brains of people with Alzheimer's. Those plaques contain billions of copies of amyloid beta all stuck together in one gloppy mess.
But the protein also exists in a more soluble form, either in single units or in small groups of 50 or 100.
These smaller clusters don't cause the same large-scale mayhem as plaques, but they do damage neurons, impairing their ability to learn.
And the Yale researchers wanted to find out how.
They discovered that amyloid beta binds to the prion proteins normally found on neurons.

So drugs that prevent this amyloid-prion coupling could be a potent weapon against Alzheimer's.

2. allergic , strophic , neurotoxic , histrionic
3. harmless , mollusks , commons , augments
4. exulted , content , published , demist

2. neurotoxic
3. harmless
4. published

sense_groups.english: It's like the molecular version of the Joker and the Riddler teaming up against Batman.
sense_groups.chinese: 这就像是分子版的小丑和谜语人联手对抗蝙蝠侠。

sense_groups.english: Scientists at Yale University have discovered that amyloid beta, a protein involved in Alzheimer's disease, can damage brain cells by binding to prion proteins, which are themselves infamous because, in their abnormal form, they cause things like mad cow disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 耶鲁大学的科学家发现，与阿尔茨海默病有关的蛋白质β-淀粉样蛋白，可以通过结合朊病毒蛋白来损伤脑细胞，而朊病毒蛋白本身因其异常形式会导致疯牛病等疾病而臭名昭著。

sense_groups.english: Amyloid beta is best known as the protein that forms the giant plaques that riddle the brains of people with Alzheimer's.
sense_groups.chinese: β-淀粉样蛋白最出名的是形成巨大斑块，这些斑块遍布阿尔茨海默病患者的大脑。

sense_groups.english: Those plaques contain billions of copies of amyloid beta all stuck together in one gloppy mess.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些斑块包含数十亿个β-淀粉样蛋白副本，全部粘在一起形成一团黏糊糊的东西。

sense_groups.english: But the protein also exists in a more soluble form, either in single units or in small groups of 50 or 100.
sense_groups.chinese: 但这种蛋白质也以更可溶的形式存在，要么是单个单元，要么是50或100个的小团。

sense_groups.english: These smaller clusters don't cause the same large-scale mayhem as plaques, but they do damage neurons, impairing their ability to learn.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些较小的团簇不会像斑块那样造成大规模破坏，但它们确实会损伤神经元，损害其学习能力。

sense_groups.english: And the Yale researchers wanted to find out how.
sense_groups.chinese: 耶鲁大学的研究人员想弄清楚这是如何发生的。

sense_groups.english: They discovered that amyloid beta binds to the prion proteins normally found on neurons.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们发现β-淀粉样蛋白会结合通常存在于神经元上的朊病毒蛋白。

sense_groups.english: What's more, the prions ramp up amyloid beta's neurotoxic effects.
sense_groups.chinese: 更重要的是，朊病毒会增强β-淀粉样蛋白的神经毒性作用。

sense_groups.english: Take away the prions and amyloid-beta clusters are harmless, findings published in the journal Nature.
sense_groups.chinese: 去除朊病毒后，β-淀粉样蛋白团簇就无害了，这一发现发表在《自然》杂志上。

sense_groups.english: So drugs that prevent this amyloid-prion coupling could be a potent weapon against Alzheimer's.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，阻止这种淀粉样蛋白-朊病毒结合的药物可能成为对抗阿尔茨海默病的有效武器。

questions.name: #424 Employee Mood
questions.en:
Research from the Terry College of Business reveals ______ a happy, helpful employee takes effort and, eventually, that effort ______ the energy needed to do one’s job.
It could lead to quiet quitting – the new term for just doing your job but not going above and beyond – or even actual quitting.
The more people adjust their moods to be happy, the fewer emotional resources they have ______ the end of the day.
That means they are less able to handle challenging tasks and interactions and have a harder time staying on task.
Their tank is empty despite being in a good mood, Frank explained.
For managers, this means it may make more sense to meet employees ______ they are emotionally and not force upbeat attitudes in the office.
For employees, it may mean letting bad days happen and leaving more mood-demanding work — such as sales calls or tough conversations — for better days.
1. becomes , becoming , become , become to
2. concludes , erodes , expects , collects
3. at , since , by , for
4. where , which , what , that

2. concludes , erodes , expects , collects

2. erodes
3. at
