Sound depressing, even apocalyptic?
Well, it could be the future.
If government ______ are right, about 20 years from now, two out of five households will be single ______ .
And there is evidence the situation is already ______ .
According to a report, Social Isolation in America, published in the American Sociological Review in 2006, the average American today has only two close friends.
Twenty-five per cent of those surveyed said they do not have anyone to talk with about important things—And yet, while some are ______ a crisis in our ability to make friends, others are saying exactly the opposite.
For example, MSN's Anatomy of Friendship Report, published last November, suggests that the average Briton has 54 friends—a ______ rise of 64 per cent since 2003.
1. prediction , goals , aims , forecasts
2. household , occupied , occupancy , family
3. damaging , improving , deteriorating , recovering
4. denouncing , releasing , requiring , declaring
5. spectacular , applausive , amazing , special

sense_groups.english: Sound depressing, even apocalyptic?

sense_groups.chinese: 嗯，这可能是未来的景象。

sense_groups.chinese: 如果政府的预测正确，

sense_groups.chinese: 去年11月发布，

questions.name: #546 Edison
questions.en:
Thomas Alva Edison was both a scientist and an inventor.
Born in 1847, Edison would see ______ changes take place in his lifetime.
He was also to be responsible for making many of those changes occur.
When Edison was born, society still thought of electricity as a ______ , a fad.
By the time he died, entire cities were lit by electricity.
Much of the credit for that progress goes to Edison.
In his lifetime, Edison patented 1,093 inventions, earning him the nickname “The Wizard of Menlo Park.” The most famous of his inventions was the incandescent light bulb.
Besides the light bulb, Edison ______ the phonograph and the “kinetoscope,” a small box for viewing moving films.
Thomas Edison is also the first person in the US to make his own filmstrips.
He also ______ upon the original design of the stock ticker, the telegraph, and Alexander Graham Bell’s telephone.
He believed in hard work, sometimes working twenty hours a day.
Edison was quoted as saying, “Genius is one percent inspiration and 99 percent perspiration.” In ______ to this important American, electric lights in the United States were dimmed for one minute on October 21, 1931, a few days after his death.
1. experimental , moderate , tremendous , trenchant
2. news , miracle , tradition , novelty
3. looked , imposed , depended , improved
4. honor , tribute , addition , memory

sense_groups.english: Thomas Alva Edison was both a scientist and an inventor.
sense_groups.chinese: 托马斯·阿尔瓦·爱迪生既是一位科学家，也是一位发明家。

sense_groups.english: Born in 1847, Edison would see tremendous changes take place in his lifetime.
sense_groups.chinese: 爱迪生出生于1847年，他一生中见证了巨大的变化。

sense_groups.english: He was also to be responsible for making many of those changes occur.
sense_groups.chinese: 他也负责促成了许多这些变化的发生。

sense_groups.english: When Edison was born, society still thought of electricity as a novelty, a fad.
sense_groups.chinese: 当爱迪生出生时，社会仍将电视为一种新奇事物，一种时尚。

sense_groups.english: By the time he died, entire cities were lit by electricity.
sense_groups.chinese: 到他去世时，整个城市都用电照明。

sense_groups.english: Much of the credit for that progress goes to Edison.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一进步很大程度上归功于爱迪生。

sense_groups.english: In his lifetime, Edison patented 1,093 inventions, earning him the nickname “The Wizard of Menlo Park.”
sense_groups.chinese: 在他的一生中，爱迪生获得了1093项发明专利，为他赢得了“门洛帕克的奇才”的绰号。

sense_groups.english: The most famous of his inventions was the incandescent light bulb.
sense_groups.chinese: 他最著名的发明是白炽灯泡。

sense_groups.english: Besides the light bulb, Edison developed the phonograph and the “kinetoscope,” a small box for viewing moving films.
sense_groups.chinese: 除了灯泡，爱迪生还发明了留声机和“活动电影放映机”，这是一种观看活动电影的小盒子。

sense_groups.english: Thomas Edison is also the first person in the US to make his own filmstrips.
sense_groups.chinese: 托马斯·爱迪生也是美国第一个制作自己电影胶片的人。

sense_groups.english: He also improved upon the original design of the stock ticker, the telegraph, and Alexander Graham Bell’s telephone.
sense_groups.chinese: 他还改进了股票行情自动收录器、电报和亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔的电话的原始设计。

sense_groups.english: He believed in hard work, sometimes working twenty hours a day.
sense_groups.chinese: 他相信勤奋工作，有时一天工作二十个小时。

sense_groups.english: Edison was quoted as saying, “Genius is one percent inspiration and 99 percent perspiration.”
sense_groups.chinese: 爱迪生曾说过：“天才是百分之一的灵感加上百分之九十九的汗水。”

sense_groups.english: In tribute to this important American, electric lights in the United States were dimmed for one minute on October 21, 1931, a few days after his death.
sense_groups.chinese: 为了向这位重要的美国人致敬，1931年10月21日，也就是他去世几天后，美国各地的电灯调暗了一分钟。

questions.name: #547 Impressionist
questions.en:
Impressionism was a nineteenth century art movement that began as a loose association of Paris-based artists who started publicly exhibiting their art in the 1860s.
Characteristics of Impressionist painting include visible brush strokes, light colors, open composition, ______ on light in its changing qualities (often accentuating the effects of the passage of time), ordinary subject matter, and unusual visual angles.
The name of the movement ______ ______ from Claude Monet's Impression, Sunrise (Impression, soleil levant).
Critic Louis Leroy inadvertently coined the term in a satiric review published in Le Charivari.
Radicals in their time, early Impressionists broke the rules of academic painting.
They began by giving colors, freely brushed, primacy over line, drawing ______ from the work of painters such as Eugene Delacroix.
They also took the ______ of painting out of the studio and into the world.
Previously, not only still-lives and portraits, but also landscapes had been painted indoors, but the Impressionists found that they could ______ the momentary and transient effects of sunlight by painting air (in plain air).
1. emphasized , emphasis , emphatic, , emphasize
2. deriving , have derived , derive , is derived
3. inspiration , inspiring , inspired , inspire
4. act , actor , action , active
5. capture , carry , conduct , culminate
questions.answer:
1. emphasis
2. is
3. derived
4. inspiration
5. act
6. capture

sense_groups.chinese: 最初是由巴黎艺术家组成的松散团体

sense_groups.english: who started publicly exhibiting their art in the 1860s.

sense_groups.chinese: 印象派绘画的特点包括可见的笔触、明亮的色彩、开放的构图

sense_groups.chinese: 该运动的名字来源于克劳德·莫奈的《印象·日出》。

sense_groups.chinese: 评论家路易·勒鲁瓦在《喧闹》杂志上发表的一篇讽刺评论中无意中创造了这个术语。

sense_groups.english: Radicals in their time, early Impressionists broke the rules of academic painting.
sense_groups.chinese: 作为当时的激进派，早期印象派打破了学院派绘画的规则。

sense_groups.english: They began by giving colors, freely brushed, primacy over line,

sense_groups.english: They also took the act of painting out of the studio and into the world.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们还将绘画行为从画室带到了户外。

sense_groups.english: Previously, not only still-lives and portraits, but also landscapes had been painted indoors,

sense_groups.english: by painting air (in plain air).
sense_groups.chinese: 通过户外写生（在露天中作画）。

questions.name: #548 Trigger Points
questions.en:
All approaches aim to increase blood flow to areas of tension and to release painful knots ______ muscle known as "trigger points".
"Trigger points are tense areas of muscle that are almost constantly contracting," says Kippen.
"The contraction causes pain, which in turn causes contraction, so you have a vicious circle.
This is what deep tissue massage aims to break.
"The way to do this, as I found out under Ogedengbe's elbow, is to apply pressure ______ the point, stopping the blood flow, and then to release, which causes the brain to flood the affected area ______ blood, encouraging the muscle to relax.
At the same time, says Kippen, you can fool the tensed muscle ______ relaxing ______ applying pressure to a complementary one nearby.
"If you cause any muscle to contract, its opposite will expand.
So you try to trick the body into relaxing the muscle that is in spasm."

2. in , to , on , for
3. by , of , with , in

5. from , with , by , to

questions.name: #551 Spanish Language
questions.en:
If after years of Spanish classes, some people still find it impossible to understand some native speakers, they should not worry.
This does not ______ mean the lessons were wasted.
Millions of Spanish speakers use neither standard Latin American Spanish nor Castilian, which ______ in US schools.
The confusion is partly political - the Spanish-speaking world is very diverse.
Spanish is the language of 19 separate countries and Puerto Rico.
This means that there is no one standard dialect.
The most common Spanish dialect taught in the US is standard Latin American.
It is sometimes called "Highland" Spanish since it is generally spoken in the ______ areas of Latin America.
While each country retains its own ______ and has some unique vocabulary, residents of countries such as Mexico, Colombia, Peru, and Bolivia generally speak Latin American Spanish, especially in urban centers.
This dialect is noted for its ______ of each letter and its strong "r" sounds.
This Spanish was spoken in Spain in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries and was brought to the Americas by the early colonists.
However, the Spanish of Madrid and of northern Spain, called Castilian, developed ______ that never reached the New World.
These include the pronunciation of "ci" and "ce" as "th." In Madrid, "gracias" (thank you) becomes "gratheas" (as opposed to "gras-see-as" in Latin America).
Another difference is the use of the word "vosotros" (you all, or you guys) as the informal form of "ustedes" in Spain.
Castilian sounds to Latin Americans much like British English sounds to US residents.
1. usually , only , particularly , necessarily
2. evolve , proceed , precede , predominate
3. mountainous , coastal , rocky , hidden
4. accents , actions , authority , thoughts
5. elucidation , remembering , pronunciation , collection
6. normality , characteristics , problems , distinguishes
questions.answer:
1. necessarily
2. predominate
3. mountainous
4. accents
5. pronunciation
6. characteristics

sense_groups.english: If after years of Spanish classes, some people still find it impossible to understand some native speakers, they should not worry.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果在上了多年西班牙语课后，有些人仍然觉得无法理解一些母语者，他们不必担心。

sense_groups.english: This does not necessarily mean the lessons were wasted.
sense_groups.chinese: 这并不一定意味着课程白上了。

sense_groups.english: Millions of Spanish speakers use neither standard Latin American Spanish nor Castilian, which predominate in US schools.
sense_groups.chinese: 数百万西班牙语使用者既不使用标准拉丁美洲西班牙语，也不使用在美国学校中占主导地位的卡斯蒂利亚西班牙语。

sense_groups.chinese: 这种困惑部分源于政治因素——西班牙语世界非常多样化。

sense_groups.english: This means that there is no one standard dialect.

sense_groups.chinese: 虽然每个国家保留自己的口音并有一些独特词汇，但墨西哥、哥伦比亚、秘鲁和玻利维亚等国的居民通常说拉丁美洲西班牙语，尤其是在城市中心。

sense_groups.english: This dialect is noted for its pronunciation of each letter and its strong "r" sounds.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种方言以每个字母的发音和强烈的“r”音而闻名。

sense_groups.english: This Spanish was spoken in Spain in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries and was brought to the Americas by the early colonists.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种西班牙语在16和17世纪在西班牙使用，并由早期殖民者带到美洲。

sense_groups.english: However, the Spanish of Madrid and of northern Spain, called Castilian, developed characteristics that never reached the New World.

sense_groups.chinese: 这些包括将“ci”和“ce”发音为“th”。在马德里，“gracias”（谢谢）变成“gratheas”（与拉丁美洲的“gras-see-as”相对）。

sense_groups.english: Another difference is the use of the word "vosotros" (you all, or you guys) as the informal form of "ustedes" in Spain.
sense_groups.chinese: 另一个区别是在西班牙使用“vosotros”（你们大家）作为“ustedes”的非正式形式。

sense_groups.english: Castilian sounds to Latin Americans much like British English sounds to US residents.
sense_groups.chinese: 卡斯蒂利亚西班牙语对拉丁美洲人来说，就像英式英语对美国居民一样。

questions.name: #552 Ocean Floor
questions.en:
The ocean floor is home to many unique communities of plants and animals.
Most of these marine ecosystems are near the water surface, such as the Great Barrier Reef, a 2,000-km long coral ______ off the northeastern coast of Australia.
Coral reefs, like nearly all complex living communities, depend on solar energy for growth (photosynthesis).
The sun's energy, however, penetrates at most only about 300 m below the surface of the water.
The relatively shallow penetration of solar energy and the sinking of cold, subpolar water combine to make most of the deep ocean floor a ______ environment with few life forms.
In 1977, scientists discovered hot springs at a depth of 2.5 km, on the Galapagos Rift (spreading ridge) off the coast of Ecuador.
This exciting discovery was not really ______ ______ .
Since the early 1970s, scientists had predicted that hot springs (geothermal vents) should be found at the active spreading centers along the mid-oceanic ridges, where magma, at temperatures over 1,000° Presumably was being erupted to form new oceanic crust.

1. system , reality , structure , formation
2. versatile , frigid , warm , perfect
3. a surprise , any chance , some sign , climax
4. no expectation , undermined , unexpected , predictable
5. struggling , died , thrived , exists

questions.name: #556 Kimbell
questions.en:
The first section of the book covers new modes of assessment.
In Chapter 1, Kimbell (Goldsmith College, London) responds to ______ of design programs as formalistic and conventional, stating that a focus on risk-taking rather than hard work in design innovation is equally problematic.
His research contains three parts that include preliminary exploration of design innovation qualities, investigation of resulting classroom practices, and development of evidence-based assessment.
The assessment he describes is presented in the form of a structured worksheet, which includes a collaborative ______ and digital photographs, in story format.

  ______ judgments are evident in terms such as “wow” and “yawn” and reward the quality and quantity of ideas with the term, “sparkiness”, which fittingly is a pun as the model project was to design light bulb packaging.
In addition, the assessment focuses on the process of optimizing or complexity control as well as proving ideas with thoughtful criticism and not just generation of novel ideas.
The definitions for qualities such as “technical” and “aesthetic” pertaining to users, are too narrow and ill-defined.

sense_groups.english: The first section of the book covers new modes of assessment.
sense_groups.chinese: 本书的第一部分涵盖了新的评估模式。

sense_groups.english: In Chapter 1, Kimbell (Goldsmith College, London) responds to criticisms of design programs as formalistic and conventional, stating that a focus on risk-taking rather than hard work in design innovation is equally problematic.
sense_groups.chinese: 在第一章中，伦敦金史密斯学院的Kimbell回应了对设计项目形式化和传统的批评，指出在设计创新中关注冒险而非努力同样有问题。

sense_groups.english: His research contains three parts that include preliminary exploration of design innovation qualities, investigation of resulting classroom practices, and development of evidence-based assessment.
sense_groups.chinese: 他的研究包含三个部分：初步探索设计创新品质、调查由此产生的课堂实践，以及开发基于证据的评估。

sense_groups.english: The assessment he describes is presented in the form of a structured worksheet, which includes a collaborative element and digital photographs, in story format.
sense_groups.chinese: 他所描述的评估以结构化工作表的形式呈现，其中包含协作元素和数字照片，以故事格式呈现。

sense_groups.english: The assessment sheet includes holistic impressions as well as details about “having, growing, and proving” ideas.

sense_groups.chinese: 此外，评估侧重于优化或复杂性控制的过程，以及通过深思熟虑的批评来证明想法，而不仅仅是产生新颖的想法。

But as I stretched to catch the drips and drops of their humming dialogue, I couldn’t ______ it all, only that it was English.
Those words now flying before me sounded a little familiar.
I had read them and tried to speak them, but I had never heard them ______ back to me in such a speedy, fluent manner.
My big plan of beating the city folks was thawing before my eyes.
1. majored , major , majors , majoring
2. telling , told , tells , tell
3. talking , talked , talks , talk
4. understanding , understand , understands , understood

sense_groups.english: There were twenty-six freshmen majoring in English at Beijing Language Institute in the class of 1983.
sense_groups.chinese: 1983届北京语言学院有26名英语专业的新生。

sense_groups.english: I was assigned to Group Two with another eleven boy and girls who had come from big cities in China.
sense_groups.chinese: 我被分到第二组，和另外十一个来自中国大城市的男孩女孩一起。

sense_groups.english: I was told that language study required smallness so that we would each get more attention from the skillful teachers.
sense_groups.chinese: 有人告诉我，语言学习需要小班制，这样我们每个人都能得到熟练老师更多的关注。

sense_groups.chinese: 学校越好，班级越小。

sense_groups.chinese: 我意识到我的同学们都已经在用英语交谈了，简单的句子在脸红红的介绍和轻松的聊天中互相抛来抛去。

sense_groups.english: Their intonations were curving and dramatic and their pronunciation refined and accurate.

sense_groups.english: But as I stretched to catch the drips and drops of their humming dialogue, I couldn’t understand it all, only that it was English.
sense_groups.chinese: 但当我努力捕捉他们嗡嗡对话中的点点滴滴时，我并不能完全理解，只知道那是英语。

sense_groups.english: Those words now flying before me sounded a little familiar.
sense_groups.chinese: 那些在我面前飞过的词语听起来有点熟悉。

sense_groups.english: I had read them and tried to speak them, but I had never heard them spoken back to me in such a speedy, fluent manner.
sense_groups.chinese: 我读过它们，也试着说过，但我从未听过它们以如此快速、流利的方式回响在我耳边。

sense_groups.english: My big plan of beating the city folks was thawing before my eyes.
sense_groups.chinese: 我打败城里人的大计划在我眼前融化了。

questions.name: #558 Jean Piaget
questions.en:
Jean Piaget, the pioneering Swiss philosopher and psychologist, spent much of his professional life listening to children, watching children and poring ______ reports of researchers around the world who were doing the same.
He found, to put it most succinctly ,that children don't think like grownups.
After thousands of interactions with young people often barely old enough to talk, Piaget began to ______ that behind their cute and seemingly illogical ______ were thought processes that had their own kind of order and their own special logic.
Einstein called it a ______ "so simple that only a genius could have thought of it." Piaget's insight opened a new window into the inner workings of the mind.
By the end of a wide-ranging and remarkably ______ research career that spanned nearly 75 years, from his first scientific publication at age 10 to work still in progress when he died at 84, Piaget had developed several new fields of science: developmental psychology, cognitive theory and what came to be called genetic epistemology.
Although not an educational reformer, he ______ a way of thinking about children that provided the foundation for today’s education-reform ______ .
It was a shift comparable to the displacement of stories of "noble savages" and "cannibals" by modern anthropology.
One might say that Piaget was the first to take children's thinking seriously.
1. over , towards , like , above
2. suspect , dictate , understand , assume
3. oblivion , utterances , speaking , communications
4. misunderstanding , discovery , invention , distress
5. written , reviewed , prolific , proved
6. guided , designed , opened , fashioned
7. movements , application , transformation , revolution
questions.answer:
1. over
2. suspect
3. utterances
4. discovery
5. prolific
6. fashioned
7. movements

Although not an educational reformer, he ______ a way of thinking about children that provided the foundation for today’s education-reform ______ .

sense_groups.english: Jean Piaget, the pioneering Swiss philosopher and psychologist, spent much of his professional life listening to children, watching children and poring over reports of researchers around the world who were doing the same.
sense_groups.chinese: 让·皮亚杰，这位开创性的瑞士哲学家和心理学家，职业生涯的大部分时间都在倾听儿童、观察儿童，并仔细研读世界各地同样在做这些的研究人员的报告。

sense_groups.english: He found, to put it most succinctly, that children don't think like grownups.
sense_groups.chinese: 他发现，简而言之，儿童不像成年人那样思考。

sense_groups.english: After thousands of interactions with young people often barely old enough to talk, Piaget began to suspect that behind their cute and seemingly illogical utterances were thought processes that had their own kind of order and their own special logic.
sense_groups.chinese: 在与数千名通常刚会说话的年轻人互动后，皮亚杰开始怀疑，在他们可爱且看似不合逻辑的话语背后，存在着具有自身秩序和特殊逻辑的思维过程。

sense_groups.english: Einstein called it a discovery "so simple that only a genius could have thought of it."
sense_groups.chinese: 爱因斯坦称其为一项发现，“简单到只有天才才能想到它。”

sense_groups.english: Piaget's insight opened a new window into the inner workings of the mind.
sense_groups.chinese: 皮亚杰的洞察力为理解心灵的内部运作打开了一扇新窗户。

sense_groups.english: By the end of a wide-ranging and remarkably prolific research career that spanned nearly 75 years, from his first scientific publication at age 10 to work still in progress when he died at 84, Piaget had developed several new fields of science: developmental psychology, cognitive theory and what came to be called genetic epistemology.
sense_groups.chinese: 在跨越近75年的广泛且多产的研究生涯结束时——从他10岁发表第一篇科学论文到84岁去世时仍在进行的工作——皮亚杰开创了几个新的科学领域：发展心理学、认知理论以及后来被称为发生认识论的学科。

sense_groups.english: Although not an educational reformer, he fashioned a way of thinking about children that provided the foundation for today’s education-reform movements.
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然不是教育改革者，但他塑造了一种思考儿童的方式，为当今的教育改革运动奠定了基础。

sense_groups.english: It was a shift comparable to the displacement of stories of "noble savages" and "cannibals" by modern anthropology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一转变堪比现代人类学取代了“高贵的野蛮人”和“食人族”的故事。

sense_groups.english: One might say that Piaget was the first to take children's thinking seriously.
sense_groups.chinese: 可以说，皮亚杰是第一个认真对待儿童思维的人。

questions.name: #559 Definition of Country
questions.en:

questions.name: #561 Market for Vegetarian Foods
questions.en:

questions.name: #562 Job Hunting
questions.en:
When it comes to job-hunting, first impressions are critical.
Remember, you are marketing a product - yourself - to a potential employer.
The first thing the employer sees when greeting you is your ______ ;thus, you must make every effort to have the proper dress for the type of job you are seeking.
Will dressing properly get you the job?
Of course not, but it will give you a competitive edge and a ______ first impression.
Should you be judged by what you wear?
Perhaps not, but the reality is, of course, that you are judged.
Throughout the entire job-seeking process employers use short-cuts — heuristics or rules of thumb — to save time.
With cover letters, it’s the opening paragraph and a quick scan of your qualifications.
With resumes, it is a quick scan of your accomplishments.
With the job interview, it’s how you’re dressed that sets the ______ of the interview.
How should you dress?
Dressing conservatively is always the safest route, but you should also try and do a little investigating of your ______ employer so that what you wear to the interview makes you look as though you ______ in with the organization.
If you overdress (which is rare but can happen) or under dress (the more likely scenario), the potential employer may feel that you don't care enough about the job.
1. attire , make-up , suit , appearance
2. grudging , gratuitous , positive , punctilious
3. tongue , tone , key , taste
4. prospective , prosper , proactive , projective
5. fit , keep , jump , suit

questions.name: #563 Non-indigenous Plants
questions.en:
The invasion of non-indigenous plants is considered a primary threat to integrity and function of ecosystems.
However, there is little quantitative or ______ evidence for ecosystem impacts of invasive species.
Justifications for control are often based on potential, but not presently realized, recognized or quantified, negative impacts.
Should lack of scientific certainty about impacts of non-indigenous species result in postponing measures to prevent degradation?
Recently, management of purple loosestrife (Lythrum salicaria), has been criticized for lack of evidence demonstrating negative impacts of L. salicaria, and management using biocontrol for lack of evidence documenting the failure of conventional control methods.
Although little quantitative evidence on negative impacts on native wetland biota and wetland function was available at the onset of the control program in 1985, recent work has demonstrated that the invasion of purple loosestrife into North American freshwater wetlands alters ______ rates and nutrient cycling, leads to reductions in wetland plant diversity, reduces pollination and seed output of the native Lythrum alatum, and reduces habitat ______ for specialized wetland bird species such as black terns, least bitterns, pied-billed grebes, and marsh wrens.
Conventional methods (physical, mechanical or chemical), have continuously failed to ______ the spread of purple loosestrife or to provide satisfactory control.
Although a number of generalist insect and bird species utilize purple loosestrife, wetland habitat specialists are excluded by encroachment of L. salicaria.
We conclude that negative ecosystem impacts of purple loosestrife in North America justify control of the species and that ______ effects of purple loosestrife on wetland systems and biota and the potential benefits of control outweigh potential risks associated with the introduction of biocontrol agents.
Long term experiments and monitoring programs that are in place will evaluate the impact of these insects on purple loosestrife, on wetland plant succession and other wetland biota.
1. experiencing , experience , experimental , experiments
2. decomposing , composition , composing , decomposition
3. fixability , stability , friability , suitability
4. engage , curb , monopolize , reduce
5. encroachment , engagement , enlightenment , enrollment
6. beneficial , positive , detrimental , neutral

sense_groups.chinese: 现有的长期实验和监测项目将评估这些昆虫对千屈菜、湿地植物演替和其他湿地生物群的影响。

questions.name: #564 Roman Arena

questions.name: #572 Hans Christian Andersen
questions.en:
Fans of biographical criticism have a luxurious source in the works of Hans Christian Andersen.
Like Lewis Carroll (and, to a lesser extent, Kenneth Grahame), Andersen was near- pathologically uncomfortable in the company of adults.
Of course, all three had to work and ______ with adults, but all three really ______ well to children and their simpler worlds.
Andersen, for a time, ran a puppet theater and was incredibly popular with children, and, of course, he wrote an impressive body of fairy tales which have been produced in thousands of editions since the 19th century.
Most everyone has read or at least knows the titles of many of Andersen’s works: “The Ugly Duckling,” “The Emperor’s New Clothes,” “The Nightingale,” “The Little Mermaid,” “The Match Girl,” and many others.
Though, as with most folk and fairy tales, they ______ adult rereaders much differently than they do young first-time readers.
Charming tales of ducks who feel ______ because they don’t fit in, only to exult in the discovery that they are majestic swans, gives child readers clearly-identifiable messages: don’t tease people because they’re different; don’t fret about your being different because some day you’ll discover what special ______ you have.
A closer, deeper look at many of Andersen’s tales (including “The Ugly Duckling,” which is not on our reading list), reveals a darker, harder, more ______ thread.
People are often cruel and unfeeling, love is torturous–in general, the things of the material world cause suffering.
There is often a happy ending, but it’s not conventionally happy.
Characters are rewarded, but only after they manage (often through death) to transcend the rigors of the mortal world.
1. talk , interact , play , influence
2. react , related , reimburse , relevant
3. simulate , stimulate , strike , stipulate
4. nervous , shamed , awkward , harmful
5. gifts , occasions , presents , treasures
6. harmful , thoughtful , painful , colorful
questions.answer:
1. interact
2. related
3. strike
4. awkward
5. gifts

sense_groups.english: Like Lewis Carroll (and, to a lesser extent, Kenneth Grahame),

sense_groups.english: Most everyone has read or at least knows the titles of many of Andersen’s works:

sense_groups.chinese: 因为总有一天你会发现自己的特殊天赋。

sense_groups.english: A closer, deeper look at many of Andersen’s tales
sense_groups.chinese: 对安徒生的许多童话进行更仔细、更深入的审视，

sense_groups.english: (including “The Ugly Duckling,” which is not on our reading list),
sense_groups.chinese: （包括不在我们阅读清单上的《丑小鸭》），

sense_groups.chinese: 揭示了一条更黑暗、更艰难、更痛苦的主线。

sense_groups.english: People are often cruel and unfeeling, love is torturous–
sense_groups.chinese: 人们常常残忍无情，爱是折磨人的——

sense_groups.chinese: 总的来说，物质世界的事物带来痛苦。

sense_groups.english: There is often a happy ending, but it’s not conventionally happy.
sense_groups.chinese: 通常会有幸福的结局，但并非传统意义上的幸福。

sense_groups.english: Characters are rewarded,
sense_groups.chinese: 角色得到回报，

sense_groups.chinese: 但只有当他们（通常通过死亡）超越尘世的严酷之后才得以实现。

questions.name: #573 Medalists
questions.en:
In an often-cited study about counterfactuals, Medvec, Madey, and Gilovich (1995) found that bronze medalists appeared happier than silver medalists in television coverage of the 1992 Summer Olympics.
Medvec et al ______ that bronze medalists compared themselves to 4th place finishers, ______ silver medalists compared themselves to gold medalists.
These counterfactuals were the most ______ because they were either qualitatively different (gold vs silver) or categorically different (medal vs no medal) from what ______ occurred.
Drawing on archival data and experimental studies, we show that Olympic athletes (among others) are more likely to make counterfactual comparisons based on their ______ expectations, consistent with decision affect theory.
Silver medalists are more likely to be disappointed because their personal expectations are higher than ______ of bronze medalists.
1. argued , questioned , persuaded , flighted
2. whereabouts , wherever , whatsoever , whereas
3. advantaged , outperformed , salient , worried
4. playfully , finally , actually , totally
5. after , last , before , prior
6. that , these , those , this
questions.answer:
1. argued
2. whereas
3. salient
4. actually
5. prior
6. those
questions.full:
In an often-cited study about counterfactuals, Medvec, Madey, and Gilovich (1995) found that bronze medalists appeared happier than silver medalists in television coverage of the 1992 Summer Olympics.
Medvec et al ______ that bronze medalists compared themselves to 4th place finishers, ______ silver medalists compared themselves to gold medalists.
These counterfactuals were the most ______ because they were either qualitatively different (gold vs silver) or categorically different (medal vs no medal) from what ______ occurred.
Drawing on archival data and experimental studies, we show that Olympic athletes (among others) are more likely to make counterfactual comparisons based on their ______ expectations, consistent with decision affect theory.
Silver medalists are more likely to be disappointed because their personal expectations are higher than ______ of bronze medalists.

1. argued , questioned , persuaded , flighted
2. whereabouts , wherever , whatsoever , whereas
3. advantaged , outperformed , salient , worried
4. playfully , finally , actually , totally
5. after , last , before , prior
6. that , these , those , this

答案:
1. argued
2. whereas
3. salient
4. actually
5. prior
6. those

sense_groups.english: In an often-cited study about counterfactuals, Medvec, Madey, and Gilovich (1995) found that bronze medalists appeared happier than silver medalists in television coverage of the 1992 Summer Olympics.
sense_groups.chinese: 在一项关于反事实思维的常被引用的研究中，Medvec、Madey 和 Gilovich（1995）发现，在1992年夏季奥运会的电视报道中，铜牌得主看起来比银牌得主更开心。

sense_groups.english: Medvec et al argued that bronze medalists compared themselves to 4th place finishers, whereas silver medalists compared themselves to gold medalists.
sense_groups.chinese: Medvec 等人认为，铜牌得主将自己与第四名进行比较，而银牌得主则将自己与金牌得主进行比较。

sense_groups.english: These counterfactuals were the most salient because they were either qualitatively different (gold vs silver) or categorically different (medal vs no medal) from what actually occurred.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些反事实思维最为显著，因为它们要么在质量上不同（金牌与银牌），要么在类别上不同（有奖牌与无奖牌），与实际发生的情况不同。

sense_groups.english: Drawing on archival data and experimental studies, we show that Olympic athletes (among others) are more likely to make counterfactual comparisons based on their prior expectations, consistent with decision affect theory.
sense_groups.chinese: 利用档案数据和实验研究，我们表明奥运运动员（以及其他人群）更倾向于根据他们先前的期望进行反事实比较，这与决策情感理论一致。

sense_groups.english: Silver medalists are more likely to be disappointed because their personal expectations are higher than those of bronze medalists.
sense_groups.chinese: 银牌得主更可能感到失望，因为他们的个人期望高于铜牌得主。

questions.name: #574 Video Conference
questions.en:
Never has the carbon footprint of multi-national corporations been under such intense scrutiny.
Inter-city train journeys and long-haul flights to ______ face-to-face business meetings contribute significantly to greenhouse gases and the resulting ______ on the environment.
The Anglo-US company Teliris has introduced a new video-conferencing technology and partnered with the Carbon Neutral Company, enabling corporate outfits to become more environmentally responsible.
The innovation allows simulated face-to-face meetings to be held across continents without the time ______ or environmental burden of international travel.
Previous designs have enabled video-conferencing on a point-to-point, dual-location basis.
The firm's VirtuaLive technology, however, can bring people together from up to five ______ locations anywhere in the world - with ______ transmission quality.
1. create , conduct , produce , generate
2. gases , strain , affect , steam
3. pressure , limit , stress , press
4. separate , each , single , respectively
5. unreasonable , unrealistic , unreliable , unrivaled
questions.full:

Inter-city train journeys and long-haul flights to ______ face-to-face business meetings contribute significantly to greenhouse gases and the resulting ______ on the environment.

Previous designs have enabled video-conferencing on a point-to-point, dual-location basis.

1. create , conduct , produce , generate
2. gases , strain , affect , steam
3. pressure , limit , stress , press
4. separate , each , single , respectively

答案:

2. strain

sense_groups.english: Never has the carbon footprint of multi-national corporations been under such intense scrutiny.
sense_groups.chinese: 跨国公司的碳足迹从未受到如此严格的审查。

sense_groups.english: Inter-city train journeys and long-haul flights to conduct face-to-face business meetings contribute significantly to greenhouse gases
sense_groups.chinese: 为进行面对面商务会议而进行的城际火车旅行和长途航班，对温室气体排放贡献巨大，

sense_groups.english: and the resulting strain on the environment.
sense_groups.chinese: 并由此对环境造成压力。

sense_groups.english: The Anglo-US company Teliris has introduced a new video-conferencing technology
sense_groups.chinese: 英美公司Teliris推出了一项新的视频会议技术，

sense_groups.english: and partnered with the Carbon Neutral Company,
sense_groups.chinese: 并与碳中和公司合作，

sense_groups.english: enabling corporate outfits to become more environmentally responsible.
sense_groups.chinese: 使企业组织能够更加环保。

sense_groups.english: The innovation allows simulated face-to-face meetings to be held across continents
sense_groups.chinese: 这项创新允许跨大洲举行模拟面对面会议，

sense_groups.english: without the time pressure or environmental burden of international travel.
sense_groups.chinese: 无需承受国际旅行的时间压力或环境负担。

sense_groups.english: Previous designs have enabled video-conferencing on a point-to-point, dual-location basis.
sense_groups.chinese: 以往的设计只能实现点对点、双地点的视频会议。

sense_groups.english: The firm's VirtuaLive technology, however, can bring people together from up to five separate locations anywhere in the world
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，该公司的VirtuaLive技术可以将来自全球多达五个不同地点的人们聚集在一起，

questions.name: #575 Natural Capital
questions.en:
Capital has often been thought of narrowly as physical capital — the machines, tools, and equipment used in the production of other goods, but our wealth and wellbeing also ______ ______ natural capital.
If we forget this, we risk degrading the services that natural ecosystems provide, which ______ our economies and sustain our lives.
These services include purifying our water, ______ our climate, reducing flood risk, and pollinating our crops.
The Natural Capital Project — a partnership ______ WWF, The Nature Conservancy, University of Minnesota and Stanford University — works to provide decision makers with ______ ways to assess the true value of the services that ecosystems provide.
An essential element of the Natural Capital Project is developing tools that help decision makers protect biodiversity and ecosystem services.
1. brings about , relies on , adds to , derives from
2. damage , champion , defend , support
3. guiding , diminishing , denying , regulating
4. liable , strong , powerful , reliable
questions.answer:
1. relies
2. on
3. support
4. regulating
5. among
6. reliable
questions.full:
Capital has often been thought of narrowly as physical capital — the machines, tools, and equipment used in the production of other goods, but our wealth and wellbeing also ______ ______ natural capital.
If we forget this, we risk degrading the services that natural ecosystems provide, which ______ our economies and sustain our lives.
These services include purifying our water, ______ our climate, reducing flood risk, and pollinating our crops.
The Natural Capital Project — a partnership ______ WWF, The Nature Conservancy, University of Minnesota and Stanford University — works to provide decision makers with ______ ways to assess the true value of the services that ecosystems provide.
An essential element of the Natural Capital Project is developing tools that help decision makers protect biodiversity and ecosystem services.

1. brings about , relies on , adds to , derives from
2. damage , champion , defend , support
3. guiding , diminishing , denying , regulating
4. liable , strong , powerful , reliable

答案:
1. relies
2. on
3. support
4. regulating
5. among
6. reliable

sense_groups.english: Capital has often been thought of narrowly as physical capital — the machines, tools, and equipment used in the production of other goods,
sense_groups.chinese: 资本通常被狭义地理解为物质资本——用于生产其他商品的机器、工具和设备，

sense_groups.english: but our wealth and wellbeing also relies on natural capital.
sense_groups.chinese: 但我们的财富和福祉也依赖于自然资本。

sense_groups.english: If we forget this, we risk degrading the services that natural ecosystems provide, which support our economies and sustain our lives.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果我们忘记这一点，我们就有可能破坏自然生态系统提供的服务，这些服务支撑着我们的经济并维持着我们的生活。

sense_groups.english: These services include purifying our water, regulating our climate, reducing flood risk, and pollinating our crops.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些服务包括净化我们的水源、调节气候、减少洪水风险以及为农作物授粉。

sense_groups.english: The Natural Capital Project — a partnership among WWF, The Nature Conservancy, University of Minnesota and Stanford University — works to provide decision makers with reliable ways to assess the true value of the services that ecosystems provide.
sense_groups.chinese: 自然资本项目——由世界自然基金会、大自然保护协会、明尼苏达大学和斯坦福大学合作——致力于为决策者提供可靠的方法来评估生态系统服务的真实价值。

sense_groups.english: An essential element of the Natural Capital Project is developing tools that help decision makers protect biodiversity and ecosystem services.
sense_groups.chinese: 自然资本项目的一个关键要素是开发工具，帮助决策者保护生物多样性和生态系统服务。

questions.name: #576 Teen Writing
questions.en:
Teens write for a variety of reasons—as part of a school assignment, to ______ a good grade, to stay in touch with friends, to share their artistic creations with others or simply to put their thoughts to paper (whether virtual or otherwise).
In our focus groups, teens said they are motivated to write when they can ______ topics that are relevant to their lives and interests, and report greater enjoyment of school writing when they have the opportunity to write creatively.
Having teachers or other adults who challenge them, ______ them with interesting curricula and give them detailed feedback also serves as a motivator for teens.
Teens also ______ writing for an audience motivates them to write and write well.
1. get , skip , maintain , avoid
2. debate , communicate , use , select
3. meet , educate , present , introduce
4. regard , learn , report , provide
questions.full:
Teens write for a variety of reasons—as part of a school assignment, to ______ a good grade, to stay in touch with friends, to share their artistic creations with others or simply to put their thoughts to paper (whether virtual or otherwise).
In our focus groups, teens said they are motivated to write when they can ______ topics that are relevant to their lives and interests, and report greater enjoyment of school writing when they have the opportunity to write creatively.
Having teachers or other adults who challenge them, ______ them with interesting curricula and give them detailed feedback also serves as a motivator for teens.
Teens also ______ writing for an audience motivates them to write and write well.

1. get , skip , maintain , avoid
2. debate , communicate , use , select
3. meet , educate , present , introduce
4. regard , learn , report , provide

答案:
1. get
2. select
3. present
4. report

sense_groups.english: Teens write for a variety of reasons—as part of a school assignment, to get a good grade, to stay in touch with friends, to share their artistic creations with others or simply to put their thoughts to paper (whether virtual or otherwise).
sense_groups.chinese: 青少年写作的原因多种多样——作为学校作业的一部分，为了获得好成绩，为了与朋友保持联系，为了与他人分享他们的艺术创作，或者仅仅是为了将他们的想法写在纸上（无论是虚拟的还是其他形式）。

sense_groups.english: In our focus groups, teens said they are motivated to write when they can select topics that are relevant to their lives and interests, and report greater enjoyment of school writing when they have the opportunity to write creatively.
sense_groups.chinese: 在我们的焦点小组中，青少年表示，当他们能够选择与自己生活和兴趣相关的主题时，他们会更有动力写作，并且当有机会进行创造性写作时，他们对学校写作的 enjoyment 更高。

sense_groups.english: Having teachers or other adults who challenge them, present them with interesting curricula and give them detailed feedback also serves as a motivator for teens.
sense_groups.chinese: 拥有挑战他们、向他们呈现有趣课程并给予详细反馈的老师或其他成年人，也是青少年的动力来源。

sense_groups.english: Teens also report writing for an audience motivates them to write and write well.
sense_groups.chinese: 青少年还报告说，为读者写作能激励他们写作并写得更好。

questions.name: #577 Enough Exercise
questions.en:
One thing is certain.
Most people do not get enough exercise in their ______ routines.

3. need , demanding , pushing , supplying
4. few , many , much , several

Satisfying this need requires a sustainable plan and a commitment.

sense_groups.chinese: 大多数人在日常生活中没有得到足够的锻炼。

sense_groups.chinese: 现代技术的所有进步——从电动开罐器到动力转向——都让生活更轻松、更舒适，并且体力要求大大降低。

questions.name: #578 Good Schools

questions.name: #579 Settlement
questions.en:
Over the last ten thousand years there seem to have been two separate and conflicting building sentiments throughout the history of towns and cities.
  ______ is the desire to start again, for a variety of reasons: an earthquake or a tidal wave may have demolished the settlement, or fire destroyed it, or the new city ______ a new political beginning.
The other can be likened to the effect of a magnet: established settlements attract people, who ______ ______ come whether or not there is any planning for their arrival.
The clash between these two sentiments is evident in every established city ______ its development has been almost completely accidental or is lost in history.
Incidentally, many settlements have been planned from the beginning but, for a variety of reasons, no settlement followed the plan.
A good example is Currowan, on the Clyde River in New South Wales, which ______ ______ in the second half of the 19th century, in expectation that people would come to establish agriculture and a small port.
But no one came.
1. It , What , One , That
2. highlights , starts , marks , protrudes
3. hesitate , ought , turn , tend
4. whereas , whatever , if , unless
5. has been surveyed , had surveyed , be surveyed , was surveyed
questions.answer:
1. One
2. marks
3. tend
4. to
5. unless
6. was
7. surveyed

Over the last ten thousand years there seem to have been two separate and conflicting building sentiments throughout the history of towns and cities.

sense_groups.english: Over the last ten thousand years there seem to have been two separate and conflicting building sentiments throughout the history of towns and cities.
sense_groups.chinese: 在过去一万年里，城镇和城市的历史中似乎存在着两种分离且相互冲突的建设理念。

sense_groups.english: One is the desire to start again, for a variety of reasons: an earthquake or a tidal wave may have demolished the settlement, or fire destroyed it, or the new city marks a new political beginning.
sense_groups.chinese: 一种是重新开始的愿望，原因多种多样：地震或海啸可能摧毁了定居点，或者火灾将其烧毁，或者新城市标志着一个新的政治开端。

sense_groups.english: The other can be likened to the effect of a magnet: established settlements attract people, who tend to come whether or not there is any planning for their arrival.
sense_groups.chinese: 另一种可以比作磁铁效应：已有的定居点吸引人们，无论是否有计划，人们往往都会来。

sense_groups.english: The clash between these two sentiments is evident in every established city unless its development has been almost completely accidental or is lost in history.
sense_groups.chinese: 这两种理念之间的冲突在每个已建立的城市中都很明显，除非其发展几乎完全是偶然的或已消失在历史中。

sense_groups.english: Incidentally, many settlements have been planned from the beginning but, for a variety of reasons, no settlement followed the plan.
sense_groups.chinese: 顺便提一下，许多定居点从一开始就有规划，但由于各种原因，没有一个定居点遵循了规划。

sense_groups.english: A good example is Currowan, on the Clyde River in New South Wales, which was surveyed in the second half of the 19th century, in expectation that people would come to establish agriculture and a small port.
sense_groups.chinese: 一个很好的例子是新南威尔士州克莱德河畔的卡罗万，它在19世纪下半叶被勘测，期望人们会来建立农业和一个小港口。

sense_groups.english: But no one came.
sense_groups.chinese: 但没有人来。

questions.name: #580 Higher Education Funding
questions.en:
Financing of Australian higher education has undergone dramatic ______ since the early 1970s.
Although the Australian Government provided regular funding for universities from the late 1950s, in 1974 it ______ full responsibility for funding higher education — abolishing tuition fees with the intention of making university education affordable to all Australians who had the ability and who wished to participate in higher education.
Since the late 1980s, there has been a move towards greater private contributions, ______ student fees.
In 1989, the Australian Government introduced the Higher Education Contribution Scheme (HECS) which included a loans scheme to help students finance their contributions.
This enabled university to remain ______ to students by delaying their payments until they could afford to pay off their loans.
In 2002, the Australian Government ______ a scheme similar to HECS for postgraduate students - the Postgraduate Education Loan Scheme (PELS).
Funding for higher education comes from various sources.
This article examines the three main sources - Australian Government funding, student fees and charges, and HECS.
While the proportion of total ______ raised through HECS is relatively small, HECS payments are a significant component of students' university costs, with many students carrying a HECS debt for several years after leaving university.
This article also focuses on characteristics of university students based on their HECS liability status, and the level of accumulated HECS debt.
1. change , appeal , exhaustion , plateau
2. assumed , subsumed , presumed , consumed
3. without , automatically , with , particularly
4. access , inaccessible , accessibility , accessible
5. produced , carried , remembered , introduced
6. expenses , expenditure , profit , revenue
questions.answer:
1. change
2. assumed
3. particularly
4. accessible
5. introduced
6. revenue

sense_groups.english: Financing of Australian higher education has undergone dramatic change since the early 1970s.
sense_groups.chinese: 自20世纪70年代初以来，澳大利亚高等教育的融资经历了巨大变化。

sense_groups.english: Although the Australian Government provided regular funding for universities from the late 1950s,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管澳大利亚政府从20世纪50年代末开始为大学提供定期资助，

sense_groups.english: in 1974 it assumed full responsibility for funding higher education
sense_groups.chinese: 但在1974年，它承担了资助高等教育的全部责任

sense_groups.english: — abolishing tuition fees with the intention of making university education affordable to all Australians who had the ability and who wished to participate in higher education.
sense_groups.chinese: ——取消学费，旨在让所有有能力且希望接受高等教育的澳大利亚人都能负担得起大学教育。

sense_groups.english: Since the late 1980s, there has been a move towards greater private contributions, particularly student fees.
sense_groups.chinese: 自20世纪80年代末以来，出现了向更多私人贡献转变的趋势，尤其是学生学费。

sense_groups.english: In 1989, the Australian Government introduced the Higher Education Contribution Scheme (HECS) which included a loans scheme to help students finance their contributions.
sense_groups.chinese: 1989年，澳大利亚政府推出了高等教育贡献计划（HECS），其中包括一项贷款计划，以帮助学生为其贡献提供资金。

sense_groups.english: This enabled university to remain accessible to students by delaying their payments until they could afford to pay off their loans.
sense_groups.chinese: 这使得大学对学生保持可及性，将付款推迟到他们有能力偿还贷款为止。

sense_groups.english: In 2002, the Australian Government introduced a scheme similar to HECS for postgraduate students - the Postgraduate Education Loan Scheme (PELS).
sense_groups.chinese: 2002年，澳大利亚政府为研究生推出了一项类似于HECS的计划——研究生教育贷款计划（PELS）。

sense_groups.english: Funding for higher education comes from various sources.
sense_groups.chinese: 高等教育的资金来自多种来源。

sense_groups.english: This article examines the three main sources - Australian Government funding, student fees and charges, and HECS.
sense_groups.chinese: 本文考察了三个主要来源——澳大利亚政府资助、学生费用和收费，以及HECS。

sense_groups.english: While the proportion of total revenue raised through HECS is relatively small,
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然通过HECS筹集的总收入比例相对较小，

sense_groups.english: HECS payments are a significant component of students' university costs,
sense_groups.chinese: 但HECS付款是学生大学成本的重要组成部分，

sense_groups.english: with many students carrying a HECS debt for several years after leaving university.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多学生在离开大学后多年仍背负着HECS债务。

sense_groups.english: This article also focuses on characteristics of university students based on their HECS liability status, and the level of accumulated HECS debt.
sense_groups.chinese: 本文还关注基于HECS负债状况的大学生特征，以及累积的HECS债务水平。

questions.en:

sense_groups.chinese: 组织需要更紧密地整合其销售活动，既要在内部协调，也要与客户需求对接

questions.name: #582 Economics
questions.en:
Economics is the study of choices.
Though some believe that economics is driven purely by money or capital, the choice is much more ______ .
If the study of economics is the study of how people choose to use their resources, analysts must also consider all of their possible resources, of which money is but one.
In practice, resources can ______ everything from time to knowledge and property to tools.
As such, economics helps illustrate how people interact within the market to ______ their diverse goals.
Beyond defining what these resources are, the concept of scarcity is also an important consideration.
These resources — no matter how broad the category — are limited, which is the source of tension in the choices people and society make: Their decisions are a result of the ______ tug of war between unlimited wants and desires and limited resources.
1. discursive , permissive , expansive , expensive
2. trespass , surpass , debate , encompass
3. idolize , realize , utilize , finalize
4. resonant , extant , blatant , constant
questions.full:
Economics is the study of choices.
Though some believe that economics is driven purely by money or capital, the choice is much more ______ .

As such, economics helps illustrate how people interact within the market to ______ their diverse goals.
Beyond defining what these resources are, the concept of scarcity is also an important consideration.
These resources — no matter how broad the category — are limited, which is the source of tension in the choices people and society make: Their decisions are a result of the ______ tug of war between unlimited wants and desires and limited resources.

1. discursive , permissive , expansive , expensive
2. trespass , surpass , debate , encompass

2. encompass
3. realize
4. constant

sense_groups.english: Economics is the study of choices.
sense_groups.chinese: 经济学是研究选择的学科。

sense_groups.english: Though some believe that economics is driven purely by money or capital,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管有些人认为经济学纯粹由金钱或资本驱动，

sense_groups.english: the choice is much more expansive.
sense_groups.chinese: 但选择要广泛得多。

sense_groups.english: If the study of economics is the study of how people choose to use their resources,
sense_groups.chinese: 如果经济学研究的是人们如何选择使用资源，

sense_groups.english: analysts must also consider all of their possible resources,
sense_groups.chinese: 分析者还必须考虑所有可能的资源，

sense_groups.english: of which money is but one.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中金钱只是其中之一。

sense_groups.english: In practice, resources can encompass everything from time to knowledge and property to tools.
sense_groups.chinese: 实际上，资源可以涵盖从时间到知识、从财产到工具的一切。

sense_groups.english: As such, economics helps illustrate how people interact within the market to realize their diverse goals.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，经济学有助于说明人们如何在市场中互动以实现各自不同的目标。

sense_groups.english: Beyond defining what these resources are,
sense_groups.chinese: 除了定义这些资源是什么，

sense_groups.english: the concept of scarcity is also an important consideration.
sense_groups.chinese: 稀缺性的概念也是一个重要的考量因素。

sense_groups.english: These resources — no matter how broad the category — are limited,
sense_groups.chinese: 这些资源——无论类别多么广泛——都是有限的，

sense_groups.english: which is the source of tension in the choices people and society make:
sense_groups.chinese: 这是人们和社会做出选择时紧张的根源：

sense_groups.english: Their decisions are a result of the constant tug of war between unlimited wants and desires and limited resources.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们的决定是无限欲望与有限资源之间持续拉锯的结果。

questions.name: #583 Wine and Ale
questions.en:
By the Bronze Age drinking ______ were being made of sheet metal, primarily bronze or gold.
However, the peak of feasting – and in particular, of the “political” type of feast came in the late Hallstatt period (about 600 – 450 BC), soon after the foundation of the Greek ______ of Massalia (Marseille) at the mouth of the Rhine.
From that date on, the blood of the grape began to make its way north and east along major river systems together with imported metal and ceramic drinking vessels from the Greek world.
  ______ was thus added to the list of mood- altering beverages – such as mead and ale available to establish social networks in Iron Age Europe.
Attic pottery fragments found at hillforts such as Heuneburg in Germany and ______ goods such as the monumental 5th century Greek bronze krater found at Vix in Burgundy supply archaeological evidence of this interaction.
Organic ______ such as leather or wooden wine barrels may also have travelled north into Europe but have not survived.
It is unknown what goods were ______ in return, but they may have included salted meat, hides, timber, amber and slaves.
1. vehicles , boats , vessels , ships
2. group , jungle , colony , place
3. Alcohol , Sugar , Wine , Foam
4. solid , mortgage , luxury , disgusting
5. content , market , places , containers
6. changed , bought , made , traded
questions.answer:
1. vessels
2. colony
3. Wine
4. luxury
5. containers
6. traded

sense_groups.chinese: 到了青铜时代，饮酒器皿开始用金属片制成，主要是青铜或黄金。

sense_groups.english: However, the peak of feasting – and in particular, of the “political” type of feast came in the late Hallstatt period (about 600 – 450 BC), soon after the foundation of the Greek colony of Massalia (Marseille) at the mouth of the Rhine.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，宴饮的顶峰——尤其是“政治”型宴饮——出现在哈尔施塔特晚期（约公元前600-450年），就在希腊殖民地马萨利亚（马赛）在莱茵河口建立后不久。

2. As

sense_groups.chinese: “kariya”女性指的是职业女性，而“manshon”则是指公寓。

sense_groups.chinese: 因此，一个政府小组提议出版一本关于如何说规范日语的手册。

sense_groups.chinese: 在日本，一个“kuru”的人是指冷静且从不生气的人。

sense_groups.english: On the other hand, someone who is kakkoii is hip, or in translation, "cool."

sense_groups.chinese: 类似地，一个“hotto”的人容易兴奋，也许充满激情，但不一定是当下受欢迎的人或个性。

questions.name: #607 Jack Lewis
questions.en:
S. Lewis, or Jack Lewis, as he preferred to be called, was born in Belfast, Ireland (now Northern Ireland) on November 29, 1898.
He was the second son of Albert Lewis, a lawyer, and Flora Hamilton Lewis.
His older brother, Warren Hamilton Lewis, who was known as Warnie, had been born three years ______ in 1895.
Lewis's early childhood was relatively happy and carefree.
In those days Northern Ireland was not yet ______ by bitter civil strife, and the Lewises were comfortably off.
The family home, called Little Lea, was a large, gabled house with dark, narrow passages and an overgrown garden, which Warnie and Jack played in and ______ together.
There was also a library that was crammed with books - two of Jack's favorites were Treasure Island by Robert Louis Stevenson and The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett.
This somewhat idyllic boyhood came to an end for Lewis when his mother became ill and died of cancer in 1908.
Barely a month after her death the two boys were sent away from home to go to boarding school in England.
Lewis hated the school, with its strict rules and hard, ______ headmaster, and he missed Belfast terribly.
Fortunately for him, the school closed in 1910, and he was able to return to Ireland.
After a year, however, he was sent back to England to study.
This time, the ______ proved to be mostly positive.
As a teenager, Lewis learned to love poetry, especially the works of Virgil and Homer.
He also ______ an interest in modern languages, mastering French, German, and Italian.
1. early , earlier , older , later
2. experienced , happened , survived , plagued
3. studied , quarreled , explored , implored
4. systematic , unsympathetic , professional , synchronized
5. experiment , experience , problem , mystery
6. forsook , developed , engaged , misled
questions.answer:
1. earlier
2. plagued
3. explored
4. unsympathetic
5. experience
6. developed

questions.name: #608 Defining Work
questions.en:

In larger traditional societies, carpentry, stonemasonry, and shipbuilding are also prominent.
In modern societies where industrial development exists, people work in a much wider variety of occupations.

sense_groups.english: Work, in sociology, is defined as the carrying out of tasks, which involves the expenditure of mental and physical effort, and its objective is the production of goods and services that cater to human needs.

sense_groups.chinese: 职业或工作，是为了换取固定工资或薪水而进行的工作。

questions.name: #610 Happy
questions.en:
Want to know what will make you happy?
Then ask a total stranger — or so says a new study from Harvard University, which shows that another person’s experience is often more ______ than your own best guess.
The study, which appears in the current issue of Science, was led by Daniel Gilbert, professor of psychology at Harvard and author of the 2007 bestseller “Stumbling on Happiness,” along with Matthew Killingsworth and Rebecca Eyre, also of Harvard, and Timothy Wilson of the University of Virginia.
“If you want to know how much you will enjoy an experience, you are better off knowing how much someone else enjoyed it than knowing anything about the experience itself,” says Gilbert.
“Rather than closing our eyes and ______ the future, we should examine the experience of those who have been there.
Previous research in psychology, neuroscience, and behavioral economics ______ ______ that people have difficulty predicting what they will like and how much they will like it, which ______ them to make a wide variety of poor decisions.
Interventions aimed at ______ the accuracy with which people imagine future events have been generally unsuccessful.
1. predictable , informative , positive , informal
2. imagining , approaching , imitating , staging
3. has shown , have shown , showing , shown
4. leads , forces , compels , requires
5. improving , reducing , implying , controlling
questions.answer:
1. informative
2. imagining
3. has
4. shown
5. leads
6. improving

questions.name: #611 Canadian Arctic
questions.en:

However, it was difficult to get the dose right and could kill some people ______ ______ the effect on their heart.

3. has transported , was transported , transported , have transported

2. remained

4. transported

questions.name: #613 EE and AVG
questions.en:
Currently, there is concern about the increasing amount of time children spend engaged in sedentary activities, the number of children who fail to achieve minimum daily physical activity guidelines (i.e. 60 min of moderate-to-vigorous intensity activities every day), and the apparent increase in obesity prevalence as a result of such sedentary behaviors .
Screen-based activities, including television viewing and playing computer games, are ______ of the most frequently observed sedentary activities that children partake with children spending 2.5–4 h per day participating in such activities.
The introduction of “active video games” (AVGs) into the gaming market presents an opportunity to convert traditional, sedentary screen-time into active screen-time and thus increases total daily energy expenditure (EE).
Modern AVGs utilize cameras and motion sensors to allow the gamer to physically perform a variety of actions, dependent on the console, such as swinging a tennis racquet or running.
The most demanding AVGs provided similar responses to walking and, based on international standards, should be classified as low-intensity activities.
Whilst AVGs may provide children with a better alternative to sedentary gaming, they are not a sufficient ______ for normal physical activity, e.g. sports and outdoor play.
1. wasted , prevailing , engaged , being
2. maximum , mini , minimum , enough
3. connectivity , position , behaviors , stuff
4. relative , independent , dependent , part
5. consumption , employment , replacement , analogy

Screen-based activities, including television viewing and playing computer games, are ______ of the most frequently observed sedentary activities that children partake with children spending 2.5–4 h per day participating in such activities.

The most demanding AVGs provided similar responses to walking and, based on international standards, should be classified as low-intensity activities.

sense_groups.chinese: 未能达到每日最低体力活动指南（即每天60分钟中高强度活动）的儿童数量，

sense_groups.english: and the apparent increase in obesity prevalence as a result of such sedentary behaviors .
sense_groups.chinese: 以及由于这些久坐行为导致的肥胖率明显上升。

sense_groups.english: Screen-based activities, including television viewing and playing computer games, are part of the most frequently observed sedentary activities that children partake with children spending 2.5–4 h per day participating in such activities.
sense_groups.chinese: 屏幕活动，包括看电视和玩电脑游戏，是儿童最常见的久坐活动之一，儿童每天花2.5到4小时参与这些活动。

sense_groups.chinese: “主动视频游戏”（AVGs）进入游戏市场，为将传统的久坐屏幕时间转化为活跃屏幕时间提供了机会，从而增加每日总能量消耗。

But they do have industrial applications and were used in the drill bits that helped dig the Panama Canal.
Now a team led by Stephen Haggerty of Florida International University in Miami has presented a new study ______ that the odd stones were brought to Earth by an asteroid billions of years ago.

The test revealed the presence of many hydrogen-carbon bonds, indicating that the diamonds probably formed in a hydrogen-rich environment—such as that found in space.

"They're not ______ ,” Haggerty said, "but they're very similar." Astrophysicists, he added, have developed theories predicting that Nano diamonds form easily in the titanic stellar explosions called supernovas, which scatter debris through interstellar space.
The deposits in the Central African Republic and Brazil, he said, probably come from the impact of a diamond-rich asteroid billions of years ago, when South America and Africa were joined.

questions.name: #640 Debtor
questions.en:
There isn’t a financial director around who wouldn’t like to ______ cash flow by reducing debtor days- in other words, get customers to pay up faster.
In Europe’s top 1,000 quoted companies, nearly one quarter of all invoices are unpaid at any ______ in time, according to recent research carried out by the ASF organization.

2. point

4. fail
5. This
6. is

questions.name: #641 History of Sociology

It ______ in the early 19th century in response to the challenges of modernity.
Increasing mobility and technological advances resulted in the increasing ______ of people to cultures and societies different from their own.
The impact of this exposure was varied, but for some people, it included the breakdown of traditional norms and customs and ______ a revised understanding of how the world works.
Sociologists responded to these changes by trying to understand what holds social groups together and also to explore possible solutions to the breakdown of social solidarity.
Thinkers of the Enlightenment period in the 18th century also helped set the ______ for the sociologists who would follow.
This period was the first time in history that thinkers tried to provide general explanations of the social world.

3. unwarranted , transplanted , warranted , implanted

questions.name: #643 Opportunity Cost
questions.en:
Opportunity cost incorporates the notion of scarcity: No matter what we do, there is always a trade-off.
We must trade off one thing for another because resources are limited and can be used in different ways.
  ______ ______ ______ , we use up resources that could have been used to acquire something else.
The ______ of opportunity cost allows us to measure this tradeoff.
Most decisions ______ several alternatives.
For example, if you spend an hour studying for an economics exam, you have one fewer hour to pursue other activities.
To determine the opportunity cost of an activity, we look at what you consider the best of these 'other' activities.
For example, suppose the alternatives to studying economics are studying for a history exam or working in a job that pays $10 per hour.
If you consider studying for history a ______ use of your time than working, then the opportunity cost of studying economics is the four extra points you could have received on a history exam if you studied history instead of economics.
Alternatively, if working is the best alternative, the opportunity cost of studying economics is the $10 you could have earned instead.
1. Despite spending nothing , By not acquiring something , By acquiring something , Upon sustaining anything
2. image , use , notion , strategy
3. involved , have involved , involve , had involved
4. better , worst , best , worse
questions.answer:
1. By
2. acquiring
3. something
4. notion
5. involve
6. better

We must trade off one thing for another because resources are limited and can be used in different ways.
  ______ ______ ______ , we use up resources that could have been used to acquire something else.

Alternatively, if working is the best alternative, the opportunity cost of studying economics is the $10 you could have earned instead.

1. Despite spending nothing , By not acquiring something , By acquiring something , Upon sustaining anything
2. image , use , notion , strategy

4. better , worst , best , worse

答案:
1. By
2. acquiring
3. something
4. notion
5. involve
6. better

sense_groups.english: Opportunity cost incorporates the notion of scarcity:
sense_groups.chinese: 机会成本包含了稀缺性的概念：

sense_groups.english: No matter what we do, there is always a trade-off.
sense_groups.chinese: 无论我们做什么，总是存在权衡。

sense_groups.english: We must trade off one thing for another because resources are limited and can be used in different ways.
sense_groups.chinese: 我们必须用一样东西换取另一样，因为资源有限且可以用于不同用途。

sense_groups.english: By acquiring something, we use up resources that could have been used to acquire something else.
sense_groups.chinese: 通过获得某物，我们用掉了本可用于获得其他东西的资源。

sense_groups.english: The notion of opportunity cost allows us to measure this tradeoff.
sense_groups.chinese: 机会成本的概念使我们能够衡量这种权衡。

sense_groups.english: Most decisions involve several alternatives.
sense_groups.chinese: 大多数决策涉及多个备选方案。

sense_groups.english: For example, if you spend an hour studying for an economics exam, you have one fewer hour to pursue other activities.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，如果你花一小时准备经济学考试，你就少了一小时去做其他活动。

sense_groups.english: To determine the opportunity cost of an activity, we look at what you consider the best of these 'other' activities.
sense_groups.chinese: 要确定一项活动的机会成本，我们看你认为这些“其他”活动中最好的那个。

sense_groups.english: For example, suppose the alternatives to studying economics are studying for a history exam or working in a job that pays $10 per hour.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，假设学习经济学的替代方案是准备历史考试或做一份每小时10美元的工作。

sense_groups.english: If you consider studying for history a better use of your time than working, then the opportunity cost of studying economics is the four extra points you could have received on a history exam if you studied history instead of economics.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你认为学习历史比工作更能利用时间，那么学习经济学的机会成本就是如果你学习历史而不是经济学，你本可以在历史考试中多得的四分。

sense_groups.english: Alternatively, if working is the best alternative, the opportunity cost of studying economics is the $10 you could have earned instead.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者，如果工作是最好的选择，那么学习经济学的机会成本就是你本可以赚到的10美元。

questions.en:

After all, the users of older and less capable browsers won't know what they are missing.
The ______ ______ to progressive enhancement is the belief among developers and clients that websites should look the same in every browser.

sense_groups.chinese: 它增添了那种让你坐立不安的元素，促使你一直读到故事的高潮。

sense_groups.english: In literature, the rising action encompasses the decisions, background circumstances, and character flaws that lead a story from the opening exposition through the drama and run-up to the climax.
sense_groups.chinese: 在文学中，上升动作包括决定、背景环境和性格缺陷，这些将故事从开头的阐述部分，通过戏剧性发展，一直引向高潮。

sense_groups.english: The primary conflict can be an external one, such as a clash between two men trying to exert their dominance at work, or it can be internal, as in the case of a college student who realizes she wants to leave school but cringes at the thought of telling her parents.
sense_groups.chinese: 主要冲突可以是外部的，比如两个男人试图在工作中展现主导地位而发生的冲突；也可以是内部的，比如一个大学生意识到自己想退学，但一想到要告诉父母就退缩了。

sense_groups.english: As you read a novel, pay attention to clues that predict trouble down the road.
sense_groups.chinese: 当你读小说时，注意那些预示着未来麻烦的线索。

sense_groups.english: It could be anything from the appearance of a character who seems shady and untrustworthy, to the description of a clear morning marred by one dark cloud on the horizon.
sense_groups.chinese: 它可以是任何东西，从出现一个看起来可疑且不可信的角色，到描述一个晴朗的早晨被地平线上的一朵乌云破坏。

questions.name: #651 Dairy-tech
questions.en:
Now, one tech startup wants to take wearables to another market: cows.
The company’s “mooON” device goes around the animal’s leg, and ______ their activity levels.
When cows are sick, they move less, and when they are ovulating, they move more.
Stellapps combines information from the step trackers with data that farmers and vets enter into a smartphone app, which ______ reminders for routine protocols such as vaccinations and artificial insemination.
Healthier cows produce more milk, and by tracking and better managing their animals, so farmers can increase ______ .
In India, Stellapps uses an ultrasonic analyzer to measure the nutritional content of the milk.
At the unit, volume sensors monitor the milk to prevent it from being watered down or stolen, says Mukundan.
From there, the milk is taken to a processing plant to be pasteurized and packaged, or ______ into products like cheese or yogurt.
1. stabilizes , tracks , polls , overwhelms
2. argues , imbues , retrieves , issues
3. fields , infields , yields , heralds
4. contracted , converted , combated , constrained
questions.full:
Now, one tech startup wants to take wearables to another market: cows.
The company’s “mooON” device goes around the animal’s leg, and ______ their activity levels.
When cows are sick, they move less, and when they are ovulating, they move more.
Stellapps combines information from the step trackers with data that farmers and vets enter into a smartphone app, which ______ reminders for routine protocols such as vaccinations and artificial insemination.
Healthier cows produce more milk, and by tracking and better managing their animals, so farmers can increase ______ .
In India, Stellapps uses an ultrasonic analyzer to measure the nutritional content of the milk.
At the unit, volume sensors monitor the milk to prevent it from being watered down or stolen, says Mukundan.
From there, the milk is taken to a processing plant to be pasteurized and packaged, or ______ into products like cheese or yogurt.

1. stabilizes , tracks , polls , overwhelms
2. argues , imbues , retrieves , issues
3. fields , infields , yields , heralds
4. contracted , converted , combated , constrained

答案:
1. tracks
2. issues
3. yields
4. converted

sense_groups.english: Now, one tech startup wants to take wearables to another market: cows.
sense_groups.chinese: 现在，一家科技初创公司想把可穿戴设备带到另一个市场：奶牛。

sense_groups.english: The company’s “mooON” device goes around the animal’s leg, and tracks their activity levels.
sense_groups.chinese: 该公司的“mooON”设备套在动物的腿上，并追踪它们的活动水平。

sense_groups.english: When cows are sick, they move less, and when they are ovulating, they move more.
sense_groups.chinese: 当奶牛生病时，它们活动减少；当它们排卵时，活动增多。

sense_groups.english: Stellapps combines information from the step trackers with data that farmers and vets enter into a smartphone app, which issues reminders for routine protocols such as vaccinations and artificial insemination.
sense_groups.chinese: Stellapps将计步器的信息与农民和兽医输入智能手机应用的数据相结合，该应用会发出常规规程的提醒，比如疫苗接种和人工授精。

sense_groups.english: Healthier cows produce more milk, and by tracking and better managing their animals, so farmers can increase yields.
sense_groups.chinese: 更健康的奶牛产奶更多，通过追踪和更好地管理动物，农民可以提高产量。

sense_groups.english: In India, Stellapps uses an ultrasonic analyzer to measure the nutritional content of the milk.
sense_groups.chinese: 在印度，Stellapps使用超声波分析仪测量牛奶的营养成分。

sense_groups.english: At the unit, volume sensors monitor the milk to prevent it from being watered down or stolen, says Mukundan.
sense_groups.chinese: 在该设备中，体积传感器监控牛奶，防止掺水或被盗，Mukundan说。

sense_groups.english: From there, the milk is taken to a processing plant to be pasteurized and packaged, or converted into products like cheese or yogurt.
sense_groups.chinese: 从那里，牛奶被送到加工厂进行巴氏杀菌和包装，或者转化为奶酪或酸奶等产品。

questions.name: #652 Three Robots
questions.en:
On a field in England, three robots have been given a mission: to find and zap weeds with electricity before planting seeds in the cleared soil.
The robots – named Tom, Dylan and Harry – were developed by Small Robot Company to ______ land of unwanted weeds with minimal use of chemicals and heavy machinery.
Robot Tom can scan 20 hectares (49 acres) a day, collecting data which is then used by Dylan, a “crop-care” robot, to zap weeds.
Then it’s robot Harry’s ______ to plant seeds in the weed-free soil.
Using the full system, once it is up and running, farmers could ______ costs by 40% and chemical usage by up to 95%.
“But you have to ______ in mind we only have to go into the parts of the field where the weeds are.” Plants that are neutral or beneficial to the crops are left untouched.
1. rip , rid , rig , cultivate
2. turn , field , luck , homeland
3. reduce , deduce , distribute , increase
4. bear , catch , flee , bend
questions.full:
On a field in England, three robots have been given a mission: to find and zap weeds with electricity before planting seeds in the cleared soil.
The robots – named Tom, Dylan and Harry – were developed by Small Robot Company to ______ land of unwanted weeds with minimal use of chemicals and heavy machinery.
Robot Tom can scan 20 hectares (49 acres) a day, collecting data which is then used by Dylan, a “crop-care” robot, to zap weeds.
Then it’s robot Harry’s ______ to plant seeds in the weed-free soil.
